goal.content: The Customer wants to place a bid on an auction item.

preconditions.content: The Customer has selected an auction item on which to place a bid.
The Customer is registered on the Website and has provided valid credit card information.
Before any auction participant may place a bid, they must agree to be bound by the Terms of Use Agreement by checking the required Terms of Use acceptance checkbox.

trigger.content: The Customer initiates placing a bid on the selected auction item by clicking the bid-entry action (for example, 'Bid Now!' or the 'Bid' button).

main_flow.content: The Customer selects a bid amount for the selected auction item.
The Customer activates the applicable bid submission control (for example, 'Place Bid', 'Place Single Bid', or 'Place SmartBid') for the selected auction item.
The system checks the bidder's sign-in status before allowing the bid to be placed.
When the Customer has the required minimum information to bid, the system returns the bidder to the product details page of the item they initially tried to bid on.

Before the bid is placed, the Customer agrees to be bound by the Terms of Use Agreement by checking the required checkbox labeled 'I accept and agree with the JTVauctions.com Terms of Use Agreement (required to participate in JTVauctions.com auctions).'

The system displays a bid confirmation pop-up telling the Customer they have just bid '$XX, using a "[type] bid"', with controls including 'Yes, Place SmartBid' and 'Cancel' (or equivalent for single bids).
The Customer confirms the bid by clicking 'Yes, Place SmartBid' or the equivalent single-bid confirmation button.
The bid is placed on the selected auction item, and the Customer remains on the product details page.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 1: Instead of selecting a standard single bid amount, the Customer may use SmartBid (proxy bidding or max bidding) by setting a maximum bid amount, and the system auto-bids on the Customer's behalf up to that limit.
Diverges from Step 3: If the Customer has not signed in before attempting to place a bid, the system takes the Customer directly to the sign-in page instead of proceeding with the bid.

exception_flow.content: Diverges from Step 1: If the Customer enters a bid amount that is not valid (e.g., below minimum increment or exceeds maximum allowed), the system displays an error message and prevents the bid from being placed.
Diverges from Step 2: If the auction's Auction Status is 'Closed', bidding is not possible.
Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer does not agree to be bound by the Terms of Use Agreement, the Customer cannot submit a bid on the Website. Exit: the bid cannot be submitted.

postconditions.content: A bid has been placed on the selected auction item.
After the bid is placed successfully, the Customer remains on the product details page of the item they initially tried to bid on.

After the bid is placed, the system displays the item in the Customer's 'My Current Bidding Activity' list with columns for Item #, Description, My Current Bid, My SmartBid, Current High Bid, Total Bids, Last Bid Time, Ending Time, and an Action column containing a 'Bid' button.

After the bid is placed, the system records the bid details in the Customer's Bid History, including Closed Date/Time, Auction Sequence, Item Number, Last Bid amount, Max Bid (SmartBid) amount if applicable, and Winning Bid status.
After the bid is placed successfully, the system updates the 'High Bid' and '# of Bids' columns in the auction history table to reflect the new bid amount and increments the bid count.

goal.content: To allow a customer to place and confirm a bid on an item.

preconditions.content: The customer has provided the minimum information needed to place bids.
The customer is not in Review status.
The auction participant has agreed to be bound by the Terms of Use Agreement.

trigger.content: The customer places a bid on a specific product.

main_flow.content: The customer places a bid from the bidding page.
Before allowing a bid to be placed, the system will check the bidder’s sign-in status.
A bid confirmation pop-up message will appear, telling the customer that they have just bid “$XX, using a “[type]” bid”.
The customer confirms their bid.
After the user confirms their bid, they will remain on the product details page.

alternative_flow.content: From the sign-in status check, if the bidder has not signed in, the system will take the bidder directly to the sign-in page before allowing a bid to be placed.
At the bid confirmation pop-up, the customer can select the Cancel button instead of the Yes, Place SmartBid button.

exception_flow.content: If the bidder has not signed in, the system will take the bidder directly to the sign-in page before allowing a bid to be placed. Exit: the bid is not placed; the bidder is directed to the sign-in page.
If the customer account is in Review status (suspended), the customer may not bid. Exit: the bid is not placed.

postconditions.content: The customer’s bid has been placed and confirmed.
After the user confirms their bid, they will remain on the product details page.

If the customer placed a SmartBid, the customer has set a maximum bid amount and the system will bid for them automatically according to the minimum bid increment until the customer wins the auction or meets their maximum bid.
The “Bid History” section includes the customer’s last bid on that auction and their SmartBid (max bid) if one was placed.

goal.content: The Customer wants to register on the Website by creating a new customer account.

preconditions.content: The Customer is an individual who is either 18 years of age or older, or between the ages of 13 and 18 and using the Website with the permission of a parent or guardian.

trigger.content: The use case is triggered when a NEW customer tries to create a new JTVauctions.com account.

main_flow.content: The Customer accesses Registration Page 1, which displays a welcome headline and fields for creating a free membership account.
The Customer enters First Name, Last Name, Email Address (entered twice), Password (8–12 characters, entered twice), and Member ID ('Handle', required).
The Customer selects a default payment method from Credit Card, PayPal, or Amazon Payments.
The Customer checks the checkbox to agree to the Terms of Use Agreement before proceeding.
The Customer clicks 'Finish Now' to proceed to Registration Page 2 to complete additional information.
On Registration Page 2, the system pre-populates fields from Page 1 (except Phone Number), and the Customer enters their Phone Number.
The Customer enters or confirms Billing and Shipping Addresses; a 'Same as Billing Address' checkbox is available to duplicate billing information to shipping.
The Customer selects a Shipping Preference (e.g., standard ground or expedited) via radio button.
The Customer selects Email Preferences via checkboxes for transactional emails and may access a link to change newsletter subscription.
The Customer clicks 'Save Changes' to complete registration.
The system completes registration and displays a pop-up instructing the Customer to add shop@jewelryTV.rsys1.com to their safe senders list and enable cookies.

The system sends an automated transactional email with a Thank You message instructing the Customer to enable cookies and add the appropriate email address(es) to their whitelist or Safe Senders list.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 1: Instead of directly accessing Registration Page 1, the Customer clicks the 'Register Now' button in the 'New to JTVauctions?' section of the Sign In page, which leads to Registration Page 1.

Diverges from Step 5: Instead of clicking 'Finish Now' to proceed to Registration Page 2, the Customer clicks the 'I Want to Sign in Now!' button (labeled as 'browse now'), which takes the Customer to the sign-in page and allows immediate browsing and bidding without completing additional registration information at that time; if the Customer was previously browsing before registering and then signs in via this 'browse now' path, the system returns them to their last product details page, or to the home page if they were on the home page.

exception_flow.content: At Step 2, if the registrant tries to create a new account using an existing email address, the system notifies the registrant that the email address is already in use and asks the registrant whether they need to reset the password.

At Step 2, in the duplicate-email exception, if the registrant indicates 'yes' to resetting the password, the system generates an email to the email address with a temporary password, and the user is advised to change it.
If the Customer does not agree to be bound by the Terms of Use Agreement, the Customer cannot access or use the Website, submit an order, or bid on the Website.

When the system's duplicate-account validation checks multiple fields (for example, first name, last name, and street address) and finds matches, the system informs the Customer that an account already exists, offers to send sign-in information to the email address on file, and prevents creation of a second account. If the Customer accepts the offer, the system generates an email to that address with a temporary password and advises the Customer to change it.

Before the new account can be successfully established, the system cross-references the Consumer Protection negative file; if there is a match, the registrant receives a message stating: 'We are sorry, we are unable to create an auction account for you at this time. If you believe this message to be in error, please contact our Customer Service team at: 800-550-8393.'

postconditions.content: The new customer account is successfully established in the system.

After successful registration completion, the system displays a personalized welcome message ('Welcome, Rick!') on the account edit page, indicating that the Customer is logged in and has access to membership account information management features.

After the Customer clicks 'Save Changes', the system updates and displays both 'My Current Billing Address' and 'My Current Shipping Address' sections with the newly entered or confirmed address data.

The system sends an automated transactional email with a Welcome and Thank You message using the customer's real name, instructing the Customer to add the appropriate email address(es) to their whitelist or Safe Senders list.

goal.content: The goal of the use case is for the customer to complete payment for won auction items using their chosen method (PayPal or Amazon Payments) within the required timeframe.

preconditions.content: The Customer has won auction items and has unpaid winnings to pay for.
The Customer has a registered account with established billing/shipping addresses and payment methods, and the account's default method of payment is either PayPal or Amazon Payments.
The Customer's account is not in Review Status and is not locked due to prior non-payment exceeding policy thresholds.

trigger.content: The Customer arrives at the 'Returning Winners Payments Page' after winning auction items.

main_flow.content: The system displays the 'PayPal / Amazon Pmts Page for Returning Winners' to the Customer.
The Customer selects the items to pay for from the list of won items by checking the 'Pay Now' checkbox next to each item.
The Customer selects a shipping speed option (USPS Standard or Expedited) via radio buttons.
The Customer selects a checkout option by clicking either the PayPal logo button or the Amazon Payments logo button.
The system launches the checkout process for the selected payment provider.
The Customer completes the selected PayPal or Amazon Payments checkout process within the required timeframe.
Upon completion, the system returns the Customer to a Thank You page that uses the global header and footer and includes a link to the homepage.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 4 when the Customer chooses the 'Checkout Later' option: payment is deferred, allowing the Customer to return and pay anytime within 7 days (168 hours) after winning the auction.
Diverges from Step 5 when PayPal is selected: the Customer is immediately taken to the PayPal checkout process on a PayPal-hosted page.
Diverges from Step 5 when Amazon Payments is selected: the Amazon Payments checkout widget loads on the page without leaving the site, graying out the background and disabling other links.

exception_flow.content: At main-flow Step 6 (including when payment was deferred via the 'Checkout Later' alternative), if the Customer does not complete payment for the PayPal or Amazon Payments order within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending/winning, the system automatically cancels the order and places the item into 'Hold' status. Exit: order cancelled.

At main-flow Step 6, when the PayPal or Amazon Payments order expires because payment was not received within 168 hours, the system automatically locks the Customer's account and places it into 'Review Status', preventing the Customer from bidding again until a Customer Service representative unlocks it; the Customer cannot unlock the account by paying for the cancelled order. Exit: account locked/Review Status until Customer Service unlock.

At main-flow Step 4, if the Customer has failed to pay for auction winnings more than three times in a twelve-month period (unless less than 10% of total winnings), the Customer becomes subject to an escalation policy that restricts payment methods to credit cards only, so the PayPal or Amazon Payments checkout option is not available. Exit: PayPal/Amazon payment path unavailable due to credit-card-only restriction.

postconditions.content: The Customer has completed payment for the selected won auction items using the chosen PayPal or Amazon Payments method within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time.
The order is not cancelled and does not enter a 'hold' status.
The item's Payment Status is updated to 'Paid' in the My Bid History table.
The Customer is returned to a Thank You page that uses the global header and footer and includes a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.
The system sends a confirmation email stating that another email will be sent shortly confirming the order and shipping information.

goal.content: To complete checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing a checkout option and completing the transaction(s).

preconditions.content: The customer has won an auction.
The customer has unpaid auction winnings.
The customer’s registration data includes a default Method of Payment (MOP) of PayPal or Amazon Payments.
The customer has been identified via a cookie, the “pay now” link in the winner notification email from Responsys, or because they signed in.

trigger.content: The customer chooses a checkout option to complete their transaction(s) for won items.

main_flow.content: The post-auction checkout page displays a congratulatory message: Congratulations! You've won XX items for a total of $XXX.XX. We've included a list of these items below.

The page states: You are seeing this message because you have chosen either PayPal or Amazon Payments as your default method of payment. Please complete your transaction(s) now by choosing a checkout option.
The final section is the Checkout Options section, which consists of three logo buttons, with a radio button next to each.
The user chooses a checkout option.

The selected checkout process is presented: clicking on the PayPal logo or radio button immediately takes the user to the PayPal checkout process, and the next page the user sees is a PayPal-hosted page; clicking on the Amazon Payments logo or radio button immediately loads the Amazon Payments checkout widget on the page, without leaving the page, while the page remains in the background, grayed out, and all other links are disabled, and the rest of the process is per the Amazon integration guidelines documentation.
The user completes the transaction(s) through the selected checkout process.

alternative_flow.content: 1. Clicking on the PayPal logo or radio button immediately takes the user to the PayPal checkout process; the next page the user sees is a PayPal-hosted page.

2. Clicking on the Amazon Payments logo or radio button immediately loads the Amazon Payments checkout widget on the page, without leaving the page; the page remains in the background, but grayed out, and all other links are disabled; the rest of the process is per the Amazon integration guidelines documentation.
3. Clicking on the “Checkout Later” button or radio button immediately grays out the page and disables all links; a DIV layer appears.

4. Orders won with an alternative payment method, i.e. PayPal or Amazon Payments, will be placed in a Hold status until payment is received; when an auction is won, the customer will be sent an email, requiring payment; if payment is not received within 168 hours, the item order will be cancelled.

exception_flow.content: 1. If the customer selects “Checkout Later” instead of completing checkout, the page grays out and disables all links and a DIV layer appears; the DIV states that the customer can come back to pay anytime within 7 days (exactly 168 hours) after winning auction(s), that unpaid orders will be cancelled after the payment window expires, and that bidding incurs an obligation to pay when they win per the Terms of Use Agreement. Exit: the customer selects “Return to Payments” to close the DIV and re-enable page links, or selects “JTVauctions Homepage” to go to the home page.
2. If the customer does not pay within the payment window, any unpaid orders will be cancelled after the payment window expires. Exit: the unpaid order is cancelled.

postconditions.content: The Amazon or PayPal checkout process has been completed.
The user is returned to a Thank You page.
Payment is received for the order(s) won with an alternative payment method, i.e. PayPal or Amazon Payments.
Payment is made within seven days (168 hours) of the auction’s closing date/time.

use_case_name: Monitor Current and Past Auction Status

goal.content: The Customer wants to monitor the status of their current and past auctions.

preconditions.content: The Customer is logged in to the system with a registered account.

trigger.content: The use case is triggered when the Customer accesses the 'My Current Bids' page via a vanity URL (www.jtvauctions.com/mybids) or by clicking the 'My Current Bids' link in the global site header.

main_flow.content: The Customer accesses the 'My Current Bids' page to view a list of items they are currently bidding on.
The system displays the current bid data sorted by ending time, with the soonest ending auction at the top.
If the Customer's current bid is less than the Current High Bid, the system highlights the dollar amount in the 'My Current Bid' column in bold red.
The Customer accesses the 'My Bid History' page.
The system displays the 'My Bid History' page with 'Items I've Won' and 'Items I Bid On, But Did Not Win' sections.
The system sorts the auction lists by ending time, with the most recent items appearing at the top.

For won items, the system displays a Payment Status column showing 'Paid' if the default payment type is a credit card, or 'Not Paid' in bold red if the default is PayPal or Amazon Payments and the Customer has not yet paid.

The Customer navigates to the 'Recently Ended Auctions' page, and the system displays a table of recently ended auctions with Item #, Description, Auction Number, Winning Amount, Winner, and Ending Time, sorted by ending time with the soonest ending auction at the top.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from main flow step 1: Instead of accessing the 'My Current Bids' page through the global site header, the Customer may access it directly via the vanity URL www.jtvauctions.com/mybids to monitor current auction status.

Diverges from main flow step 1: Instead of first accessing 'My Current Bids', the Customer may access the 'My Watch List' page via the 'My Watch List' link in the global site header or the vanity URL www.jtvauctions.com/mywatchlist. The page displays a table sorted by ending time with columns for Item #, Description, Auction Number, Current High Bid, Total Bids, Last Bid Time, Ending Time, and an Action column containing a 'Bid' button.
Diverges from main flow step 1: Instead of first accessing 'My Current Bids', the Customer may navigate directly to the 'My Bid History' page to monitor past auction status.

Diverges from main flow step 4: Instead of accessing 'My Bid History', the Customer may follow the 'Recently Ended Auctions' link from the 'My Current Bids' page (or other pages) to view past auction status. This page displays a table sorted by ending time showing Item #, Description, Auction Number, Winning Amount, Winner, and Ending Time, and shows 24 hours worth of history.

Diverges from main flow step 4: Instead of manually navigating to 'My Bid History', the Customer may click the 'Click Here Now' link in the 'Winner Alert! You're a Winner!' banner in the global header to view won items.

exception_flow.content: If the Customer has won an item and their default payment type is PayPal or Amazon Payments but they have not yet paid, the system displays the Payment Status as 'Not Paid' in bold red; the 'Not Paid' status serves as a link to the 'Returning Winner's Payments' page, providing the recovery path/hand-off that directs the Customer to resolve the unpaid status.

When monitoring past auction status via 'My Bid History', the system displays distinct 'Items I've Won' and 'Items I Bid On, But Did Not Win' sections, sorted by ending time with the most recent on top, and includes payment status indicators for won items.

When monitoring past auction status via the 'Recently Ended Auctions' page, the system displays a table with columns for Item #, Description, Auction Number, Winning Amount, Winner, and Ending Time, sorted by ending time with the soonest ending auction at the top.

use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

goal.content: To transmit Air and Surface surveillance tracks after achieving Active status and performing sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration.

preconditions.content: C2 JU has achieved Active status, either initially or by returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
Sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation of local sensor data, and data registration have been performed before transmitting tracks.

trigger.content: The C² JU assumes R² of an IU when one of the following occurs: a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds; a J2 PPLI message other than J2.0 is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence; a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU; or the Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.

main_flow.content: C2 JU determines the type of surveillance message from the Environment/Category of the IU being reported.
C2 JU determines the IFF/SIF code status for the track as Valid Data or No Data according to the specified criteria.
C2 JU reports all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for the track in accordance with the J3 message transmit rules, reporting No Data as zeroes when no valid code is currently held.
C2 JU reports the Identity as Friend.
C2 JU reports the Track Number, Platform, and Platform Activity values received in previous PPLI messages.
C2 JU waits the minimum 12 seconds before reporting the Air or Surface track.
C2 JU, having assumed R² for the IU, reports the Air or Surface surveillance track via the interface as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 5 when the Environment/Category changes from SPACE TRK to AIR TRK or SURF TRK: C2 JU retains the original Track Number and reports the entity in the appropriate J3.x surveillance message; if the change is proposed by J7.0 (ACT = 1), the R² JU must manually accept or reject it, and data does not change until after acceptance.
Diverges from Step 2 upon receipt of a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message: C2 JU automatically sets the designated mode(s) for the specified track to the No Data status.
Diverges from Step 3 when the clearing function (J7.5 (ACT = 0)) changes a Valid Data value to No Data status: C2 JU does not transmit a change report for that transition.

Diverges from Step 3 when a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message results in no IFF/SIF data being held: C2 JU does not continue transmitting the periodic J3 message that includes the continuation word containing IFF/SIF data.
Diverges from Step 2 when the R² unit reports a No Data status (value 0) for one or more modes in a required IFF/SIF Surveillance data report: C2 JU data updating occurs spontaneously.

exception_flow.content: When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert, the operator has the following manual actions available for attempting resolution of the difference: (1) update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; (2) initiate J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message (any mode); (3) initiate J7.5 (ACT = 1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message (any mode); (4) change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; (5) decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing the assignment of a new track number to local data; (6) clear operator alert (any mode).

If a correlation is not found for a received J2 PPLI report, the C² JU integrates it into its surveillance database; if no subsequent J2 messages are received and the C² JU still has no local data, the C² JU assumes no responsibility for reporting the subject JU on the Surveillance Network PG.

postconditions.content: The Air and Surface surveillance track has been successfully reported as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG, with the JU with R² reporting the most current IFF/SIF surveillance data available in the interface for Air and Surface tracks.
The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator for the reported track or point are reported as value 1.
Upon the C2 JU assuming R² of the IU, the identity of the reported track is set to Friend.
The IFF/SIF data status in the J3 continuation word is reported with a nonzero code in the applicable Mode Code field for Valid Data, or with zeroes for No Data.

use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

goal.content: To originate and report real-time air and surface (maritime) tracks using the J3.2 and J3.3 surveillance messages.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU has an automatic correlation capability for air and surface tracks.
The C2 JU has an automatic decorrelation capability for real-time air or surface tracks it initiates.
The C2 JU has the capability to perform common tracking in accordance with the correlation and decorrelation procedures and criteria.
Sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration have been performed.
After initially achieving Active status or returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, the minimum wait of 12 seconds before reporting air and surface tracks has elapsed.

trigger.content: A C2 JU initiates a real-time air or surface track.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU, having the capability to originate and report real-time air or surface tracks, performs common tracking in accordance with the correlation and decorrelation procedures and criteria.

In common tracking, the C2 JU shares a common track number and shifting R^2 between C2 JUs; each air, surface (maritime), land (ground), and space tracked object is normally reported by one C2 JU while other C2 JUs withhold their reports to prevent cluttering the tactical plot.
The C2 JU commences the correlation process by comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with data received on the interface to prevent or eliminate dual designations.
The C2 JU periodically compares remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
When the C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action, either automatically or manually.
The C2 JU reports Air surveillance data using the J3.2 (PTI = 1) message and Surface (Maritime) surveillance data using the J3.3 (PTI = 1) message.
For Air surveillance reporting, the C2 JU includes Altitude and Altitude Source when available.

The C2 JU reports the velocity of Air and Surface (Maritime) tracks as course and speed, with speed reported in data miles per hour of ground speed and course reported in degrees with respect to true north.
The C2 JU exchanges track identity as defined in paragraph 4.4.2.1.

alternative_flow.content: At main flow step 0, the C2 JU may also perform manual decorrelation, and may have a capability to require manual confirmation of automatic decorrelations.

At main flow step 4, if a correlation request is rejected, the C2 JU transmits the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection. When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.

At main flow step 5, if the C2 JU does not have R^2, it is responsible for monitoring IFF/SIF surveillance data and only reporting if it holds different data with the J7.5 message; the JU with R^2 reports all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for that track in accordance with the transmit rules for the J3 messages.

At main flow step 5, if the C2 JU ceases reporting a track for which it currently has R^2, it transmits the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, except when it ceases reporting because it has relinquished R^2 to another JU or when that track becomes an Active IU on the network with the same TN.

exception_flow.content: If a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection. Exit: the rejection is reported via J7.2.

After initially achieving Active status, or after returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, C2 JUs capable of assuming R^2 for air, surface, or land tracks shall not transmit air, surface, or land tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed; the minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds. Exit: transmission is withheld until those checks and the minimum wait are complete.

For IFF/SIF surveillance data reporting, all JUs without R^2 are responsible for monitoring such data and only reporting if they hold different data with the J7.5 message. Exit: if different data are held, report them with J7.5; otherwise continue monitoring and do not report.

postconditions.content: Air surveillance data is reported using the J3.2 (PTI = 1) message.
Surface (Maritime) surveillance data is reported using the J3.3 (PTI = 1) message.
Air surveillance reporting includes Altitude and Altitude Source when available.

The velocity of Air and Surface (Maritime) tracks is reported as course and speed, with speed reported in data miles per hour of ground speed and course reported in degrees with respect to true north.
Track identity is exchanged as defined in paragraph 4.4.2.1.

goal.content: To transmit air, surface, or land tracks after achieving Active status and performing sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration.

use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

goal.content: To transmit and receive all the response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks, which are held locally by their system.

preconditions.content: The C² JU must be capable of reporting air or surface tracks.
The C² JU must have the capability to transmit and receive all the response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks, which are held locally by their system.
The C² JU must have an automatic correlation capability if it originates real-time air or surface tracks.
The C² JU must have locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) for comparison with received interface data to prevent or eliminate dual designations.

trigger.content: A system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and receives no further updates on the remote track.

main_flow.content: The C² JU compares locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with data received on the interface to prevent or eliminate dual designations.
If a track for which positional data has been locally derived by a C² JU is currently being reported by another C² JU, it is referred to as a 'common local track'.
All C² JUs perform correlation and decorrelation of their local track data with respect to the remote data they are receiving to ensure common tracking functions properly.
The C² JU reports the position of a real-time track extrapolated to the time of transmission.
Nonreal-time data is identified as such and time tags are provided; nonreal-time track positions are not extrapolated.
The source of track data is provided via Source TN in the transmitted message.
Track reporting ensures that information on the track is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible.
Data are correlated and dual designation is minimized during track reporting.
Proper rules for reporting a track are followed according to system configuration and operational requirements.

alternative_flow.content: If the Dropped TN Mode IV data is a higher value than the Retained TN Mode IV data, it shall be transferred to the Retained TN.
If the Dropped TN had the Force Tell Indicator set to value 1, the Retained TN shall have the Force Tell Indicator set to value 1.
If the Dropped TN had the Emergency Indicator set to value 1, the Retained TN shall have the Emergency Indicator set to value 1.

Common local tracks shall be decorrelated if, on receipt of 2(1-5, 1) consecutive remote track reports, the remote track falls outside a distance of 1.5(1.0-2.0, 0.1) times the maximum correlation distance calculated in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f(3).
The local track shall be automatically tested once for correlation against remote tracks (not common local tracks) in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and g.
If the automatic correlation test fails, assign a new TN (TN B) to the local track and report TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.

When a C² JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.

The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
When the RV field is set to value 0 it indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable, and when the RV field is set to value 1 it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.

exception_flow.content: If the C² JU recognizes that two tracks are eligible for correlation and initiates a J7.2 Correlation message, receiving IUs may reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request if certain prespecified conditions exist.
When the RV field in the J7.2 message is set to value 1, it indicates that a reverse correlation request would be rejected by the originating JU.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.

If the RV field is set to value 3 (indicating manually initiated correlation), the correlation shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection — implying an exception path exists even for manual correlations under specific constraints.

After initially achieving Active status, or after returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, C² JUs capable of assuming R² for air, surface, or land tracks shall not transmit those tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed — failure to complete these steps constitutes an exception preventing track publication.

The minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds; for land tracks it is 60 seconds. If operational necessity requires shorter wait times or none at all, system design must allow override — otherwise, premature transmission without meeting timing constraints constitutes an exception condition.

postconditions.content: All C² JUs capable of reporting air or surface tracks have transmitted and received all the response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks, which are held locally by their system.

Dual designations between remote and local tracks (and optionally common local tracks) have been resolved through periodic comparison and correlation rules in accordance with section 4.4.4.3.1, Air and Surface Track Correlation.
Correlation requests initiated via J7.2 messages have been either accepted, rejected (with RV=2), or responded to with reverse correlation (RV=0 or RV=1) as per prespecified conditions.
Manually initiated correlations (indicated by RV=3) have been accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.
Tracks published include validated identity, position, velocity, strength, and source TN; nonreal-time data is identified with time tags and not extrapolated.
Minimum wait times before transmitting tracks (12 seconds for air/surface, 60 seconds for land) have been observed unless overridden by operational necessity.

use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

goal.content: The C2 JU publishes air and surface surveillance tracks to ensure the exchange of complete, accurate, and timely surveillance information for joint operations while minimizing dual designations.

trigger.content: The C2 JU initiates the publication of air and surface surveillance tracks when there is a requirement to exchange surveillance information and data usable in providing threat warning information among systems involved in joint operations.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU ensures that surveillance track information exchanged is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible, and that data are correlated to minimize dual designation.
The C2 JU follows proper reporting rules, including providing the source of track data (Source TN) and reporting the position of real-time tracks extrapolated to the time of transmission.
After initially achieving Active status or returning to it, the C2 JU waits a minimum of 12 seconds before transmitting air and surface tracks to allow for responsibility checks and correlation.

If the C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported are eligible for correlation (dual designation), it initiates action to resolve the dual designation, potentially by transmitting a J7.2 Correlation message.

alternative_flow.content: If operational necessity requires it, the C2 JU may override the minimum 12-second wait time before transmitting tracks, or eliminate the wait entirely.

When the C2 JU initiates a J7.2 Correlation message to resolve a dual designation, receiving IUs may reject the requested correlation under certain prespecified conditions, in which case a J7.2 message with Response Value (RV) set to 2 is transmitted to report the rejection.

If a correlation is found between a received PPLI report and a local track for which the C2 JU has reporting responsibility (R²), the JU transmits a J7.2 Correlation message with RV=1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), ceases reporting the surveillance track, and transmits a J7.0 Drop Track message.

If a correlation is found between a received PPLI report and a track held by another C2 JU with R², and the Track Numbers (TNs) are different, the JU transmits a J7.2 (RV=1) Correlation message identifying the PPLI TN as retained and the surveillance TN as dropped.

exception_flow.content: If receiving IUs reject a requested correlation under prespecified conditions, they transmit a J7.2 message with Response Value (RV) set to 2 to report the rejection, exiting the correlation attempt.

If a C² JU finds correlation between a received PPLI report and a local track for which it has R², it transmits J7.2 (RV=1), ceases reporting the surveillance track, and sends J7.0 Drop Track message — exiting further reporting of that track.
If a system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT=0) message and receives no further updates on a remote track, it may purge the remote track from its database as an exception handling measure.

Automatic correlation is restricted if tracks have Identity (ID) conflict, different Mode II codes (with local code current), both are locally derived real-time tracks, or either has Strength > 1 — requiring manual intervention or inhibition via operator-selectable capability.

use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

goal.content: The goal is to resolve existing dual designations of ballistic missile tracks through track correlation when two tracks being reported to the interface are recognized as eligible for correlation.

preconditions.content: C2 JU has correlated local sensor data.
All IUs are periodically comparing remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
Tracks and IUs are present so their positions can be extrapolated to the same time for correlation comparison.

trigger.content: C2 JU recognizes that two tracks—one a local track or common local track and one a remote/interface track—are eligible for correlation.

main_flow.content: C2 JU initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation after recognizing that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
The process of correlation consists of comparing locally derived sensor data (e.g., position, velocity, boost indication) with the data received on the interface.
When the two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, they are deemed a tentative correlation.
Upon the next correlation stimulus, the same two tracks are tested again.
When the two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, they are processed for dual designation resolution.
C2 JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks, identifying the track number to be retained and the track number to be dropped.

The receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
Upon successful correlation, if the originating C2 JU holds R² data for the Dropped TN, it transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message to drop the Dropped TN.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 1: C2 JU may use a manual capability to initiate the correlation of any two tracks irrespective of the correlation test criteria, correlation restrictions, or other correlation requirements.
Diverges from Step 1: Tracks with TQ less than or equal to e are not eligible for correlation, except that new local real-time tracks can still be recognized as eligible for correlation.
Diverges from Step 2: If the speed of either track is less than 10 dmh, the course differential criterion is not applied in the correlation test.

Diverges from Step 5: An exception to the automatic correlation restrictions allows correlation if one track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile and the other has an ID of Friend, permitting the breaking of an engagement or destruction of a missile in flight.
Diverges from Step 6: The J7.2 Correlation message shall not be inhibited by any filter.

Diverges from Step 7: A receiving IU that desires to reverse the requested correlation uses the RV field to determine whether to originate a reverse correlation request; when responding with a reverse correlation, it transmits the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.

exception_flow.content: Diverges from Step 2 when the Altitude Source of either track is 0 (No Statement/Estimated) or 2 (Aircraft Report): Altitude shall not be used in the correlation test. Outcome: altitude is excluded from the correlation test.
Diverges from Step 2 when a track has TQ ≤ e: that track shall not be tested for correlation. Outcome: the correlation test is not performed for that track.

Diverges from Step 5 when automatic correlation is attempted and the local/remote data held indicates that both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks (i.e., being updated with local positional data): C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate the two tracks. Outcome: automatic correlation is not performed.

Diverges from Step 5 when conflicting IDs are the only correlation restriction, i.e., an ID difference that cannot be automatically accepted or rejected: the operator shall be alerted and the differences presented for evaluation, with options to (a) change the local ID or Exercise Indicator and ID, allowing automatic correlation; (b) transmit an ID Difference Report, allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed; (c) confirm the restriction, inhibiting the correlation; or (d) conduct voice coordination to resolve the situation. Outcome: operator action determines whether automatic correlation is allowed, inhibited, or resolved via voice coordination.

Diverges from Step 5 when a selection conflict occurs because both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN have an OCC: the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check. Outcome: the correlation is abandoned until the next correlation check.

Diverges from Step 6 after transmission of the correlation request when no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received for the Dropped TN within 60 seconds: the correlation is deemed to have failed and all associated processing shall be cancelled. Outcome: the correlation fails and associated processing is cancelled.
Diverges from Step 7 when both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN have an OCC: the correlation shall be rejected. Outcome: correlation is rejected.
Diverges from Step 7 when the two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict: the correlation shall be rejected. Outcome: correlation is rejected.
Diverges from Step 7 when one track is simulated and the other is live: the correlation shall be rejected. Outcome: correlation is rejected.

Diverges from Step 7 when a correlation request is rejected: the JU shall transmit the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection. Outcome: the rejection is reported by J7.2 with RV = 2.

Diverges from Step 7 when a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation: the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination. Outcome: the originating JU alerts the operator to conduct voice coordination.

Diverges from Step 7 when a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R^2 and the TNs are different: the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN. Outcome: a J7.2 RV = 1 message is transmitted with the specified Retained TN and Dropped TN.

Diverges from Step 7 when a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R^2 and the TNs are the same: the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track, except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded. Outcome: PPLI information is accepted and J3 surveillance data is disregarded, or when Geodetic Position Quality is 0, the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message is discarded.

Diverges from Step 7 when the own unit has R^2 for the Dropped TN: a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message shall be transmitted; if the Dropped TN is reported by another IU after this transmission, the own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track and shall not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds. Outcome: J7.0 Drop Track is transmitted, and if the Dropped TN is later reported by another IU, it is retained as a remote track with no reattempted correlation for 60 seconds.

postconditions.content: The two eligible tracks have been correlated, resolving the dual designation.
If the own unit held the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN is designated as a common local track upon successful correlation.
If the originating C2 JU holds R^2 data for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is transmitted for the Dropped TN upon successful correlation.
After acceptance of a manual correlation (RV field set to value 3), the resulting track is not subject to automatic decorrelation processing for 5 minutes.

use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

goal.content: The goal is to prevent or eliminate dual designations of ballistic missile tracks through the process of track correlation.

preconditions.content: C2 JU has correlated local sensor data.
All IUs are periodically comparing remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
Two tracks have passed the correlation tests and restrictions twice, satisfying the eligibility requirement for correlation execution.

trigger.content: C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

main_flow.content: C2 JU initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation after recognizing that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
The process of correlation consists of comparing locally derived sensor data (e.g., position, velocity, boost indication) with the data received on the interface.
When the two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, they are deemed a tentative correlation.
Upon the next correlation stimulus, the same two tracks are tested again.
When the two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, they are processed for dual designation resolution.
C2 JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks, identifying the track number to be retained and the track number to be dropped.

The receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.

Diverges from Step 3: If the speed of either track is less than 10 dmh, the course differential criterion is not applied in the correlation test.

use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

goal.content: To recognize and resolve air and surface track dual designations by having a C2 JU initiate track correlation, transmit a J7.2 Correlation message requesting other C2 IUs to perform correlation of the two tracks, and identify the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

preconditions.content: Two tracks are being reported to the interface and are eligible for correlation.
The dual designation is for air or surface tracks; the rules for land (ground) and space track dual designation resolution are TBD.
The C2 JU has the capability to perform common tracking in accordance with the correlation and decorrelation procedures and criteria.
The C2 JU has an automatic correlation capability for real-time air or surface tracks it originates.

trigger.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

main_flow.content: All IUs periodically compare remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.

All C2 JUs perform correlation and decorrelation of their local track data with respect to the remote data which they are receiving; the correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface, in order to prevent or eliminate dual designations.

When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
The recognizing JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.

The J7.2 Correlation message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped, and the originating JU indicates in the message if it has any constraint which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation.

C2 JUs shall not automatically select as the TN to be dropped a TN which has any of the OCCs listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(6 7); in the absence of such a selection constraint, JUs shall select the higher TN as the TN to be dropped.

Receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.

Two tracks shall pass the correlation tests and restrictions twice before the correlation is executed; when they pass once they are deemed a tentative correlation, are tested again upon the next correlation stimulus, and, if they pass the second correlation test with no correlation restriction, are processed for dual designation resolution in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1j and k.

alternative_flow.content: If prespecified conditions exist that require or allow rejection of the requested correlation, the receiving IU rejects the correlation and transmits the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection.

If a receiving IU desires to reverse the requested correlation, it uses the RV field to determine if a reverse correlation request should be originated or if the original correlation request should be rejected; RV value 0 indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable, and RV value 1 indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.
If the RV field is set to value 3, the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.
If the Retained TN and the Dropped TN will decorrelate when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the correlation shall be rejected.

If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 0, the reverse correlation shall be transmitted if the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint; if both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 1, the correlation shall be rejected.

If the above actions result in resolution of the ID conflict, the TN to be retained shall be tested for decorrelation in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.2a before executing the correlation, except the test shall be conducted only once.

exception_flow.content: If the dual designation involves land (ground) or space tracks, the rules for land (ground) and space track dual designation resolution are TBD; exit the exception path with no resolution procedure specified for those tracks.

If prespecified conditions require or allow a receiving IU to reject the requested correlation, the receiving IU rejects the correlation and transmits the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection; exit with the correlation request rejected.

If a receiving IU desires to reverse the requested correlation, it uses the RV field to determine whether to originate a reverse correlation request or reject the original correlation request: RV value 0 indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable, and RV value 1 indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected; exit by originating a reverse correlation request (RV=0) or by rejecting the original correlation request and transmitting the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection (RV=1).

If the RV field is set to value 3, the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection; if such a condition applies, reject the correlation and transmit the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection; exit with the correlation accepted or the rejection reported.

postconditions.content: A J7.2 Correlation message has been transmitted by the recognizing C2 JU requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
The J7.2 Correlation message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
The receiving C2 IUs have accepted the requested correlation.
The two tracks have successfully passed the correlation tests and restrictions twice with no correlation restriction, and the correlation has been executed.

The TN to be dropped was not automatically selected from a TN having any of the OCCs listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(6 7); absent such a selection constraint, the higher TN was selected as the TN to be dropped.
For the track corresponding to the dropped TN, the C2 JU has ceased reporting the track and has transmitted a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.

use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

goal.content: To resolve dual designations by correlating two tracks which are being reported to the interface and are eligible for correlation.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU must have the capability to transmit and receive all response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks held locally.
All IUs must periodically compare remote tracks to local tracks (and optionally common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.

The frequency of comparisons, criteria for determining that two tracks represent the same object, and correlation rules must be in accordance with section 4.4.4.3.1, Air and Surface Track Correlation.

trigger.content: A C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
The recognizing JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
The J7.2 message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

Receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.

exception_flow.content: If the receiving IU has prespecified conditions that require or allow it to reject the requested correlation, it may reject the correlation request.

If the receiving IU desires to reverse the requested correlation and the originating JU’s J7.2 message has RV field set to 0 (indicating reverse correlation is acceptable), the receiving IU may originate a reverse correlation request.

If the receiving IU desires to reverse the requested correlation but the originating JU’s J7.2 message has RV field set to 1 (indicating reverse correlation would be rejected), the receiving IU must not originate a reverse correlation request and may instead reject the original correlation request.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the receiving IU shall transmit a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection.

If the correlation was manually initiated (RV field set to 3 in the J7.2 message), the receiving IU shall accept the correlation unless certain conditions apply which require rejection as specified in paragraph 4.7.3.2.c.

postconditions.content: The dual designation is resolved, with one Track Number (TN) retained and the other TN dropped.
All receiving C² IUs have performed the correlation of the two tracks as requested in the J7.2 message, unless a rejection was transmitted.
If the correlation request was rejected, a J7.2 message with the Response Value (RV) field set to value 2 has been transmitted to report the rejection.
If a reverse correlation request was originated and accepted, the roles of the retained and dropped Track Numbers are reversed from the original request.

use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

goal.content: To resolve dual designations by initiating correlation actions to determine if two tracks represent the same object and identifying which track number (TN) to retain or drop.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
The system is capable of transmitting and receiving all the response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks, which are held locally by their system.
Each track is subject to one or more (not necessarily the same) of the below operational contingency constraints (OCC).
If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator shall be alerted.

trigger.content: A C² JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

main_flow.content: The recognizing C² JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
The recognizing C² JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
The J7.2 message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

Receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
If any constraint exists that would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation, the originating JU indicates this in the J7.2 message using the Response Value (RV) field.
When the RV field is set to value 0, it indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable; when set to value 1, it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.

Receiving IUs desiring to reverse the requested correlation use the RV field to determine if a reverse correlation request should be originated or if the original correlation request should be rejected.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.

exception_flow.content: If the TN is the subject of a current engagement status message (i.e., the TN is the same TN appearing in a J10.2 Engagement Status message Target TN or Reference TN field), correlation may be rejected.

If the TN is the subject of a pending J9.0 Command message originated by or addressed to own unit or a J12.0 Mission Assignment message originated by own unit for which a reply is required and has not been transmitted or received, correlation may be rejected.
If the TN is currently a controlled track (i.e., a J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message has been transmitted or received), correlation may be rejected.
If the TN is an active or inactive IU, correlation may be rejected.

JUs may apply one exception: if either subject track in the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed — but the Unknown/Hostile track shall be dropped (Track Number = TN-2).

This exception allows breaking the engagement and/or destroying missile(s) in flight and must be applied by any JU upon receipt of a J7.2 Correlation message; thus, any JU receiving a J7.2 Correlation message and also holding OCCs on both tracks or conflicting IDs on the two tracks (if the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled per paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(1)) shall reject the correlation in accordance with paragraph 4.7.3.7a(1).

If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator shall be alerted to take one of the following actions: change the local TN or Exercise Indicator and ID (thereby allowing automatic correlation), or transmit an ID Difference Report (thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed).

postconditions.content: The dual designation is resolved by correlating two tracks, with one Track Number (TN) retained and the other TN dropped.
All receiving C² IUs have accepted the requested correlation unless prespecified conditions required rejection or a reverse correlation request was originated.
If a reverse correlation was requested and acceptable (RV=0), it has been processed; if prohibited (RV=1), no reverse correlation was initiated.
If any receiving IU rejected the correlation, a J7.2 message with RV field set to value 2 was transmitted to report the rejection.
If the correlation was manually initiated (RV=3), it was accepted unless specific conditions requiring rejection applied.

use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

goal.content: The C2 JU initiates action to resolve dual designations when it recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

preconditions.content: All IUs must be capable of periodically comparing remote tracks to local tracks (and optionally common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
The C2 JU must recognize that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation before initiating resolution action.
Correlation rules applied must be in accordance with section 4.4.4.3.1 (Air and Surface Track Correlation).
Each C2 JU must have automatic correlation capability for real-time air or surface tracks to prevent or eliminate dual designations.

Operational contingency constraints (OCCs) such as engagement status, pending commands, controlled track status, or IU activity state must be evaluated for each track, as they may restrict correlation unless an exception applies.

trigger.content: The C2 JU initiates action to resolve dual designations when it recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

alternative_flow.content: Receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
When the RV field is set to value 0, it indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable; when set to value 1, it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.

If either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, and that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed as an exception to OCC restrictions.

exception_flow.content: If a selection conflict occurs due to Operational Contingency Constraints (OCCs) on both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN, the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check.

Receiving C2 JUs shall not accept the requested correlation if there is a correlation restriction as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g (e.g., engagement status, pending commands, controlled track). In this case, the correlation shall be rejected.
If the Retained TN and Dropped TN would decorrelate when subjected to decorrelation criteria, the correlation shall be rejected.
If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 1 (indicating reverse correlation is rejected), the correlation shall be rejected.
If both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.

C2 JUs receiving a manually initiated correlation (RV=3) shall reject the request if the two tracks are of a different E/C, have an existing E/C conflict, one is simulated and the other live, or both are locally derived real-time tracks.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the receiving JU shall transmit a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection.

If the originating C2 JU holds R-squared for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message; if the JU does not hold the Dropped TN, it shall take no further action.

postconditions.content: The recognizing C² JU transmits a J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform correlation of the two tracks, identifying the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

goal.content: To adhere to Correlation Restrictions that inhibit automatic correlation when Identity conflicts or different Mode II codes exist.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU has received remote IFF/SIF data (e.g., Mode I, II, III, or IV) and possesses own-unit data in one of the documented states ('NO DATA', 'VALID NON-CURRENT DATA', or 'VALID CURRENT DATA') sufficient to initiate identity-conflict/difference-resolution processing.

Before the use case begins, an automatic-correlation-inhibiting identity condition exists for two tracks: either (a) the local/remote data held indicates an Identity (ID) difference that constitutes a conflict, or (b) the two tracks have different Mode II codes with the local Mode II code current; in either case, the applicable correlation restriction is not inhibited by parameter.

trigger.content: During correlation processing, the C2 JU detects that two tracks have an Identity difference that constitutes a conflict or have different Mode II codes with the local Mode II code current.

main_flow.content: C2 JU identifies the applicable correlation-inhibiting condition for the tracks: an Identity conflict or different Mode II codes with the local Mode II code current.
C2 JU determines that the automatic correlation restriction has not been inhibited by a system initialization parameter and operator-selectable capability.
C2 JU adheres to the applicable Correlation Restriction and does not automatically correlate the two tracks.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from main flow Step 3 when conflicting IDs are the only correlation restriction: the operator shall be alerted to take one of the following actions: (a) Change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation; (b) Transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed; (c) Confirm the restriction, thereby inhibiting the correlation; or (d) Conduct voice coordination to resolve the situation.

exception_flow.content: If the R² JU identifies that an ID conflict exists, the operator shall be alerted and the local ID data shall continue to be reported in the appropriate surveillance message, with the Identity Difference Indicator set to value 1; the conflict will be resolved by manual means.

If the Identity Difference Indicator is set to value 1 for a non-R² unit, the unit may either: (a) follow the actions in Table 4.7-2 while inhibiting transmission of the J7.0 (ACT = 1) message until a surveillance message is received with the Identity Difference Indicator reset to value 0; or (b) take no action with respect to the reported ID, with an operator alert provided as a system option.

When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert, the operator has the following manual actions available for attempting resolution of the difference: (1) update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; (2) initiate a J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message (any mode); (3) initiate a J7.5 (ACT = 1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message (any mode); (4) change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; (5) decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing assignment of a new track number to the local data; and (6) clear the operator alert (any mode).

If any of the manual resolution actions result in resolution of the ID conflict, the track number to be retained shall be tested for decorrelation in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.2a before executing the correlation, except that the test shall be conducted only once.

When erroneous codes are detected and there are no other valid codes available or changes are inhibited (as in Mode II code reporting), the system shall have a capability to delete or clear the erroneous codes so that the interface can return to a No Data status for the specified track and its corresponding mode(s).

When the Identity Difference Indicator is set to value 1, if the R² JU is directed to automatically reject the remote ID, the system shall discard the message and the track shall continue to be reported with local data.

When erroneous codes are detected and there are no other valid codes available or changes are inhibited (as in Mode II code reporting), the system shall have a capability to delete or clear the erroneous codes so that the interface can return to a No Data status for the specified track and its corresponding mode(s).

When the Identity Difference Indicator is set to value 1, if the R² JU is directed to automatically reject the remote ID, the system shall discard the message and the track shall continue to be reported with local data.
