goal.content: Ensure accurate and timely classification of tracks to support friendly force awareness and threat response

preconditions.content: The C2 JU has received a track report (e.g., J2 PPLI message) that requires identity classification.
The track is not yet classified under one of the standard identity definitions: Pending, Unknown, Assumed Friend, Friend, Neutral, Suspect, or Hostile.
If the track is an exercise track, the Exercise Indicator in the J3 track messages must be set to distinguish it from live tracks.
Correlation restrictions do not apply if manual correlation is performed or if no conflicting conditions exist per paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f.
For inactive or limited status interface units, reporting rules for real-time tracks must be followed if local sensor data is correlated.

trigger.content: Receipt of a J2 PPLI message, detection of decorrelation criteria being met, or receipt of a Drop Track message (J7.0) for an Interface Unit.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU assigns a standard identity to the track based on its characteristics, behavior, origin, or nationality using one of the following definitions: Pending (not yet subjected to identification), Unknown (evaluated but not identified), Assumed Friend (assumed friendly due to characteristics/behavior/origin), Friend (belonging to a declared friendly nation), Neutral (neither supporting nor opposing friendly forces), Suspect (potentially hostile), or Hostile (declared belonging to an opposing entity).

If the track is involved in an exercise and is a live track, the C2 JU sets the Exercise Indicator in the J3 track messages to distinguish it from other live tracks; only tracks with standard identity of Friend can be modified by the exercise identity.

The C2 JU may further amplify the track’s identity using Special Interest Indicator, Exercise Indicator, Identity Amplifying Descriptor, Specific Type, Platform, Platform Activity, and Identity Confidence fields as defined in paragraph 4.4.2.1.

For retransmission purposes, if the C2 JU assumes R² for a previously-reported track, it shall accept all defined field values for retransmission and operator appreciation regardless of actual values implemented by the originating C² JU.

If the C2 JU holds locally derived data that differs from the value accepted for retransmission (and is not No Statement), it shall report the locally derived data instead — except for non-NS data in Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type fields received from the controlling unit, which must be retransmitted regardless of locally derived data.
If the Special Interest Indicator is set to value 1, the C2 JU shall retransmit it as value 1 when assuming R².

Surveillance data reporting is initiated by the JU which first detects or initiates a track/point and makes it available for reporting on the interface; each track/point shall be assigned a TN from the JU’s allocated block at that time, and the JU shall have R² for the track/point.

alternative_flow.content: The C2 JU may elect to accept, automatically, changes in Environment/Category, Identity or Exercise Indicator received in a track report with the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1, provided the new identity is Friend and the locally held identity is not Hostile.

When accepting a remote ID change, the C2 JU shall also retain the received values of the Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator fields for retransmission and operator appreciation, except when controlling units apply specific rules (paragraphs 4.7.1.2b and c).

If a Platform, Platform Activity or Specific Type value of 0 (No Statement) is received and a non-zero value is held locally, the C2 JU retains the local value as an exception to difference resolution rules.
If an Air Platform value of 6 (Tanker), 7 (Tanker Boom Only), or 8 (Tanker Drogue Only) is held locally and a different value is received, an operator alert is optional.
Differences in Environment/Category, ID, Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, Exercise Indicator and Special Interest Indicator field values may be resolved using the J7.0 (ACT = 2) message.

If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.

If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track, except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
Subsurface tracks shall not be correlated with IUs.

Simulated tracks will not be correlated with live tracks; prior coordination with all interface participants is required when transmitting simulated tracks to ensure they are not assigned TNs from other systems' TN blocks.

exception_flow.content: Automatic correlation shall be inhibited if the two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict, unless systems have an initialization parameter and operator selectable capability to inhibit this automatic restriction.

Automatic correlation shall be inhibited if the two tracks have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current, unless systems have an initialization parameter and operator selectable capability to inhibit this automatic restriction.
Automatic correlation shall be inhibited if both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data.

Automatic correlation shall be inhibited if either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1; however, systems shall not inhibit correlation if either track has Strength set to No Statement.

postconditions.content: The track is assigned a standard identity classification (Pending, Unknown, Assumed Friend, Friend, Neutral, Suspect, or Hostile) based on its characteristics, behavior, origin, or nationality.

If the track is an exercise track, the Exercise Indicator in the J3 track messages is set to distinguish it from other live tracks; only tracks with standard identity of Friend can be modified by the exercise identity.

The track’s identity may be further amplified using Special Interest Indicator, Exercise Indicator, Identity Amplifying Descriptor, Specific Type, Platform, Platform Activity, and Identity Confidence fields.
If correlation is not found, the C² JU integrates the received J2 PPLI report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.

If decorrelation criteria are met, the PPLI and local track data are decorrelated, and the C² JU initiates a new surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number; the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IPF/SIF Indicator field are both reported as No Statement.

For inactive or limited status interface units, if reporting rules for real-time tracks apply, the C² JU assumes R² of the IU and reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG, with identity reported as Friend, and retains previously received PPLI values for Track Number, Platform, and Platform Activity.
Automatic correlation is restricted if conflicting conditions exist per paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f, unless operator-selectable capabilities are configured to inhibit such restrictions.

goal.content: To terminate and purge the C2 JU's surveillance tracks, including Air, Surface/Maritime, Land/Ground, subsurface, and ballistic missile tracks.

preconditions.content: A surveillance track exists for the C2 JU as either a local track or a common local track, or, for automatic purge, a remote track/point exists.
Before a J7.0 (ACT = 0) termination message is transmitted for a track, the C2 JU currently has R² for that specific track.

For automatic purging of a remote track/point, the specified time interval since its last report has elapsed, no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message has been received for it, and no further updates have been received on it.

trigger.content: The use case is triggered when the C2 JU ceases reporting a surveillance track, deactivates relevant NOTACK areas, Moving Havens, or FWDAs for a subsurface track, or when the specified time interval since a remote track/point's last report has elapsed without further updates and without a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU identifies a surveillance track to terminate and purge, selecting from a supported track category such as Air, Surface/Maritime, Land/Ground, or subsurface.
The C2 JU ceases reporting the selected track while it currently has R² for that track.
The system transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message for the selected track.
The system terminates and purges the selected surveillance track.

Each system automatically purges remote tracks (DRT = 0-3) after a system-selected time interval if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received and no further updates are received on the remote track; a JU may have the capability to purge remote tracks/points by automatically dropping a remote track/point after a specified time interval has elapsed since the track's/point's last report. The JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a purged remote track/point; for NOTACK areas, Moving Havens, and FWDAs, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted at the time of deactivation.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 2: for a subsurface track, termination and purge can be triggered when the C2 JU deactivates relevant NOTACK areas, Moving Havens, or FWDAs, rather than the JU ceasing to report the track.

Diverges from Step 3: when a remote track/point (DRT = 0-3) receives no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and no further updates, the system automatically purges it after the specified time interval since its last report, without transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

goal.content: To terminate and purge surveillance tracks, including dropping remote tracks via J7.0 messages or automatically purging them after a specified time interval when no longer updated.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU has the capability to automatically initiate tracks for release to the interface without operator action.
The C2 JU has the capability to deactivate the automatic track initiation capability.

If the C2 JU is returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration have been performed.

trigger.content: The C2 JU needs to terminate a track by sending a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, or automatically purges remote tracks after a specified time interval has elapsed since the track's last report.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU terminates a track by sending a J7.0 message with the Track Management Action field set to value 0 (Drop Track Report).
For locally held remote tracks, NonC² JUs process the J7.0 Drop Track Report message.
Alternatively, the C2 JU may automatically purge locally held remote tracks after a specified time interval when these tracks are no longer being updated.
If purging is due to irregular reporting of nonreal-time tracks, the system does not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

exception_flow.content: If a C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 2) message, the JU shall reject any received data on that track that differ for a 30-second lock-out period, except for ID data from the controlling unit of the track and for processing an Exercise Status Order.

Receiving JUs which do not implement the changed Environment/Category and have R² on the track must cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.
If it is desired to change the simulation status of a track due to operator error, the track shall be dropped using the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, and a new track shall be reported.

goal.content: Ensure track data integrity and network consistency by terminating local reporting of surveillance tracks and purging remote tracks when no further updates are received.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU is currently reporting a surveillance track (air, surface, land, subsurface, or ballistic missile) on the interface.
The C2 JU has detected that it will cease reporting the track — either because it has relinquished R² to another JU, or due to operator action, system design, or time-based purge criteria.
For remote tracks being purged, the system has not received a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and no further updates are expected within a system-defined time interval.
The track is not an active IU on the network with the same TN as previously used for reference (except in KUMPAK areas, moving havens, and EWGAs where J7.0 must be transmitted at deactivation).
If terminating electronic warfare surveillance data, the information is no longer valid or time-related update requirements are not met.

trigger.content: The C2 JU ceases reporting a track for which it currently has R², or detects that no further updates are expected on a remote track within a system-defined time interval.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message to terminate reporting of a track for which it currently has R², except when the track becomes an active IU on the network with the same TN as previously used for reference.

If terminating electronic warfare surveillance data, the C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message when the information is no longer valid or time-related update requirements are not met; this message shall not be transmitted on remote reports.
For subsurface tracks in NOTACK areas, moving havens, and EWGAs, the C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT=0) message at time of deactivation even if the track becomes an active IU with the same TN.
When a system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and receives no further updates on a remote track, it automatically purges those tracks after a system-selected time interval.

Under conditions where irregular reporting of subsurface surveillance tracks occurs and no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received, the system shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message but may still purge tracks based on system criteria.

alternative_flow.content: If a JU ceases reporting a track because it has relinquished R² to another JU, the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is not transmitted.

If the track becomes an Active IU on the network with the same TN, the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is not transmitted — except in NOTACK areas, moving havens, and EWGAs where it shall be transmitted at deactivation.
For subsurface tracks, differences in position, velocity, or depth recognized by a JU are not resolved through automated conflict processing and shall not generate a J7.0 (ACT = 1 or 2) message.

Under irregular reporting conditions for subsurface surveillance tracks, if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received, the system shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message but may still purge tracks based on system criteria; DATUMS (DRT = 4) shall not be purged automatically.
Subsurface tracks shall not be correlated with IUs.

goal.content: A JU wants to transfer reporting responsibility for a specific point, line, or area from one JU to another JU.

preconditions.content: Reporting responsibility for the specific point, line, or area is currently held by an active originator JU that reports the entity.

main_flow.content: C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track Report message indicating that the JU with R² specified in the Source TN field has dropped or ceased reporting the track specified in the Reference TN field.
The receiving JU processes the J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track Report message for the locally held remote track.
Immediately prior to assuming R² for the air or surface track after receipt of the Drop Track message, the receiving JU tests the track for correlation once.
The receiving JU assumes R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
The latest JU to report the point has R² for that point.

For a line or area entity, when the JU with R² ceases reporting it, the JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message for each Reference TN (a segmented line or multisided area defined by more than one Reference TN requires a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message for each Reference TN); a receiving JU that does not purge the point, line, or area assumes R² for the entity so that it remains active on the interface.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 1: if a J3.4 message containing the Track Number is not received for two consecutive periodic updates, another JU may assume reporting responsibility for the contact instead of transfer being initiated by a J7.0 Drop Track message.

Diverges from Step 1: a JU receiving a J2 PPLI message from a JU that has R² may assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit if local reporting eligibility remains and no remote report has been received; this includes when the PPLI NPS Indicator is Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure.

Diverges from Step 1: a C² JU with correlated local sensor data assumes R² of an IU when a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, when the NPS Indicator is set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or when Geodetic Position Quality is set to value 0, rather than only upon a J7.0 Drop Track message.

Diverges from Step 1: for a previously reported emergency point, any JU with additional or more current information on the point may report on it through operator action only, providing an alternative to transfer initiation by a J7.0 Drop Track message.

Diverges from Step 4: for an emergency point, if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received, the unit with R² is declared inactive, or no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may assume R² for the point by operator action only.

Diverges from Step 1: a JU with R² for a non-real-time ballistic missile track relinquishes R² upon receiving a remote real-time track report for that track, instead of using a J7.0 Drop Track message to initiate transfer.

Diverges from Step 1: after applying all other rules, a JU relinquishes R² for a real-time track upon receiving a remote track report with TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose Source TN is greater than the local Source TN, instead of using a J7.0 Drop Track message to initiate transfer.

exception_flow.content: After the C2 JU transmits the J7.0 Drop Track Report message, if the Dropped TN is reported by another IU, own unit retains the Dropped TN as a remote track and does not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds after transmission of the J7.0.

If the correlation test at Step 3 finds a correlation with a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the Track Numbers (TNs) are different, the receiving JU transmits a J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message, retains the Source TN from the PPLI message as the Retained TN, and designates the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN; the Retained TN is the surviving track identity and the Dropped TN is handled as dropped, and if the Dropped TN is later reported by another IU after transmission of the J7.0, own unit retains it as a remote track and does not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for 60 seconds after transmission of the J7.0.

If the correlation test at Step 3 finds a correlation with a track for which another C2 JU has R², the TNs are the same, and the Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, the receiving JU accepts the surveillance track and discards the PPLI message.

If no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received for the dropped TN after a period of 60 seconds from transmission of the correlation request, the correlation is deemed to have failed and all associated processing for the correlation is cancelled.

If a C² JU finds a correlation between received PPLI reports and local sensor data for a track where the C² JU has R², it transmits a J7.2 Correlation message with Response Value (RV) set to 1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), retains the Source TN from the PPLI message, drops the surveillance TN, ceases reporting the track, and transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message.
C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local or remote data held indicates an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict.
For a ballistic missile launch point, if no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another IU may assume R² for the point by operator action only.

postconditions.content: The JU assuming R² has and retains the reporting responsibility until it is relinquished in accordance with the rules or until the track is dropped.
For a point, the latest JU to report the point has R² for that point.
For a relinquishment to another JU, the originating JU ceases reporting the transferred entity without transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message.
For an emergency point, the JU assuming R² uses the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.

For a ballistic missile track, the JU assuming R² for the track need not assume R² for the associated launch point; the unit no longer holding R² on the ballistic missile track may continue to report the launch point.

goal.content: To transfer reporting responsibility (R^2) for a track by having a C2 JU relinquish or assume R^2 in accordance with the applicable R^2 rules.

preconditions.content: For air, surface, or land tracks, the C2 JU is capable of assuming R^2 for the track.
For air, surface, or land tracks, the C2 JU has initially achieved Active status or has returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
For air, surface, or land tracks, sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed before transmitting the tracks.
For air and surface tracks, the minimum wait before transmitting tracks is 12 seconds; for land tracks, the minimum wait before transmitting tracks is 48 seconds.

trigger.content: The use case is initiated when a C2 JU receives a remote track report in which remote TQ is greater than the local TQ, or receives a remote track report for the track which contains a TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose STN is greater than the local STN, for a real-time Air, Surface (Maritime) or Land (Ground) track.

main_flow.content: C2 JU receives a remote track report for a real-time track.
C2 JU receives a remote track report with TQ greater than the local TQ for a real-time track.
Upon reception of a remote track report with TQ greater than the local TQ, the C2 JU relinquishes R^2 for the real-time track.

After applying all the applicable rules, upon reception of a remote track report with TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose Source TN is greater than the local Source TN, the C2 JU relinquishes R^2 for the real-time track.
A C2 JU with R^2 retains the responsibility until it is relinquished in accordance with the rules or until the track is dropped.

Common tracking shares a common track number and shifts R^2 between C2 JUs; each air, surface (maritime), land (ground), and space tracked object is normally reported by one C2 JU while other C2 JUs withhold their reports.

For air, surface, or land tracks, C2 JUs capable of assuming R^2 shall not transmit tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed; the minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds and for land tracks is 48 seconds.

alternative_flow.content: For Subsurface tracks, it is often desirable that more than one JU report the same Subsurface contact using different TNs; the first JU to report a contact assumes reporting responsibility for that Track Number, and no other JU shall report the contact using that track number unless one of the specified conditions occurs, including receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message containing the TN.

If a locally derived ballistic missile track is uncorrelated with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG, the C2 JU shall report on the uncorrelated local ballistic missile track and shall assume R^2 for that track in accordance with the R^2 rules.

If the received remote track report does not cause relinquishment under the applicable TQ or Source TN rules, the C2 JU with R^2 retains responsibility for the real-time track until it is relinquished in accordance with the rules or until the track is dropped.

If the track is a ballistic missile track, a unit assuming R^2 for the ballistic missile track need not assume R^2 for the associated launch point; the unit no longer holding R^2 on the ballistic missile track may continue to report the launch point in accordance with the transmit/receive rules.

If IFF/SIF surveillance data are involved, the JU with R^2 reports all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for that track in accordance with the transmit rules for the J3 messages; JUs without R^2 monitor such data and only report if they hold different data with the J7.5 message.
If the C2 JU assumes R^2 for a track, the J3.XC1 message is transmitted only by the JU with R^2, at the next opportunity for new tracks when assuming R^2 or when data changes.
For air, surface, or land tracks, the minimum wait before transmitting tracks may be either an automatic or a manual function.
If a C2 JU is deactivating a receive filter, the minimum wait before reporting air, surface, or land tracks also applies.

exception_flow.content: 1. If a C^2 JU capable of assuming R^2 for air, surface, or land tracks has not completed sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration, or the minimum wait has not elapsed (12 seconds for air and surface tracks; 48 seconds for land tracks), the C^2 JU shall not transmit those tracks; Exit: track transmission is deferred until the checks and minimum wait are satisfied.
2. If a J3.7 message is transmitted by a non-R^2 JU with the Response Indicator set to value 1, it shall not affect reporting responsibility; Exit: reporting responsibility remains unchanged.

3. For Subsurface tracks, if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message containing the TN is received, the prohibition on another JU reporting the contact using that track number is lifted; Exit: another JU may report the contact using that track number under the stated drop-track condition.

4. For an emergency point, if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received, the unit with R^2 is declared inactive, or no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may, by operator action only, assume R^2 for the point; Exit: the assuming JU shall use the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit, and the latest JU to report the point has R^2.

5. If a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, or a J2 PPLI message other than J2.0 is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU, a C^2 JU shall assume R^2 of an IU in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C^2 JU has correlated local sensor data; Exit: the C^2 JU assumes R^2 for the IU.
6. If the track is dropped, the JU with R^2 does not retain responsibility beyond the drop; Exit: R^2 retention for that track ends when the track is dropped.

7. If a J3.5 (PTI = 0) message is received, Course and Speed shall be set to No Statement, the Track Quality field shall be set to 0, and Course, Speed, and Track Quality shall not be processed; Exit: those fields from the J3.5 (PTI = 0) message are not processed.

postconditions.content: The C2 JU has relinquished R^2 for the real-time track upon reception of a remote track report with TQ greater than the local TQ.

After applying all the above rules, the C2 JU has relinquished R^2 for the real-time track upon reception of a remote track report with TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose Source TN is greater than the local Source TN.

When a locally derived ballistic missile track is uncorrelated with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG, the C2 JU has reported on the uncorrelated local ballistic missile track and has assumed R^2 for that track in accordance with the R^2 rules.
For an emergency point, a JU assuming R^2 shall use the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.
For an emergency point, the latest JU to report the point has R^2.
For Subsurface tracks, the first JU to report a contact assumes reporting responsibility for that Track Number.

alternative_flow.content: If a correlation is not found, the C² JU shall integrate the received J2 PPLI report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.

If J2 messages are not received subsequent to this action and the receiving C² JU still has no local data, the C² JU assumes no responsibility for reporting the subject JU on the Surveillance Network PG.
If the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system's decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated.
After decorrelation, the C² JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field shall both be reported as No Statement.

A JU assumes R² if it has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface (Maritime) track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a locally held Land (Ground) track for approximately 120 seconds.

A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a locally held track shall assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.

Immediately prior to assuming R² for an air or surface track after receipt of a Drop Track message, a JU shall test the track for correlation in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and g, except the test shall be conducted only once.
A JU without R² for a nonreal-time track with the TQ field set to value 0 shall assume R² for that track when the track is locally updated by a new nonreal-time report.
A JU reporting a nonreal-time track has R² regardless of the time value in the track report; the time value in the track report is not a criterion for an R² shift.

A JU receiving a J2 PPLI message (with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure) from a JU that has R² of a locally held track, may assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.

A JU relinquishes R² for a real-time Air, Surface (Maritime) or Land (Ground) track upon reception of a remote track report in which remote TQ is greater than the local TQ, or upon reception of a remote track report for the track which contains a TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose STN is greater than the local STN.
A JU with R² on a track retains the responsibility until it is relinquished in accordance with the above rules or until the track is dropped.

use_case_name: Exchange IFF and SIF Transponder Data

goal.content: C2 JU aims to exchange IFF and SIF transponder data by transmitting available Modes I, II, and III Codes in J3.1/J3.5 (PTI = 0) messages and reporting IFF/SIF surveillance data in J3.2C1/J3.3C1 words for Air and Surface tracks.

preconditions.content: IFF/SIF transponder data, including Modes I, II, and III Codes when available, is available for exchange.
C2 JU has correlated local sensor data and holds R² for the tracks whose IFF/SIF surveillance data it reports in J3.2C1/J3.3C1 words.

C2 JU is in Active status and has completed sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration after initially achieving Active status or returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure before transmitting the affected tracks.

trigger.content: The use case is triggered when locally entered IFF/SIF data changes from zero to nonzero or from one nonzero value to another.

main_flow.content: C2 JU selects the IFF/SIF data to report for the track; if locally derived IFF/SIF data differs from the data being reported in the PPLI message, C2 JU reports the locally derived data.
C2 JU with R² exchanges IFF/SIF modes and codes by reporting all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for the track in accordance with the transmit rules for the J3 messages.

C2 JU transmits IFF/SIF surveillance data (J3.XC1) at the next opportunity for new tracks when assuming R² or when data changes, periodically at 1/8 the basic message rate for realtime tracks, and with each NRT track report.
C2 JU selects the applicable IFF/SIF surveillance message for the track category: J3.2 for Air tracks or J3.3 for Surface (Maritime) tracks.
When C2 JU receives remote Mode I or III data and has no own unit data (R² UNIT NO DATA), C2 JU accepts the data and transmits it in a J3.XC1 word at the next transmit opportunity (AT).

C2 JU sets the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator in the J3 message to value 2 when all IFF/SIF nonzero mode codes were obtained from or are the same as the codes received in the J2 message for the subject TN; otherwise, if the Mode II code was obtained from or is the same as the Mode II code received in the J2 message, C2 JU sets the indicator to value 1.
Software inhibits any change to a valid Mode II code for the specific local track.
C2 JU treats all unique Mode II codes as unique tracks.
When local sensors detect a Mode II code change, C2 JU treats it as a new track.
Receiving units that hold valid nonzero IFF/SIF data respond as required by the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix, Table 4.7-5.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 2: when locally entered IFF/SIF data changes from zero to a nonzero value or from one nonzero value to another, C2 JU reports the difference in accordance with Table 4.7-5 IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix, using a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message to transmit the IFF/SIF Difference Report.

Diverges from Step 3: in response to operator action, a JU transmits a J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request to initiate data updating, providing a manual alternative to the periodic or event-driven surveillance transmission.
Diverges from Step 3: data updating can occur spontaneously when the R² unit reports a No Data status (value 0) for one or more modes in a required IFF/SIF Surveillance data report, J3.XC1.

Diverges from Step 4: if the locally held Environment/Category of a track differs from the Environment/Category received in a J3.X or J7.0 (ACT = 1) message for that track, the operator is alerted, even when the received Environment/Category is not implemented.

Diverges from Step 4: when a JU changes the Environment/Category of a track (e.g., Space to air, Air to space/surface/land), or when an operator rejects a difference report, and the JU has R², C2 JU transmits the local Environment/Category in the appropriate Surveillance report.

Diverges from Step 10: when a controlling unit receives a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message reporting an ID different from local ID data, it automatically rejects the received ID and originates a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message containing the local ID data with the Controlling Unit Indicator field set to value 1.

Diverges from Step 10: for NonR² JUs, when an ID conflict is indicated, the unit may take no action with respect to the reported ID; in this variant, an operator alert may be provided as a system option.
Diverges from Step 10: in the case of ID conflicts, the differences are presented to the operators for their evaluation, and these conflicts may also require voice coordination for final resolution.

Diverges from Step 10: when a NonR² unit receives a J7.5 (ACT = 2) message from the R² unit and holds valid local data (nonzero codes) for the requested mode(s), it responds by initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message; if the requested data has already been transmitted by another JU, the remaining JUs need not respond with their local data.

exception_flow.content: Diverges from Step 2 when an IFF/SIF Mode I, II, or III code field is all zeroes: an all-zero code is illegal for use as an assigned operational IFF/SIF Mode I, II, or III code and indicates that the reporting unit has no data; the branch treats that code field as indicating no data.

Diverges from Step 3 when a JU with R² receives or initiates a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message that results in no IFF/SIF data being held on the track: the JU shall not continue transmitting the periodic J3 message containing the continuation word with IFF/SIF data; the branch inhibits that continuing transmission.

Diverges from Step 10 when an IFF/SIF data conflict alert occurs during difference resolution: the operator has manual resolution actions available, including updating local data, initiating clear messages, initiating difference reports, changing local data to agree with remote, or decorrelating local data to assign a new track number.

Diverges from Step 10 when the same report is transmitted twice within 30 seconds during difference resolution: automatic transmission of the J7.5 (ACT = 1) message is inhibited and the operator is alerted (TC condition).

postconditions.content: IFF/SIF transponder data is exchanged through the specified J-series messages.

Following successful IFF/SIF difference resolution, the system state reflects the applicable resolution outcome: the local unit accepts and transmits received data in a J3.XC1 word (AT), accepts and transmits J3.XC1 on upgrade or rejects on downgrade with operator alert (AC1), accepts data on upgrade or takes no action on downgrade (AC2), accepts data on upgrade or rejects and transmits local data via J7.5 (ACT=1) on downgrade (AC3), or simply accepts the data (A).

use_case_name: Exchange IFF and SIF Transponder Data

goal.content: To exchange IFF/SIF modes and codes to ensure commonality of IFF/SIF data between the IUs.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU is a JU with R² if it is to transmit J3.XC1.
The C2 JU has R² for the track if it is responsible for IFF/SIF surveillance data reporting in the J3.2C1 and J3.3C1 words for Air and Surface tracks.
If the C2 JU is a nonR² unit responding to a J7.5 (ACT = 2) message from the R² unit, valid local data (nonzero codes) are held for the requested mode(s).
The applicable mode indicators are set when requesting update of IFF/SIF data via J7.5 (ACT = 2).

trigger.content: The C2 JU manually initiates a J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request with the applicable mode indicators set when requesting update of IFF/SIF data.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU manually initiates the J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request with the applicable mode indicators set when requesting update of IFF/SIF data.
R² units receiving the J7.5 (ACT = 2) message respond by initiating a J3.XC1 message regardless of the No Data status.
NonR² units receiving the J7.5 (ACT = 2) message from the R² unit respond by initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message if valid local data (nonzero codes) are held for the requested mode(s).

alternative_flow.content: When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert as required in Table 4.7-5, the operator may update local data manually or verify automatic inputs.
When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert as required in Table 4.7-5, the operator may initiate a J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message (any mode).
When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert as required in Table 4.7-5, the operator may initiate a J7.5 (ACT = 1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message (any mode).
When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert as required in Table 4.7-5, the operator may change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code.

When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert as required in Table 4.7-5, the operator may decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing the assignment of a new track number to local data.
When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert as required in Table 4.7-5, the operator may clear operator alert (any mode).
For new tracks when assuming R² or when data changes, the JU with R² transmits J3.XC1 at the next opportunity.

Any JU without R² entering a change of nonzero to nonzero or zero to nonzero value to its locally held Mode I, III or IV IFF/SIF data, or a change from zero to nonzero Mode II data, shall automatically report the new data in a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message.
JUs without R² are responsible for monitoring IFF/SIF data and only reporting if they hold different data with the J7.5 message.

exception_flow.content: Exception path 1 — No Data status: R² units receiving the J7.5 (ACT = 2) message respond by initiating a J3.XC1 message regardless of the No Data status; exit the exception path after initiating the J3.XC1 response.

Exception path 2 — Mode II code: change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; in the case of Mode II code, exit the exception path without changing local data to agree with remote data.

postconditions.content: The R² unit has initiated a J3.XC1 message in response to the J7.5 (ACT = 2) message, regardless of the No Data status.
A nonR² unit receiving the J7.5 (ACT = 2) message from the R² unit has initiated a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message if valid local data (nonzero codes) are held for the requested mode(s).

use_case_name: Exchange IFF and SIF Transponder Data

goal.content: To exchange surveillance information on the Link 16 network using fixed format messages, including IFF/SIF data for tracks.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU is participating in the exchange of J3 Surveillance messages.
Surveillance information, including track data (Air, Surface, Subsurface, Land, Space, or EW), has been identified or generated by the system.

trigger.content: The C2 JU has locally entered IFF/SIF data that changes from zero to nonzero or nonzero to another nonzero value, or receives a J7.5 (ACT = 1) Difference Report message indicating different ID/Environment/Category data.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU (with R²) reports all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for that track in accordance with the transmit rules for the J3 messages.

The C2 JU determines validity of codes for established tracks as either 'Valid Data' or 'No Data' based on criteria: No Data if no valid code is currently held; Valid Data if received from own sensors on two or more successive interrogations for Modes I, II, and III with same value, one interrogation for Mode IV, manually entered codes, or codes accepted per Table 4.7-5.

The C2 JU transmits IFF/SIF surveillance data in J3.2C1 and J3.3C1 words for Air and Surface tracks respectively, periodically at 1/8 the basic message rate for realtime tracks and with each NRT track report.
Any change in IFF/SIF code values from No Data to Valid Data or between Valid Data values is reported as occurring by the C2 JU.

If the C2 JU receives a J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message initiated by operator action, it automatically sets designated mode(s) for specified track to No Data status (except Mode IV may be automatic or operator-determined).

Upon receiving or initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message resulting in no IFF/SIF data being held on the track, the C2 JU shall not continue transmitting the periodic J3 message that includes the continuation word containing IFF/SIF data.

When reporting on the Surveillance NPG, if the C2 JU obtains target position via J12.6 Target Sorting message from a non-C² JU, it initially assigns TQ value per Table 4.4-7 and extrapolates received target’s position to time of transmission unless local sensor data has been correlated for the track.

exception_flow.content: If a C2 JU without R² receives a J3 message that includes a continuation word with remote IFF/SIF data or a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message differing from locally held data, it shall respond as indicated in Table 4.7-5.
If a C2 JU receives a J7.5 (ACT = 0) Mode IV Clear message, acceptance or rejection may be automatic or by operator determination.
If a C2 JU changes a local mode to a No Data status, it may do so without transmitting a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message.

postconditions.content: IFF/SIF surveillance data has been exchanged, with the JU with R² assumed to be reporting the most current data available in the interface.

Track information on the interface is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible, with data correlated and dual designation minimized.

use_case_name: Exchange IFF and SIF Transponder Data

goal.content: Enable C2 JU to exchange IFF/SIF transponder data via standardized message protocols (J7.5, J3.XC1) as defined in MIL-STD-6016B

preconditions.content: The C2 JU must be capable of transmitting and receiving IFF/SIF surveillance data reports (J3.XC1) and J7.5 messages as defined in MIL-STD-6016B.
The C2 JU must have valid local or remote track/mode data available for reporting, or be able to respond to requests for such data from other units (R², non-R²).
For Mode II code exchanges, the C2 JU must maintain Mode II code uniqueness to prevent erroneous track correlations; if a duplicate is detected, it shall not initiate changes until resolved.

If initiating an update request via J7.5 (ACT = 2), the C2 JU must ensure that the target unit (R² or non-R²) is capable of responding per specified rules (e.g., R² responds regardless of No Data status; non-R² only if holding valid local data).
The C2 JU must be configured to monitor and report differences in IFF/SIF data using the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix (Table 4.7-5) when applicable.

trigger.content: The use case is triggered by any JU without R² entering a change of nonzero to nonzero or zero to nonzero value to its locally held Mode I, III or IV IFF/SIF data, or a change from zero to nonzero Mode II data, which shall automatically report the new data in a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU transmits IFF/SIF surveillance data periodically via J3.XC1 messages, including own unit data and track information with associated mode codes.

Upon detecting a change in locally held Mode I, III, or IV IFF/SIF data (nonzero to nonzero or zero to nonzero), or a change from zero to nonzero Mode II data, the C2 JU automatically reports the new data in a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message.

If an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert, the C2 JU may initiate manual resolution actions such as updating local data manually, initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message, or initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 1) Difference Report message.
When responding to a J7.5 (ACT = 2) Update Request message, if the C2 JU is an R² unit, it shall respond by initiating a J3.XC1 message regardless of No Data status.

When responding to a J7.5 (ACT = 2) Update Request message, if the C2 JU is a non-R² unit holding valid local data for the requested mode(s), it shall respond by initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message; otherwise, it need not respond.
The C2 JU may transmit a J7.5 (ACT = 3) message to exchange codes that have special meaning for implementing JUs, following applicable rules defined in the standard.

alternative_flow.content: If the C2 JU receives a J7.5 (ACT = 2) message from an R² unit, it shall respond by initiating a J3.XC1 message regardless of No Data status.
If the C2 JU is a non-R² unit and receives a J7.5 (ACT = 2) message, it will respond only if valid local data (nonzero codes) are held for the requested mode(s); otherwise, it need not respond.
If the C2 JU receives a J7.5 (ACT = 2) message from another non-R² unit, it will not respond to the request.

Simulated tracks may be originated from simulated video mixed with live video, from message input provided by previously recorded or generated messages, or from a TDS’s internal simulation program; when Simulation Indicator is set in a J2 or J3 message, all associated data should be marked as simulated and not correlated with live tracks.
Prior coordination with all interface participants is required when transmitting simulated tracks on the interface to ensure they are not assigned TNs from other systems’ TN blocks.

exception_flow.content: If a C2 JU receives a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message, it shall automatically set the designated mode(s) for the specified track to No Data status, except that acceptance or rejection of a received J7.5 (ACT=0) Mode IV Clear message may be automatic or by operator determination.

If a C2 JU with R² initiates or receives a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message resulting in no IFF/SIF data being held on the track, it shall not continue transmitting the periodic J3 message that includes the continuation word containing IFF/SIF data.
Any C2 JU may change a local mode to a No Data status without transmitting a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message.

The operator display shall indicate that a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message was received, and if accepted, the No Data status should be used for all subsequent interface functions and data link messages until updated by valid code responses from local or remote sources.

postconditions.content: IFF/SIF surveillance data has been successfully exchanged between C2 JU and other units via J3.XC1 or J7.5 messages as appropriate.
If a J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message was accepted, the designated mode(s) for the specified track are set to No Data status.
If a J7.5 (ACT = 1) Difference Report message was transmitted, the recipient unit(s) have received updated IFF/SIF code differences per the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix.
If a J7.5 (ACT = 2) Update Request was responded to by an R² unit, a J3.XC1 message was initiated regardless of No Data status.
If a J7.5 (ACT = 2) Update Request was responded to by a non-R² unit holding valid local data, a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message was initiated with the requested mode codes.
Any special meaning codes exchanged via J7.5 (ACT = 3) have been processed according to applicable rules for implementing JUs.
Simulated tracks, if any were exchanged, are marked with Simulation Indicator and not correlated with live tracks.

use_case_name: Exchange IFF and SIF Transponder Data

goal.content: Enable C2 JUs to exchange IFF and SIF transponder data through standardized messages to maintain current and accurate track identification information across the network.

preconditions.content: IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) are available for transmission.
The C2 JU has a previously reported track for which the emergency point was initiated (if reporting on an emergency point).
For Land (Ground) tracks, if the J3.5C3 word is implemented, the Strength field must be computed from the Strength, Total Number of Vehicles field.
Current IFF/SIF data are defined as valid code responses that are no more than 40 seconds old since entry into the database by automatic or manual inputs.

trigger.content: The exchange of IFF and SIF transponder data is initiated by the periodic transmission of surveillance data, a change in locally held IFF/SIF data, an operator action requesting an update, or the receipt of a 'No Data' status report from another unit.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU with R² responsibility periodically transmits IFF/SIF surveillance data for its tracks using J3.XC1 messages, or when assuming R² or when data changes.
Other C2 JUs without R² monitor the surveillance data and report differences only if they hold different IFF/SIF data, using the J7.5 (ACT = 1) Difference Report message.

When a C2 JU detects a change in locally held IFF/SIF code values (from No Data to Valid Data or between Valid Data values), it reports the change via J7.5 (ACT = 1) according to the Difference Resolution Matrix.
If a C2 JU receives a 'No Data' status report or wishes to request an update, it may initiate a J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request message.
Upon receiving a J7.5 (ACT = 2) update request, the R² unit responds by transmitting a J3.XC1 message with its local IFF/SIF data regardless of No Data status.
Non-R² units receiving a J7.5 (ACT = 2) request from an R² unit respond with a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message if they hold valid nonzero local data for the requested mode(s).

alternative_flow.content: If a C2 JU receives a J3.XC1 message with 'No Data' status but holds valid nonzero local IFF/SIF data, it may respond by transmitting a J7.5 (ACT=1) Difference Report message according to the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix.

An operator may manually initiate a J7.5 (ACT=2) IFF/SIF Update Request message to solicit current data from other units; upon receipt, R² units respond with J3.XC1 regardless of their No Data status.
Non-R² units receiving a J7.5 (ACT=2) request from an R² unit will respond with J7.5 (ACT=1) only if they hold valid nonzero local data for the requested mode(s); otherwise, they do not respond.
Non-R² units receiving a J7.5 (ACT=2) request from another non-R² unit shall not respond to the request.

When resolving differences via Table 4.7-5, actions such as Accept (A), Conflict (C), Transmit Local (T1), or Alert Operator (AC) are taken depending on whether data is current, non-current, or conflicting between local and remote sources.

exception_flow.content: If a track with Valid Data subsequently fails to respond to interrogations, it shall not be changed to No Data status unless a Clear action (J7.5 ACT=0) is explicitly taken.

When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert, available manual resolution actions include: updating local data manually, initiating J7.5 (ACT=0) Clear message, initiating J7.5 (ACT=1) Difference Report, changing local data to agree with remote (except Mode II), decorrelating local data to assign a new track number, or clearing the operator alert.
Non-R² units receiving a J7.5 (ACT=2) Update Request from another non-R² unit shall not respond to the request, exiting the update flow without transmission.

If requested IFF/SIF data has already been transmitted by another JU in response to an R² unit's J7.5 (ACT=2) request, remaining JUs need not respond with their local data, exiting the response flow early.

postconditions.content: IFF/SIF surveillance data for Air and Surface tracks is reported by the JU with R² responsibility using J3.2C1 and J3.3C1 words, ensuring the most current data available in the interface is transmitted.

Validity of IFF/SIF codes for established tracks is determined as either 'Valid Data' or 'No Data' based on specific criteria: 'No Data' if no valid code is held, or 'Valid Data' if codes are received from own sensors on successive interrogations (two or more for Modes I, II, III; one for Mode IV) or manually entered/accepted via the Difference Resolution Matrix.

Changes in IFF/SIF code values from 'No Data' to 'Valid Data' or between 'Valid Data' values are reported as occurring, while changes from 'Valid Data' to 'No Data' resulting from a clearing function (J7.5 ACT = 0) do not cause a change report transmission.
Tracks with Valid Data that subsequently fail to respond to interrogations are not changed to 'No Data' status unless a Clear action is explicitly taken.

Data updating occurs spontaneously when an R² unit reports 'No Data' status (value 0) in a J3.XC1 message, prompting receiving units with valid nonzero data to respond per the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix.
Upon receipt of a J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request message, R² units respond by initiating a J3.XC1 message regardless of their No Data status.

Non-R² units receiving a J7.5 (ACT = 2) message from an R² unit respond by initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message only if they hold valid local nonzero data for the requested mode(s); if the data was already transmitted by another JU, remaining JUs need not respond.
Non-R² units receiving a J7.5 (ACT = 2) message from other non-R² units do not respond to the request.

The exchange of IFF/SIF modes and codes encompasses five functional areas: Surveillance Data Reporting, Unique Mode II Code Protection, Clearing IFF/SIF Data, Difference Resolution, and Update Request, utilizing J2.XC1, J3.XC1, and J7.5 messages as summarized in Table 4.4-6.

goal.content: Receive situational awareness information from the Surveillance NPG including track and Reference Point data necessary to support the platform mission.

preconditions.content: The Link 16 network is operational and capable of exchanging surveillance information using fixed format messages.
C² JUs participating in the exchange of J3 Surveillance messages are transmitting surveillance information in Network PGs as defined in paragraph 4.2.3.10.5.

trigger.content: The Non-C2 JU receives a surveillance message (e.g., J3 series) or a status change message (e.g., J7.0 with ACT = 3 or 4) containing updated track data or alert indicators.

main_flow.content: The Non-C2 JU receives situational awareness information from the Surveillance NPG including track and Reference Point data necessary to support the platform mission.
The received surveillance information may include Point surveillance data included in the J3.0 Reference Point message and the J3.1 Emergency Point message.
The received surveillance information may include Air and Surface (Maritime) surveillance data included in the J3.2 Air Track message and the J3.3 Surface (Maritime) Track message.
The received surveillance information may include Subsurface (Maritime) surveillance data included in the J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track message.
The received surveillance information may include Land (Ground) surveillance data included in the J3.5 Land (Ground) Point/Track message.
The received surveillance information may include Space and Ballistic Missile surveillance data included in the J3.6 Space Track message.
The received surveillance information may include Electronic Warfare surveillance data included in the J3.7 EW Product Information message.

If the received data includes Request Indicator Values for categories such as REFERENCE POINT, EA DATA, ES DATA, EW FIXES, WEAPON STATUS, AMPLIFICATION, or FILTER, the system processes the corresponding response messages (e.g., J3.0, J3.7, J14.2, J10.2, J13.3, J13.5, J6.0, J7.6).

The Non-C2 JU applies receive filters to delete data received on a data link prior to entry into an IU database if configured to prevent data link overload conditions, overload of a system database, and/or undesired data from entering a system database.

alternative_flow.content: If the received data includes a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message, the Non-C2 JU shall clear the alert in its databases upon receipt.
Optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J2.0 message with the EMG IND and/or FT IND set to value 0.
Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message initiating/terminating an alert on a PU/RU being forwarded onto Link 16, the FJU shall accept and report the condition in the J2.0 message.
Other receiving JUs shall initiate/terminate the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message.
A C² JU shall have the capability to initiate/terminate a force tell alert on another JU by setting/clearing the FT IND in a J7.0 (ACT = 4) message.
Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 4) message, the JU whose force tell status is being changed shall accept and report the change in its J2 message.
The other JUs shall set/clear the alert indicator in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 4) message.
Optionally, other JUs may clear the alert indicator upon reception of a J2 message with FT IND set to value 0.
If the received data includes Request Indicator Values for FILTER, the system processes the corresponding response message J7.6, which is transmitted to a specific address only.
If the received data includes Request Indicator Values for REFERENCE POINT, the system responds only with J3.0 lines and areas defined by more than one J3.0 message.

If the received data includes Request Indicator Values for EA DATA, ES DATA, or EW FIXES, the system responds only with existing EW ACTION VALUE = 7, 8, or 9 evaluations and associations concerning the applicable requested data type, which own JU has initiated if the request is collectively addressed, or locally held if the request is specifically addressed.
These J14.2 messages shall be addressed to the requesting unit, with R/C = 1.

If the received data includes a track that needs to be dropped due to operator error or simulation status change, the track shall be dropped using the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, and a new track shall be reported.
The one exception to dropping a track via J7.0 (ACT = 0) is that a change from live to simulated shall be accepted if the track is being received from an FJU.
If the Non-C2 JU has the capability to purge remote tracks/points, it may automatically drop a remote track/point after a specified time interval has elapsed since the track's/point's last report.
The JU shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a purged remote track/point.

exception_flow.content: If a Non-C2 JU receives a J7.0 (ACT = 2) Change Data Order message containing an ID of Pending, it shall not accept that order.
Receiving JUs which do not implement the changed Environment/Category and have R² on the track must cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

postconditions.content: The Non-C2 JU has accepted the alert in its databases.
The Non-C2 JU has cleared the alert in its databases if set, upon receipt of a J2 message with the EMG IND set to value 0.
The Non-C2 JU has set or cleared the alert indicator in its databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 4) message regarding force tell status changes.
Optionally, other JUs may clear the alert indicator upon reception of a J2 message with FT IND set to value 0.

goal.content: Receive situational awareness information from the Surveillance NPG including track and Reference Point data necessary to support the platform mission.

preconditions.content: C2 JUs participating in the exchange of J3 Surveillance messages shall transmit surveillance information in Network PGs as defined in paragraph 4.2.3.10.5.
Non-C2 JUs shall not transmit on the Surveillance NPG.

trigger.content: C2 JUs transmit surveillance information in Network PGs as defined in paragraph 4.2.3.10.5.

main_flow.content: Non-C2 JUs receive situational awareness information from the Surveillance NPG including track and Reference Point data necessary to support the platform mission.
The received surveillance information includes point surveillance data included in the J3.0 Reference Point message and the J3.1 Emergency Point message.
The received surveillance information includes Air and Surface (Maritime) surveillance data included in the J3.2 Air Track message and the J3.3 Surface (Maritime) Track message.
The received surveillance information includes Subsurface (Maritime) surveillance data included in the J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track message.
The received surveillance information includes Land (Ground) surveillance data included in the J3.5 Land (Ground) Point/Track message.
The received surveillance information includes Space and Ballistic Missile surveillance data included in the J3.6 Space Track message.
The received surveillance information includes Electronic Warfare surveillance data included in the J3.7 EW Product Information message.

alternative_flow.content: If a JU drops or ceases reporting SA information after having reported on the interface, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.
A J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted on remote reports; remote reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria.
Non-C2 JUs shall monitor the Surveillance NPG to support their missions but are prohibited from transmitting on this NPG.
Remote surveillance track and point data available in the J3 series messages shall provide non-C2 JUs situational awareness and early warning information.

exception_flow.content: If a correlation is not found, the C2 JU shall integrate the received PPLI report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.

If J2 messages are not received subsequent to this action and the receiving C2 JU still has no local data, the C2 JU assumes no responsibility for reporting the subject JU on the Surveillance Network PG.
If the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system's decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated.
After decorrelation, the C2 JU shall maintain a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field shall both be removed as to statement.

A C2 JU shall assume R² of an IU (including C³ and non-C³ JUs and Forwarded TUs and ROs) in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C2 JU has correlated local sensor data when: a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, or a J2 PPLI message, other than C2.0, is received with the NPS indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the KUJ for a PU, RU, or other IU, or the Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.

A C2 JU assuming R² of an IU reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG. The type of surveillance message will depend upon the Environment/Category of the IU being reported. The Identity shall be reported as Friend. The Track Number, Platform and Platform Activity values received in previous PPLI messages shall be reported. The PPLI Track Number and Identity indicator shall be reported as value 1, and shall be maintained if another C2 JU assumes R² of the IU.

goal.content: To initiate an emergency or force tell alert on tracks by setting the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in J3.2 Air Track, J3.3 Surface (Maritime) Track, J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track, or J3.5 Land (Ground) Point/Track messages.

preconditions.content: The System Operator has identified a track or point—specifically an Air Track, Surface (Maritime) Track, Subsurface (Maritime) Track, or Land (Ground) Point/Track—and the applicable J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 message in which to initiate the emergency or force tell alert.
The initiating JU possesses the R² role required to initiate an emergency or force tell alert on tracks.
If the alert to be initiated is an EMG IND emergency alert, the selected track or point is not a Reference Point, line, area, or Space/Ballistic Missile Track.

trigger.content: The System Operator, acting through the JU with R² for the track, initiates an emergency or force tell alert by setting the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in the J3.2 Air Track, J3.3 Surface (Maritime) Track, J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track, or J3.5 Land (Ground) Point/Track message.

main_flow.content: The System Operator selects the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND for the identified track or point, according to whether an emergency alert or a force tell alert is to be initiated.

The System Operator sets the selected EMG IND or FT IND to 1 in the applicable J3 track or point message: J3.2 Air Track, J3.3 Surface (Maritime) Track, J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track, or J3.5 Land (Ground) Point/Track.
The J3 message with the set EMG IND or FT IND indicates the emergency or force tell condition, initiating the emergency or force tell alert.
The J3 message with the set indicator overrides all operator-controllable data filters.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 1 when an emergency alert is to be initiated: the JU with R² selects the EMG IND for the identified track or point.
Diverges from Step 1 when a force tell alert is to be initiated: the JU with R² selects the FT IND for the identified track or point.
Diverges from Step 2 for an Air Track: the JU with R² sets the selected EMG IND or FT IND to 1 in the J3.2 Air Track message.
Diverges from Step 2 for a Surface (Maritime) Track: the JU with R² sets the selected EMG IND or FT IND to 1 in the J3.3 Surface (Maritime) Track message.
Diverges from Step 2 for a Subsurface (Maritime) Track: the JU with R² sets the selected EMG IND or FT IND to 1 in the J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track message.
Diverges from Step 2 for a Land (Ground) Point/Track: the JU with R² sets the selected EMG IND or FT IND to 1 in the J3.5 Land (Ground) Point/Track message.

exception_flow.content: Exception branch 1 — At main flow step 2, if the System Operator attempts to set an EMG IND to 1 on a Reference Point or a Space/Ballistic Missile Track, the emergency alert shall not be initiated. Exit: no emergency alert is initiated on that target.

Exception branch 2 — At main flow step 2, if the System Operator attempts to set an EMG IND or FT IND on a track or point that is ineligible for such an alert (for example, an illegal change marked 'X', or a change from SPACE TRK to AIR TRK marked 'S' that requires operator alert), the system shall reject the data as invalid per paragraph 4.7.1.2.1. Exit: the data is rejected as invalid.

Exception branch 3 — At main flow step 2, if the System Operator is a JU without R², the JU shall initiate the emergency or force tell alert by setting the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message. Exit: the alert initiation is performed through the J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message.

Exception branch 4 — At main flow step 2, if the System Operator attempts to use the J3.1 Emergency Point message, alerts are not used for that message because J3.1 Emergency Points cannot be filtered. Exit: no alert is set in the J3.1 Emergency Point message.

postconditions.content: The applicable J3.2 Air Track, J3.3 Surface (Maritime) Track, J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track, or J3.5 Land (Ground) Point/Track message contains the selected EMG IND or FT IND set to 1.
The track or point with EMG IND or FT IND set to 1 is not filtered; the indicator overrides all operator-controllable filters, including security filters.
All receiving JUs accept the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J3 message with EMG IND or FT IND set to 1.

The alert remains active in receiving JUs' databases until it is terminated by receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message or optionally cleared by reception of a J3.X message with EMG IND and/or FT IND set to 0.

goal.content: To report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts by transmitting an emergency point as a J3.1 message.

preconditions.content: An emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts exists.
For reporting on a previously reported emergency point, reporting is performed through operator action only.
If a JU is reporting on a previously reported emergency point, that JU has additional or more current information on the point.

If another JU is to assume R^2 for an emergency point, one of the following has occurred: a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received on the emergency point, the unit with R^2 is declared inactive, or no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals.
The emergency is not on a reference point or space/ballistic missile track.

trigger.content: An emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts is to be reported by transmitting an emergency point as a J3.1 message.

main_flow.content: System Operator initiates reporting of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts by transmitting an emergency point as a J3.1 message.
Assign a TN(s) to the emergency point reported on the interface by the reporting JU.

If the emergency point is related to a previously reported track/point, include the TN, Previously Reported associated with the emergency point as amplifying information, and use a TN, Reference different from the TN, Previously Reported.

When available, include IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) in the J3.1 message; the IFF/SIF data shall contain the IFF/SIF modes and codes of the previously reported track for which the emergency point was initiated.
For reporting on a previously reported emergency point, perform the report through operator action only when the JU has additional or more current information on the point.
When assuming R^2 for an emergency point, use the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.

alternative_flow.content: 1. If the emergency point is not related to a previously reported track/point, the J3.1 message does not require the TN, Previously Reported as amplifying information.
2. If the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1 in the J3.1 message, the report is for exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.
3. If IFF/SIF data are not available, the condition for transmitting IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) in the J3.1 message is not met.
4. If the JU does not have additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point, the condition for reporting on that point through operator action only is not met.
5. If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received on the emergency point, another JU may, by operator action only, assume R^2 for the point.
6. If the unit with R^2 is declared inactive, another JU may, by operator action only, assume R^2 for the point.
7. If no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may, by operator action only, assume R^2 for the point.
8. When a JU assumes R^2 for an emergency point, it shall use the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.

exception_flow.content: If the emergency condition is on a reference point or space/ballistic missile track, the emergency shall not be initiated; exit the use case without initiating an emergency point report.

If the reporting JU is reporting on a previously reported emergency point but does not have additional or more current information on the point, it may not perform the report through operator action only; exit the use case without reporting on that emergency point.

If a J3.1 emergency point related to a previously reported track/point would have a TN, Reference that is not different from the TN, Previously Reported, the message does not satisfy the requirement; exit the use case without transmitting the noncompliant J3.1 message.
If an alert is being considered for the J3.1 Emergency Point message, alerts are not used for the J3.1 Emergency Point message because these points cannot be filtered; exit the alert path.

postconditions.content: The existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts has been reported by transmitting an emergency point as a J3.1 message.
The emergency point reported on the interface has been assigned a TN(s) by the reporting JU.

If the emergency point is related to a previously reported track/point, the J3.1 message contains, as amplifying information, the TN, Previously Reported associated with the emergency point, and the emergency point has a TN, Reference different from the TN, Previously Reported.

When available, IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) are transmitted in the J3.1 message, and the IFF/SIF data in the J3.1 message contain the IFF/SIF modes and codes of the previously reported track for which the emergency point was initiated.
The latest JU to report the emergency point has R^2 for that point.
If a JU assumes R^2 for an emergency point, it uses the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.
If the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1 in the J3.1 message, the report is for exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.
No alert is used for the J3.1 Emergency Point message because these points cannot be filtered.

goal.content: To record the details of voucher distribution, specifically voucher sales between the MISU sales team and Distributors, in the system.

preconditions.content: The system contains pre-existing Distributor Master and Sales Man Master records for the distributor and sales personnel involved in the voucher sale, including their names, so the mandatory fields can be populated.
The system has available voucher stock (Batch No's and voucher No's) to allocate vouchers during the transaction process.
The settings master contains the Wholesale Rate applicable to the sale date, enabling the system to calculate the Invoice Amount from the Quantity Sold.

trigger.content: The use case is triggered when the VMU User initiates a distribution transaction to capture voucher sales details.

main_flow.content: The VMU User selects the Name of the Distributor and the Name of the Sales Man from their respective masters.
The VMU User enters the Date of Distribution (via date selection option) and the Required Quantity of vouchers sold (numeric entry only).
Upon entry of the required number of vouchers, the system automatically picks the Batch Numbers and Voucher Numbers from available voucher stock and lists them in a grid format.
The system automatically calculates the Invoice Amount by multiplying the Wholesale Rate, taken from the settings master based on the sale date, by the Quantity Sold.
The system generates an auto-generated number as the Distribution Invoice Number.
The system records the sales details into the Database.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 1: If the Distributor or Salesman name is not available in the system, the VMU User navigates to the respective master screen and enters the new Distributor and Salesman details without closing the current distribution screen.

postconditions.content: The system has captured and stored the voucher sale details, including Distributor-wise, Salesman-wise, and Batch No wise details, in the database.
The system has generated an auto-generated number as the Distribution Invoice Number for the completed voucher distribution transaction.
