goal.content: To enter claim information exactly into the system from the manual claim form.

preconditions.content: A manual claim form (Treatment Form) submitted by the VSP is available to the MSIU Field Office User.
The MSIU Field Office User has access to the Claim Entry / Processing module of the Voucher Management System.
The system has the MSIU treatment master available to support entry of Syndrome, Clinical Examinations, Diagnosis, Lab Test, Drugs and Other Measures.

trigger.content: When a manual claim form is available, the MSIU Field Office User initiates claim registration by entering the claim information from the manual claim form into the system.

main_flow.content: The MSIU Field Office User selects a Treatment Form Number from the list of claim receipt details that have not yet been entered into the system.
Upon selection of the Treatment Form Number, the system automatically populates the Submitted Date and VSP Name fields. The Date of submission should be the current date.

Based on the entered Voucher No, the system automatically populates Client Details (Address as per Claim Form), Details of syndromes treated, Lab Test Details, Drugs Details, Success of Treatment, Referral To Treatment, and Partner Treated fields; the user is not allowed to alter any auto-populated treatment information.
The MSIU Field Office User enters the No of Mentioned Forms and No of Available Forms.
The MSIU Field Office User manually enters the Patient Name and Age and selects the Gender from the options Male/Female.
The MSIU Field Office User enters the Street/Road manually and selects District, Sub-District, County, etc. from master records for the Address field.
The MSIU Field Office User selects the Doctor Name from a list populated from the VSP Staff Master and may optionally enter a Doctor's Note.
The system captures the remaining master claim information, including Visit Count, Patient Type, Contact No, HIV Details, and Claim Status.
The MSIU Field Office User selects the Patient Status from a list of status options.
The system calculates the Claim Amount based on the visit type.
The system records the entered claim information in its database.

exception_flow.content: If details required for the Address field (such as District, Sub-District, County) are not present in the Master record, the system provides a provision to navigate quickly to its master screen to enter the new details and then return to the Claim Entry Screen.

postconditions.content: Data from the forms is entered into a computer database.

goal.content: To enter and validate claim transaction details including patient, treatment, and financial information into the system for reimbursement processing.

preconditions.content: The MSIU Field Office User must be authenticated and authorized to access the Claim Entry / Processing module.
The Service Provider must have completed the standardized patient treatment documentation form and summary claims form for reimbursement.
Master data records (including Drugs, Syndrome, Clinical Examination, Diagnosis, Lab Test, Patient Status, and Claim Status) must exist in the system to support claim validation and entry.

trigger.content: The MSIU Field Office User receives the completed standardized patient treatment documentation form and summary claims form from the Service Provider for reimbursement.

main_flow.content: The MSIU Field Office User selects the 'Claim Entry / Processing' module.

If all data validations pass, the system saves the claim record to the database with status indicating it is ready for reimbursement processing.
The system confirms successful registration of the claim submission to the user.

alternative_flow.content: If data checks and plausibilisations fail during step 3, the system flags the claim as conspicuous for investigation by the VMU.
If Contact No is missing during claim entry, the system allows continuation since it is not mandatory per design constraints.
If Treatment Form No corresponds to a form not yet entered in the system, the system permits entry but may flag for follow-up validation.

exception_flow.content: If mandatory information is incomplete during claim entry, the system rejects the claim submission and does not accept it for processing.
If data checks or plausibilisations fail during validation, the system flags the claim as conspicuous and routes it for investigation by the VMU instead of proceeding to reimbursement.

If the claim is conspicuous (fails validation), it is flagged for investigation and clearance by the VMU.
The system has recorded all mandatory master-level information except Contact No, as per design constraints.

use_case_name: Enter and Validate a Treatment Claim

goal.content: To enter a treatment claim and validate it manually and through the system.

preconditions.content: The MSIU Field Office User is ready to enter a treatment claim in the system.
The claim form for the treatment claim has been received by the MSIU Field Office from the VSP.

trigger.content: The MSIU Field Office User initiates 'Claim Entry' to process a Treatment (claims) Form submitted by the VSP.

main_flow.content: Before entering the claim, the MSIU Field Office User manually checks the Treatment (claims) Form to determine whether any mandatory information is missing.
The MSIU Field Office User initiates claim entry in the Claim Processing system and enters the Treatment Form No; the system captures the Treatment Form No and Claim No.
When the Form No is chosen, the system automatically populates the Submitted Date and VSP Name.
The system captures Voucher No, Visit Count, and Patient Type from the Bar Code reader based on the Voucher Slip Stick on the Claim Form.

Based on the Voucher No entered, the system automatically populates Client Details (Address), Details of syndromes treated, Lab Test Details, Drugs Details, Success of Treatment, Referral To Treatment, and Partner Treated fields.

The MSIU Field Office User manually enters the remaining claim form data exactly as recorded on the manual claim form; during this entry the system captures the additional master information for the claim, including Patient Name, Age, Gender, Contact No, Doctor Name, Doctor's Note, HIV Details, Patient Status, Claim Amount, and Claim Status.
The MSIU Field Office User validates the claim using a thumb-print reader for biometric verification.

Upon saving, the system validates every captured data element—voucher number, clinical information, diagnosis details, drug and investigation details, and costs—against the Database and only accepts the claim if the mandatory information is complete.
After validation, the system processes the claim and updates the Database with the validated claim information.

alternative_flow.content: The system allows the user to enter any number of Syndrome, Clinical Examination, Diagnosis, Lab Test, Drugs and Other Measures in any treatment level based on MSIU treatment master.
Diverges from Step 6 when the date of sale is a past date: the system uses the current system date as the date of distribution while accepting the past date of sale.

exception_flow.content: At Step 1, during the manual check of the Treatment (claims) Form before claim entry, if the MSIU Field Office User finds that mandatory information is missing, the user marks the Claim (Treatment Form) status as Rejected and sends it back to the VSP.

At Step 8, because all master-level information other than Contact No is mandatory and the system only accepts claims if mandatory information is complete, if any mandatory information is missing or any false information exists, the system changes the claim status to 'Rejection' or 'Quarantine', stores the claim in the quarantine area, and captures the reason for this status; the field office rejects the claim back to the VSP.

At Step 8, quarantined forms are sent back to the VSP for verification. If the VSP returns the claim with satisfactory details, the claim will be entered onto the system in the following month's batch. If the VSP returns the claim without satisfactory details, it does not proceed to re-entry in the following month's batch, indicating termination or permanent rejection of that claim instance within this use case.

At Step 7, if the thumb impression captured in the claim form mismatches previous visits for the same voucher number for the same patient/client/partner, the system automatically makes a count; if a claim from the same VSP has more than two thumb impression mismatches, the system produces a warning message and automatically In-Activates the VSP.
At Step 8, the system includes a future date sale validation check available to handle cases where the date of sale is in the future.

postconditions.content: The field office validates the claim form manually and through the system.
The Database has been updated with the validated claim information.

use_case_name: Enter and Validate a Treatment Claim

goal.content: To enter and validate a treatment claim into the system, ensuring all mandatory information is complete before acceptance.

preconditions.content: The VSP staff should get the thump impression from the patient and should stick the voucher slip on the claim form.
The user should enter the information exactly into the system from the manual claim form.

trigger.content: The MSIU Field Office User receives a completed manual claim form with voucher slip and thumb impression from the VSP staff and initiates entry of the claim into the system.

main_flow.content: The system automatically generates the Claim number with Hospital Code as Suffix + 8 digit.
The user enters the Treatment Form No (List Form No from Claim receipt details which all are not yet entered in claim).
The user enters master level information including Syndrome, Clinical Examination, Diagnosis, Lab Test, Drugs Name – Frequency –No of days - Qty, and Other measure.
If applicable, the user enters information for First Follow UP (Diagnosis, Drugs Name – Frequency –No of days - Qty) or Second Follow UP (Diagnosis, Drugs Name – Frequency –No of days - Qty).
The system validates every information during claim entry against the MSIU treatment master and mandatory requirements.
The system accepts the claim only if the mandatory information is complete.

alternative_flow.content: If the user enters incorrect Voucher No, the system may fail to automatically populate dependent fields such as Client Details, Syndrome treated, Lab Test Details, Drugs Details, Success of Treatment, Referral To Treatment, and Partner Treated.
If the user alters any information about treatment which is populating from the system based on Voucher No, it violates the system assumption that users will not alter auto-populated data.
If mandatory master level information (Syndrome, Clinical Examination, Diagnosis, Lab Test, Drugs, Other Measures) is incomplete during entry, the system will not accept the claim.
Claims with conspicuous or irregular data will be flagged for investigation and cleared by the VMU rather than being reimbursed immediately via bank transfer.

exception_flow.content: If the mandatory information is not complete during claim entry, the system will reject the claim and will not accept it.

If the user enters an incorrect Voucher No, the system may fail to auto-populate required fields (Client Details, Syndrome treated, Lab Test Details, Drugs Details, Success of Treatment, Referral To Treatment, Partner Treated), potentially causing validation failure or incomplete claim submission.
If the user alters any treatment information that was auto-populated from the system based on Voucher No, this violates system assumptions and may trigger rejection or manual review.

postconditions.content: The claim is successfully entered into the computer database with all mandatory master level information (Syndrome, Clinical Examination, Diagnosis, Lab Test, Drugs, Other Measures) complete.
A unique Claim number has been automatically generated by the system using the Hospital Code as Suffix + 8 digit format.
The Treatment Form No from the claim receipt details is recorded in the system for the claim.
All entered data has passed validation checks and plausibilisations against the MSIU treatment master.
The claim is marked as 'clean' and eligible for reimbursement via bank transfer, unless flagged as conspicuous for further investigation by the VMU.

use_case_name: Enter and Validate a Treatment Claim

goal.content: The MSIU Field Office User enters treatment claim data into the system and validates it against mandatory requirements and master data to ensure accuracy before processing payment.

preconditions.content: The system must have all mandatory master level information available and complete before accepting a claim.
The user must have the manual claim form with complete information ready for entry into the system.
The user must possess the correct Voucher Number associated with the treatment to allow automatic population of client and treatment details.
The Treatment Form Number being entered must correspond to a claim receipt detail that has not yet been entered into the system.

trigger.content: The MSIU Field Office User receives collected claim forms from the VSP (Service Provider) for processing.

main_flow.content: The MSIU Field Office User receives collected claim forms from the VSP.

The user enters the Voucher Number into the system, which automatically populates client details, syndrome treated, lab test details, drug details, and other treatment information based on the voucher.
The user enters the Treatment Form Number, selecting from a list of form numbers from claim receipt details that have not yet been entered.

The user enters or verifies mandatory clinical information including Syndrome, Clinical Examination, Diagnosis, Lab Test, Drugs (Name, Frequency, No of days, Qty), and Other Measures based on the MSIU treatment master.

The system validates the entered information against mandatory master data requirements; if any mandatory information is missed or false information exists, the system rejects the claim or places it in a quarantine area.
If the claim passes validation, the system accepts the claim entry for processing.

alternative_flow.content: If any mandatory information is missed or any false information exists during validation, the field office will reject the claim back to VSP and the system will keep those claims in a quarantine area.
The quarantined forms will be sent back to the VSP for verification; if the VSP returns the claim with satisfactory details, the claims will be entered into the system in the following month's batch.

exception_flow.content: If any mandatory information is missed or any false information exists during validation, the MSIU Field Office User rejects the claim back to the VSP, and the system places the claim in a quarantine area.
The quarantined claim forms are sent back to the VSP for verification and correction of missing or false information.
If the VSP returns the rejected claim with satisfactory and complete details, the MSIU Field Office User enters the corrected claim into the system in the following month's processing batch.

postconditions.content: The system sets the claim status to 'Accepted' if all mandatory information is complete and no false data is detected.
The system calculates the claim amount based on the visit type (First Visit, First Follow Up, or Second Follow Up) using fees from VSP Payment terms and drug costs from the Drugs Master.
The system automatically generates a unique Claim Number consisting of the Hospital Code as a suffix plus an 8-digit number.
The validated claim entry is stored in the database and is ready for further processing (e.g., payment).

goal.content: To record the return of previously sold vouchers from a distributor back to the MSIU sales team.

preconditions.content: A distributor plans to return vouchers back to the MSIU sales team.
The Distributor Master is populated with the distributor records required for the return.
The Sales Man Master is populated with the sales man records required for the return.

trigger.content: A distributor plans to return previously sold vouchers back to the MSIU sales team.

main_flow.content: The VMU User accesses the Voucher Sales Return module.
The VMU User selects the Distributor Name from the Distributor Master.
The VMU User selects the Sales Man Name from the Sales Man Master.
The system defaults the Sales Return Date to the system date, and the VMU User enters a Sales Return Date that is not later than the system date.
The VMU User enters the transaction part details, including the Batch No and Voucher No, for the vouchers being returned.
The system verifies that the returned voucher was sold to the selected Distributor.
The system calculates the Sales Return Amount as the number of vouchers returned multiplied by the whole sale rate.
The system records the voucher sales return with the captured master and transaction part details and the calculated Sales Return Amount.

At main-flow step 6, if the system determines that a returned voucher was not sold to the selected distributor, the system will not accept those vouchers as return.

postconditions.content: The system records the voucher sales return with the captured master and transaction part details.

goal.content: The MSIU Field Office User records client feedback collected by the MSIU Admin team into the system to track client satisfaction with treatment services provided through the voucher system.

goal.content: To acquire command control of the system during normal mode.

preconditions.content: The system is in normal operating mode, defined as Monday through Friday between 5:00am and 8:00pm.
The Operator is logged on to the system and is the only operator logged on at that time.
The Operator is using a workstation specified for command control.

trigger.content: The Operator requests command control via the logon screen.

main_flow.content: The Operator requests command control via the logon screen.
The system verifies that the Operator has authorization for command control.
The system activates command control for the Operator.
The Operator has command control of the system during normal mode.

alternative_flow.content: If command control is enabled by another user and the logging-in Operator has higher security, the system requests the Operator to accept or deny command control; if the Operator takes command control, the other user is notified.

exception_flow.content: At step 1, if another operator is already logged onto the system when the Operator attempts to log on, the request fails because only one operator may be logged onto the system at any given time.

At step 2, if Field Maintenance Staff attempts to acquire command control for purposes requiring a change of system mode during normal operation, the request is rejected because Field Maintenance Staff cannot change system mode.

postconditions.content: The Operator has command control of the system during normal mode.
If another user was logged in with command control and the Operator takes command control, the other user is notified.

alternative_flow.content: 1. If the TMC workstations or network server fails, resulting in loss of field status at the TMC, alternate control shall be at FCU South or FCU North; the operator shall be able to dial in from a back up computer to either FCU North or FCU south and open and close the reversible lanes.
2. If FCU North or South fails (FCU Controller failures or FCU-TSU communications failure), alternate control is at the non-failed FCU (North or South).

3. If FCUs North and South both fail (FCU Controller failures or FCUs-TSU and FCU-FCU communications failure), alternate control units include direct control at DCUs 1-5 and CMS 1-12 control from CMS cabinets; the operator shall be able to connect a lap top computer at the DCUs and operate the devices or perform manual operation from the MCU, and connect a lap top on the CMS cabinet and control the signs or perform manual operation of the signs from the cabinet.
4. If any DCU 1-5 fails, alternate control unit is MCU and manual control at the field devices.
5. If any MCU fails, alternate control unit is manual control at the field devices related to the failed MCU; the devices can be manually controlled/operated from their cabinets (e.g.: Gates).

exception_flow.content: Exception 1: If another operator is already logged onto the system, the Operator cannot be logged on to acquire command control because only one operator may be logged onto the system at any given time; exit the use case without acquiring command control.

Exception 2: If the user does not have Operator command-control authorization for normal mode, command control is not granted; Management has reporting and status checking capabilities only, and Field Maintenance Staff has command control only during maintenance mode. Exit the use case without acquiring command control.

goal.content: The use case accomplishes the issuance of control commands by an Operator to change the state of devices or system operations within the RLCS.

preconditions.content: The Operator must be a valid Personnel entity with an associated Personnel Security Level.
The Operator's Personnel Security Level must define the authorized Command Level (Status Only, Control, or Override).
The Operator must have access to a Workstation associated with their Personnel record.
The target Device or System Operation must exist in the database and have a defined status.

trigger.content: The Operator initiates a request to issue a Device control, Device Macro, Super Macro, or Override command to change the state of a device or system operation.

main_flow.content: The Operator selects the type of command to issue: Device control, Device Macro, Super Macro, or Override.
If issuing a Device control command, the Operator specifies the single command to change the state of a device.
If issuing a Device Macro Command, the system executes a group of two or more sequentially executed commands that change the states of two or more closure devices.
If issuing a Super Macro Command, the system executes a group of two or more sequentially executed macros that change the states of an Entrance.
If issuing an Override Command, the system forces the status of a device to a temporary known state for the purpose of completing an operation which otherwise would be blocked.
The RLCS application software updates and reads database tables to support the system operations associated with the command.
The system logs the command execution in the appropriate log entity (Device Command Log or System Operation Command Log).

exception_flow.content: If the Operator's Personnel Security Level does not permit the requested Command Level (e.g., 'Status Only' user attempts a control command), the system denies the command issuance.
If the target Device is in a prohibited status as defined by Device Rules, the system prevents the execution of the command sequence.

If an Override Command is issued but the configurable period for the temporary status change expires before the operation completes, the system reverts the device status and halts the dependent command sequence.

postconditions.content: The state of the targeted Device(s) or System Operation has been changed according to the issued command.
A new entry is created in the Device Command Log entity recording the Device Command ID, Date, Time, Device Status ID, and Operator ID.

If a System Operational Command was executed, a new entry is created in the System Operation Command Log entity recording the System Operation Command Log ID, Date, Time, System Operational Command ID, System Operation Status ID, and Operator ID.
The Operator's Personnel record is referenced in the newly created log entry (Device Command Log or System Operation Command Log).
If an Override Command was issued, the status of the device in the database is temporarily changed for a configurable period of time to allow the command sequence to continue.

goal.content: The Operator wants to open a reversible-lane entrance for one direction of travel by executing the specified opening sequence that commands the entrance's closure devices (such as Barrier Gates, Pop-ups, and CMS) to transition from their closed state to their open state.

preconditions.content: The system is in normal operational mode, and the Operator is logged on.
For the entrance being opened, no opposite-direction entrance closure device has a status of 'unknown' or 'open'.
For Sequence #1 (AM Opening South Bound) and Sequence #3 (PM Opening North Bound), Gate 5 at Loc. 5 is OPEN before the sequence begins.

Each opening sequence begins with a Step 0 'Status check by Operator' on all devices at all locations as a readiness verification before proceeding; the opening sequence commands entrance closure devices (such as Barrier Gates, Pop-ups, and CMS) to transition from closed to open. For Sequence #1 and Sequence #3, a sequence-specific initial state requires Gate 5 at Loc. 5 to be OPEN before the sequence begins.

trigger.content: The Operator executes the specified opening sequence for the reversible-lane entrance (e.g., Sequence #1 AM Opening South Bound or Sequence #3 PM Opening North Bound).

main_flow.content: Operator initiates the specified opening sequence for the reversible-lane entrance for one direction of travel (e.g., Sequence #1 AM Opening South Bound or Sequence #3 PM Opening North Bound).
System presents the scheduled command operation to the Operator at the GUI for confirmation prior to executing the command.
Operator confirms the scheduled command operation.
System commands the Barrier Gate to open.
System commands the Wrong Way Transverse Pop-ups to open.
System commands the Wrong Way Longitudinal Pop-ups to open.
System commands the Entrance Transverse Pop-ups to open.
System commands the Entrance Longitudinal Pop-ups to open.
System commands the CMS to display the specific message for the opened direction: I-15 northbound RLCS approach, SR 163 northbound RLCS approach, or I-15 southbound RLCS approach.
The reversible-lane entrance is open for the selected direction of travel, with the entrance's closure devices commanded to their open state.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 1: If multiple entrances exist on the reversible lanes in the direction of travel being opened, the specific order in which those entrances are opened presents no 'wrong way' safety issues.

Diverges from Step 4: For Sequence #3 (PM Opening North Bound), before the Barrier Gate is commanded to open, Gate 5 at Loc. 5 North End 15 is commanded to close; the opening sequence then continues to open the entrance's closure devices.

exception_flow.content: At any point in the opening sequence (Steps 4–9), if a closure device fails to report completion of the current sequence step within the response time window allotted for that step, the opening sequence is halted. The halted opening sequence causes the system to enter a hold state for a system-specified time. If the offending device status can be corrected within the specified time period, the Operator can enter a resume command and the system attempts to complete the original opening sequence.

At any point in the opening sequence (Steps 4–9), if the status of a closure device that was previously closed at the current entrance changes to 'unknown' or 'open' without an Operator-initiated command, the opening sequence is halted. The halted opening sequence causes the system to enter a hold state for a system-specified time. If the offending device status can be corrected within the specified time period, the Operator can enter a resume command and the system attempts to complete the original opening sequence.

At any point in the opening sequence (Steps 4–9), if the status of a closure device for the opposite direction of travel changes to 'unknown' or 'open', the opening sequence is halted. The halted opening sequence causes the system to enter a hold state for a system-specified time. If the offending device status can be corrected within the specified time period, the Operator can enter a resume command and the system attempts to complete the original opening sequence.

At a device-opening command step (Steps 4–9), if unknown or improper closure device status is detected anywhere in the system, the current device opening command is immediately terminated, and the opening sequence is halted. The halted opening sequence causes the system to enter a hold state for a system-specified time. If the offending device status can be corrected within the specified time period, the Operator can enter a resume command and the system attempts to complete the original opening sequence.

At a device-command step (Steps 4–9), if an intermediate step results in a device control failure, an Operator with proper security can use the Device Override capability to input a device status, override the status coming from the field, and continue the operating sequence through to the end.

During the opening operation (Steps 4–9), if a critical alarm occurs, the system presents the Operator with possible actions that can be taken in order to complete the operation. If overriding a device status is needed to proceed, the system determines whether the Operator has sufficient security and provides advice on how to proceed; an Operator with proper security may use Device Override to input the device status and continue the operating sequence through to the end.
At Step 4 and subsequent opening commands, if the system allows or causes an entrance to be opened in one direction when an entrance in the opposite direction is already open, the system has failed.

postconditions.content: The reversible-lane entrance is open for one direction of travel.

The entrance's closure devices—Barrier Gate, Wrong Way Transverse Pop-ups, Wrong Way Longitudinal Pop-ups, Entrance Transverse Pop-ups, Entrance Longitudinal Pop-ups, and CMS—are commanded to transition from their closed state to their open state in the specified sequence.

main_flow.content: Open Wrong Way Transverse Pop-ups; if more than one bank, open the banks in the direction from the freeway toward the reversible lanes.
Open Wrong Way Longitudinal Pop-ups; open pop-up banks beginning at the entrance ramp nose at the reversible lanes, and proceeding toward the edge of shoulder.
Open Entrance Transverse Pop-ups; if more than one bank, open the banks in the direction from the reversible lanes toward the freeway.
Open Entrance Longitudinal Pop-ups; open pop-up banks downstream (entrance ramp nose at the freeway) to upstream (edge of shoulder).

If the TMC workstations or network server fails, resulting in loss of field status at the TMC, alternate control shall be at FCU South or FCU North; the Operator shall be able to dial in from a back up computer to either FCU North or FCU South and open and close the reversible lanes. Exit: alternate control at FCU South or FCU North.

If FCU North or South fails (FCU Controller failures or FCU-TSU communications failure), loss of changeable messages signs and DCUs associated with the failed FCU occurs; alternate control is at the non-failed FCU (North or South). Exit: alternate control at the non-failed FCU.

If FCUs North and South both fail (FCU Controller failures or FCUs-TSU and FCU-FCU communications failure), loss of changeable message signs 1-12 and DCUs 1-5 occurs; alternate control units are direct control at DCUs 1-5. Exit: direct control at DCUs 1-5.

goal.content: Authorize a System Administrator to create and modify system configuration data, including staff, devices, and scheduled operations.

preconditions.content: The user is logged on to the RLCS Application as a System Administrator.
The System Administrator has been assigned a security level and password.

trigger.content: The System Administrator initiates the configuration of staff access permissions by selecting the option to assign or modify security levels and passwords for defined staff members via the GUI.

main_flow.content: The System Administrator selects the configuration option to assign or modify security levels and passwords for defined staff members.
The GUI displays the list of defined staff members and allows the administrator to select a specific staff member for modification.
The System Administrator assigns or modifies the security level for the selected staff member at the command level, device, mode, workstation, and system function as needed.
If changing user account details remotely in field units, the System Administrator initiates the remote change via the configuration option.
When making changes that affect devices, controllers, or workstations in the RLCS network, the GUI displays to the user which components will be affected by the changes.
The System Administrator confirms the changes, and the system updates the database tables accordingly.
Before storing modified data in the database, the GUI analyzes the data for any conflicting or redundant entries and notifies the System Administrator if such entries are found.
Upon successful validation and storage, the system confirms the update to the System Administrator.

exception_flow.content: If the GUI detects conflicting or redundant entries when analyzing modified database table data before storage, it notifies the System Administrator and halts the update until resolved.
If the System Administrator attempts to configure device rules without providing the additional required login password for that option, the system denies access to that configuration function.

postconditions.content: A security level and password have been assigned to the defined staff member.
User security levels have been assigned at the command level, device, mode, workstation, and system function as configured by the System Administrator.
If applicable, user accounts have been changed remotely in the field units.
The database tables have been updated with the new or modified staff access permissions after analysis for conflicting or redundant entries.

goal.content: The User wants to create a new compressed archive from one or more files or archives via the Create Archive Interface, using a supported archive/compression format.

preconditions.content: The application is running and the user has access to the file manager interface, create archive interface, or extraction interface.

trigger.content: The User initiates the use case by interacting with the Create Archive Interface. One method to access this interface is by pressing the 'File' button in the file manager interface and selecting 'Create archive' from the submenu that appears.

main_flow.content: The User uses the Create Archive Interface's file browser to select one or more files or archives as the source objects to be compressed.
The User specifies the output location and name for the new compressed archive (e.g., '.zip').
The User selects the desired archive format (e.g., 'ZIP') from the supported formats and the volume mode (e.g., 'Single volume') in the Format options.
The User confirms the operation by clicking the 'Ok' button at the bottom of the Create Archive Interface.
The new compressed archive is created from the selected file(s) or archive(s) in the selected supported archive/compression format.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 1: Instead of using the Create Archive Interface's file browser to select source objects, the User may select one or more objects in the file manager interface and press the 'Add' button on the toolbar or choose 'Add' from the context submenu, or select objects outside the application's graphical environment and choose 'Add to separate archives' from the 'Send to' menu, to open the Create Archive Interface with those objects.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of using the Create Archive Interface's file browser to select source objects, the User can initiate archive creation by dragging and dropping files onto the application interface.

Diverges from Step 2: Instead of specifying a fixed output name, the User may append a timestamp with date and time to the archive name for archiving and backup purposes, which alters the output filename but still allows successful archive creation.
Diverges from Step 3: Instead of selecting a single-volume mode, the User may choose to create multi-volume (split) archives.
Diverges from Step 3: Instead of combining all selected objects into one archive, the User may select 'Add each object to a separate archive', resulting in multiple archives being created.
Diverges from Step 3: The User may optionally set a password for the archive; if no password is set, the interface displays 'Password is not set' with a lock icon.
Diverges from Step 3: The User may enable two-factor authentication using both a password and a keyfile for the managed files and archives during archive creation.

exception_flow.content: At Step 1, if the User has included an unwanted object in the archive layout before final confirmation, the User can remove the selected object from the archive layout by pressing Cancel, Ctrl+R, or Ctrl+Backspace; this represents an intermediate recovery action during archive composition.
At Step 3, if the User attempts to compress data into an archive format that is read-only supported, the system prevents the creation of an archive.

At Step 4, when the User confirms archive creation, if the total size of the selected objects exceeds the available free space on the target storage device, the system displays a warning message indicating insufficient disk space and prevents the archive creation.

At Step 4, if the User attempts to create an archive with a name that already exists in the target directory and chooses not to overwrite it, the system displays a message box stating 'File already exists' and terminates the creation process without creating the new archive.
At Step 4, the User can cancel the archive creation operation by pressing Shift+Backspace or clicking the Cancel button; the archive creation operation is canceled.

At Step 4, after the User confirms archive creation, if password or keyfile authentication fails (e.g., incorrect credentials) during archive creation, the Create Archive Interface handles the authentication failure as an exception.

At Step 4, after the User confirms archive creation, if execution errors or status updates occur during archive creation, the Create Archive Interface visually reports the execution state through the graphic display of currently executed functions.

postconditions.content: After successful completion, a new compressed archive file exists at the user-specified output location and name (e.g., '.zip'), containing the selected source object(s) in the chosen supported archive/compression format (e.g., 'ZIP').
If the User enabled timestamp appending during creation, the resulting archive filename includes the appended timestamp.
If the User chose to split the archive into volumes, multiple volume files exist as part of the final archive state.
If encryption settings were used during creation, the resulting archive is locked via password and, optionally, a keyfile.

use_case_name: Add Files to an Existing Archive

goal.content: To add files or folders to an existing archive using the Create Archive Interface.

preconditions.content: The user is logged into the computer system and has access to the PeaZip application.
An existing archive file must be present on the local disk or accessible drive (e.g., C:, D:, E:) that can be selected for modification.
The user must have navigated to or opened the 'Create Archive Interface' where archiving options and target files are managed.

trigger.content: The user selects the 'Add' button or menu option from the File Manager Interface to initiate the process of adding files to an existing archive.

main_flow.content: The user selects the 'Add' button from the File Manager Interface toolbar.
The system opens the 'Create .zip, new archive' interface (Create Archive Interface).
The user specifies the output file path and name in the 'Output' field of the Create Archive Interface.
The user configures the desired 'Format options', such as selecting the archive format (e.g., ZIP) and volume settings.
The user reviews the list of files and folders to be added in the 'Archiving' section of the interface.
The user clicks the 'Ok' button to confirm the settings and initiate the archiving process.
The system displays a progress window (PeaLauncher) showing the status of the job, including input/output sizes and time elapsed.
Upon successful completion, the system displays a 'Job successfully completed' message in the progress window.

alternative_flow.content: The user may choose to encrypt the archive by setting a password and/or keyfile before finalizing the operation.
The user can split the selected objects' data content into more than one archive volume, defining the size of each volume manually.
The user may opt to append a timestamp to the created archive's name for archiving and backup purposes.
If a homonym file or archive already exists in the selected storage space, the user must define what action should be taken (e.g., overwrite, rename).

exception_flow.content: If the user attempts to add files but a homonym file or archive already exists in the selected storage space, the system requires the user to define an action (e.g., overwrite, rename) before proceeding.

If the user selects encryption options (password/keyfile) but fails to set them correctly or encounters an error during the locking process, the system may prevent the archive from being created until the issue is resolved.

If the PeaLauncher backend binary encounters an error during the job execution (e.g., insufficient disk space, permission denied), it will remain open displaying the error message instead of closing automatically upon completion.

postconditions.content: The selected files and folders have been successfully added to the specified archive file.
The system displays a 'Job successfully completed' message in the PeaLauncher progress window.
The progress window shows the final input size, output size (with compression percentage), and total time elapsed for the operation.

goal.content: Allow users to add one or more files or archives to an existing archive without destroying original contents, optionally with password/keyfile protection.

The Business Owner uses the report to determine whether the customer base is spending more or less and purchasing more or less often.

At step 4, if Frequency is 0, the report identifies the accounts as non-purchasing or inactive accounts.

goal.content: Enable the Auctioneer to analyze auction-available inventory by category, cost, units, and unique SKUs, including aging and performance metrics, to support decisions on inventory management and auction scheduling.

preconditions.content: The Auctioneer must have access to the Inventory Performance & Aging Report system.
The report criteria section must be available, including a 'search for auction items' search box with wildcard capability.
Radio button options must be available to choose between 'Items currently online only' and 'All sellable auction inventory'.
Radio buttons must be enabled for choosing 'Showing items with or without images' and 'Showing items with or without a valid (sellable) location.'
A Group By scrolling list box must be available with grouping options such as Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material, etc.

trigger.content: The Auctioneer opens the Inventory Performance & Aging Report from the Auction Admin Main Menu to analyze available auction inventory by category, cost, units, and unique SKUs.

main_flow.content: The Auctioneer selects the 'Inventory Performance & Aging Report' option from the Reports Menu on the Auction Administration Main Menu page.
The system displays the Inventory Performance & Aging Report interface with the criteria section, including search options and grouping controls.
The Auctioneer uses the 'search for auction items' search box to enter keywords or wildcards (% or *) to filter inventory items.
The Auctioneer selects radio button options to choose between 'Items currently online only' or 'All sellable auction inventory'.
The Auctioneer enables radio buttons to specify whether to show items with or without images and with or without a valid (sellable) location.
The Auctioneer selects one or more grouping options from the Group By scrolling list box (e.g., Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material Purity, Brand, etc.).

The system generates and displays the report results based on user-selected criteria and grouping, showing columns such as Product ID, Active Date, Last Shown Date, Qty on Open Purchase Order, Last Receipt Date, Buyer Name, Item Description, Retail Category, Gemstone, Product Type, Brand, J/G Score, GM/TE, Cost, Has Image, Location, Available Total Company Inventory On Hand, Auction Available, White Total Qty, White Total Cost, Red Unsellable Total Quantity, and Red Unsellable Total Cost.
The Auctioneer reviews the displayed inventory data, including aging buckets and performance metrics, to assess availability and make management decisions.

alternative_flow.content: If the Auctioneer selects 'Items currently online only', the system filters results to exclude items not part of available auction inventory, impacting the 'Red status' columns accordingly.
If the Auctioneer enables 'Showing items with or without images', the system includes or excludes items based on image availability in the JTV SuperNova system.
If the Auctioneer enables 'Showing items with or without a valid (sellable) location', the system includes or excludes items lacking a physical inventory location marked as sellable realm ('white').
If no grouping option is selected from the Group By list box, the system displays ungrouped results sorted by default criteria (e.g., Product ID or Active Date).
If the search box input contains invalid wildcard syntax, the system displays an error message and prompts the user to correct the search term before regenerating results.

exception_flow.content: If the search for auction items input contains invalid wildcard syntax (e.g., malformed % or *), the system displays an error message and halts report generation until corrected.
If no valid grouping option is selected from the Group By scrolling list box, the system defaults to ungrouped display but may issue a warning if user intended grouped analysis.

If filtering criteria result in zero matching items (e.g., ‘Items currently online only’ with no active listings), the system displays an empty results table with summary section showing all totals as zero.
If an item lacks a required field such as Product ID, Active Date, or Cost, the system excludes it from results and logs a data integrity exception for administrative review.

If ‘Red Unsellable Total Quantity’ or ‘Red Unsellable Total Cost’ exceeds threshold values defined by business rules (not specified in doc), the system flags the report with a red status banner indicating potential inventory risk.

postconditions.content: The system has generated and displayed a report containing inventory data filtered by the Auctioneer's selected criteria (e.g., 'Items currently online only' or 'All sellable auction inventory', image availability, location validity).

The report results are grouped according to the Auctioneer's selection from the Group By scrolling list box (options include Retail Category, Product Type, Gemstone, Material, Brand, Inventory Realm, etc.).

The 'Results' section displays columns including Product ID, Active Date, Last Shown Date, Qty on Open Purchase Order (P.O.), Last Receipt Date, Buyer Name, Item Description, Retail Category, Gemstone, Product Type, Brand, J/G Score, GM/FTE, Cost, Has Image (Yes or No), Location, Available (Total Company Inventory On Hand), and Auction Available.
The report includes summary metrics for White Total Qty, White Total Cost, Red Unsellable Total Quantity, and Red Unsellable Total Cost.
The report provides visibility into currently available auction inventory as well as product that is NOT part of available auction inventory.

goal.content: The Auctioneer wants to configure the sitewide auction rules that govern defaults and settings for reserve tiers and bid increments, overtime bidding, shipping charges and promotions, preview periods, and post-close removals visibility.

preconditions.content: The Auctioneer is logged into the system as an Auctioneer and can access the Auction Administration workspace.

trigger.content: The Auctioneer accesses the 'Manage Global Settings' page via the 'Administration Menu' link on the 'Auction Admin Main Menu Page'.

main_flow.content: On the Manage Global Settings Page, the Auctioneer configures Reserve Tier and Bid Increment Sitewide Default Settings by entering values for cost tiers, selecting opening bid options (Amount or % of Cost), and entering discrete full dollar amounts for bid increments.
As the Auctioneer enters cost tier values, the system automatically populates the low end of the next cost tier as the high end of the previous range plus $0.01.
The Auctioneer clicks Apply Changes to save the Reserve Tier and Bid Increment settings.
The Auctioneer configures Overtime Bidding by toggling the radio button to On or Off, entering a time extension duration between 10 seconds and 60 minutes, and clicking Apply Changes.

The Auctioneer configures Shipping Settings by entering values for sitewide first item shipping charge, sitewide subsequent items shipping charge, Preferred Customer revenue threshold, and New Per-Item Shipping Charge, then clicking Apply Changes.

The Auctioneer sets a temporary shipping promotion by entering starting and ending dates/times and a promotional shipping charge; the system validates that the dates are in the future, the end date is after the start date, and the promotion lasts no more than seven days; then the Auctioneer clicks Apply Changes.
The Auctioneer sets the Preview Period by entering hours and minutes, up to a maximum of 24 hours, and clicking Apply Changes.
The Auctioneer sets Post-Close Removals visibility duration by entering Hours and Minutes for how long closed auctions remain visible in browse results, then clicking Apply Changes.
The Auctioneer has applied changes for the Reserve Tier and Bid Increment, Overtime Bidding, Shipping, Preview Period, and Post-Close Removals settings.

exception_flow.content: Exception branch 6a (divergence at main-flow step 6): If the Auctioneer sets a temporary shipping promotion with dates that are not in the future, or with an ending date that is not after the start date, validation fails and the system prevents the promotion from being set.

Exception branch 6b (divergence at main-flow step 6): If the Auctioneer attempts to configure a temporary shipping promotion that lasts for more than seven days, validation fails and the system prevents the promotion from being set.

Exception branch 1a (divergence at main-flow step 1): If the Auctioneer enters a '% of Cost' value under 100% for an opening bid reserve tier, the system displays the value in BOLD RED as a warning but does not prevent the Auctioneer from proceeding with the configuration. Exit: the Auctioneer may continue configuring with the warning displayed.

postconditions.content: The configured global auction rules are saved and applied immediately as the new sitewide defaults across the supported settings sections: Reserve Tier and Bid Increment, Overtime Bidding, Shipping, Preview Period, and Post-Close Removals.

The configured reserve cost tiers, with their corresponding reserve (opening bid) amounts and discrete full dollar bid increments, are saved and active as sitewide defaults for all items in those tiers unless overridden by Event Profiles.

The configured sitewide first-item shipping charge, subsequent-items shipping charge, Preferred Customer revenue threshold, and New Per-Item Shipping Charge are persisted and active for future transactions.

The configured Post-Close Removals visibility rule is active: closed auctions are removed immediately from the site's category pages after closing and appear on the Recently-ended page for a fixed period of 24 hours.

goal.content: The Auctioneer wants to configure the sitewide auction rules that govern defaults and settings for reserve tiers and bid increments, overtime bidding, shipping charges and promotions, preview periods, and post-close removals visibility.

preconditions.content: The Auctioneer is logged into the system as an Auctioneer and can access the Auction Administration workspace.

trigger.content: The Auctioneer accesses the 'Manage Global Settings' page via the 'Administration Menu' link on the 'Auction Admin Main Menu Page'.

main_flow.content: On the Manage Global Settings Page, the Auctioneer configures Reserve Tier and Bid Increment Sitewide Default Settings by entering values for cost tiers, selecting opening bid options (Amount or % of Cost), and entering discrete full dollar amounts for bid increments.
As the Auctioneer enters cost tier values, the system automatically populates the low end of the next cost tier as the high end of the previous range plus $0.01.
The Auctioneer clicks Apply Changes to save the Reserve Tier and Bid Increment settings.
The Auctioneer configures Overtime Bidding by toggling the radio button to On or Off, entering a time extension duration between 10 seconds and 60 minutes, and clicking Apply Changes.

The Auctioneer configures Shipping Settings by entering values for sitewide first item shipping charge, sitewide subsequent items shipping charge, Preferred Customer revenue threshold, and New Per-Item Shipping Charge, then clicking Apply Changes.

The Auctioneer sets a temporary shipping promotion by entering starting and ending dates/times and a promotional shipping charge; the system validates that the dates are in the future, the end date is after the start date, and the promotion lasts no more than seven days; then the Auctioneer clicks Apply Changes.
The Auctioneer sets the Preview Period by entering hours and minutes, up to a maximum of 24 hours, and clicking Apply Changes.
The Auctioneer sets Post-Close Removals visibility duration by entering Hours and Minutes for how long closed auctions remain visible in browse results, then clicking Apply Changes.
The Auctioneer has applied changes for the Reserve Tier and Bid Increment, Overtime Bidding, Shipping, Preview Period, and Post-Close Removals settings.

exception_flow.content: Exception branch 6a (divergence at main-flow step 6): If the Auctioneer sets a temporary shipping promotion with dates that are not in the future, or with an ending date that is not after the start date, validation fails and the system prevents the promotion from being set.

Exception branch 6b (divergence at main-flow step 6): If the Auctioneer attempts to configure a temporary shipping promotion that lasts for more than seven days, validation fails and the system prevents the promotion from being set.

Exception branch 1a (divergence at main-flow step 1): If the Auctioneer enters a '% of Cost' value under 100% for an opening bid reserve tier, the system displays the value in BOLD RED as a warning but does not prevent the Auctioneer from proceeding with the configuration. Exit: the Auctioneer may continue configuring with the warning displayed.

postconditions.content: The configured global auction rules are saved and applied immediately as the new sitewide defaults across the supported settings sections: Reserve Tier and Bid Increment, Overtime Bidding, Shipping, Preview Period, and Post-Close Removals.

The configured reserve cost tiers, with their corresponding reserve (opening bid) amounts and discrete full dollar bid increments, are saved and active as sitewide defaults for all items in those tiers unless overridden by Event Profiles.

The configured sitewide first-item shipping charge, subsequent-items shipping charge, Preferred Customer revenue threshold, and New Per-Item Shipping Charge are persisted and active for future transactions.

The configured Post-Close Removals visibility rule is active: closed auctions are removed immediately from the site's category pages after closing and appear on the Recently-ended page for a fixed period of 24 hours.

goal.content: To investigate customer auction inquiries by handling customer complaints and concerns and researching bidding issues.

preconditions.content: The Customer Service Representative is logged into the Auction Administration workspace.

trigger.content: A customer auction inquiry requires investigation by the Customer Service Representative, who initiates the investigation by entering a customer's email address, phone number, or name, or a Product ID, into the search fields and clicking 'Go'.

main_flow.content: After the Customer Service Representative initiates the search, the system displays a Results section containing customer details (Last Name, First Name, City, State, Zip, Phone, E-mail) and action buttons for 'Bid History', 'Order History', 'View Notes', and 'Reset Password'.
The Customer Service Representative selects the 'Bid History' button; the system automatically scrolls to the corresponding detailed Bid History section further down the page.

The system displays the Bid History section with the item's closing date/time (or 'Active'), auction sequence numbers, product ID (SKU), the customer's last bid, SmartBid (max bid), and the winning bid.
The Customer Service Representative researches the bidding issue by reviewing the displayed Bid History data.
The Customer Service Representative handles the customer's complaint or concern by accessing and editing customer information.
The Customer Service Representative enters account notes.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from main flow step 2: Instead of selecting 'Bid History', the Customer Service Representative selects 'Order History' from the Results section; the system then displays a list of orders including dates, sequence numbers, item numbers, amounts, and status (e.g., 'Complete' or 'Order Cancelled'), allowing the CSR to investigate the order-related inquiry.

Diverges from main flow step 5: If the investigation reveals fraudulent or other undesirable activity, or at the customer's request, the Customer Service Representative can place the auction customer in 'Review' status; however, a permanent suspension of bidding rights ('Deactivate an Account') requires approval by a Customer Care manager via code.

Diverges from main flow step 5: If the customer's inquiry concerns an account in Review Status, the Customer Service Representative removes the account from Review Status only after the customer updates the account with a credit card; the customer may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until the order cancel rate falls below 10%.

Diverges from main flow step 5: If the customer's inquiry concerns an account that has been locked because of cancelled orders, the Customer Service Representative can unlock the account if the customer has not failed to pay up to three times, and then reminds the customer that winning incurs an obligation to pay.

exception_flow.content: Diverges from main_flow step 4 when the Customer Service Representative's research reveals that the customer has unresolved auction winnings older than 7 days. The system has automatically locked the account and placed it in Review Status, preventing the customer from bidding; the customer cannot unlock the account themselves because orders are cancelled after 168 hours. Exit: the account remains blocked until a Customer Service Representative removes Review Status.

Diverges from main_flow step 4 when the Customer Service Representative's research reveals that a PayPal or Amazon Payments customer allowed their order(s) to expire. The system has automatically locked the account and placed it in Review Status. Exit: the account remains in Review Status until a Customer Service Representative removes it, as Review Status accounts can only be unlocked by a Customer Service Representative.

Diverges from main_flow step 4 when the Customer Service Representative's research reveals that the customer is subject to the escalation policy (failing to pay more than three times in 12 months unless less than 10% of total). The customer cannot bid again until a Customer Service Representative removes the account from Review Status; removal requires updating the account with a credit card. Exit: the account remains unable to bid until a Customer Service Representative removes Review Status after the required credit-card update.

Diverges from main_flow step 5 when the Customer Service Representative attempts to deactivate an account without a valid supervisor's authorization code entered via the pop-up DIV layer. The system prevents the deactivation from proceeding. Exit: the deactivation is blocked pending a valid supervisor's authorization code.

postconditions.content: The customer's complaint or concern has been handled and the relevant bidding issue has been researched.
The customer record has been updated with the specific notes entered by the Customer Service Representative.

If the Customer Service Representative removed the customer's account from Review Status during the investigation (either by unlocking a locked account or by updating the account with a credit card for escalation policy removal), the customer is able to bid again.

goal.content: To enable a Customer Service Representative to resolve customer inquiries by investigating customer complaints/concerns and bidding issues using customer information and history.

preconditions.content: The Customer Service Representative has access to the Customer History Page.
The Customer Service Representative can access and edit customer information and research bidding issues.

trigger.content: A customer inquiry is received by Customer Service for resolution.

main_flow.content: The Customer Service Representative selects Customer History from the Administration Menu.
The Customer Service Representative uses the Customer History Page to aid in troubleshooting customer service issues.
The Customer Service Representative searches on customer e-mail address, phone number, or customer name.
The “Results:” section includes Last Name, First Name, City, ST, Zip, Phone, E-mail address.

alternative_flow.content: If the Customer Service Representative uses the Bid History, Order History, or View Notes buttons on the Customer History Page, those buttons utilize anchor tags to take the user to the correct section further down the page.
The Customer Service Representative can use the Reset Password button on the Customer History Page.
If the Customer Service Representative chooses to suspend or deactivate an account, the Customer History Page allows accounts to be suspended or deactivated.
If the Customer Service Representative is deactivating an account, a supervisor's authorization code is required, and a pop-up DIV layer will appear asking for a supervisor's code.
If an auction participant becomes subject to the escalation policy for Review Status accounts, they cannot bid again until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status.

For a customer subject to the escalation policy for Review Status accounts, the only way for the customer to have their account removed from Review Status is by updating their account with a credit card; they may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until their order cancel rate falls below 10%.

If Amazon Payments and PayPal customers have a history of non-payment (whose auction orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days), they will be subjected to an escalation process; when these customers contact the call center, they will simply be reminded that winning incurs an obligation to pay.
If the account is deactivated, it will be listed in RED.
If the Method of Payment is credit card, the Method of Payment section (MOP) will only display the card type, expiration date, and last four digits.

exception_flow.content: 1. If a customer inquiry requires the Customer Service Representative to place a bid for the customer, the Customer Service Representative can NOT place bids for customers. Exit: the bid is not placed by the Customer Service Representative.

2. If the Customer Service Representative chooses to deactivate an account, deactivating accounts will require a supervisor's authorization code, and a pop-up DIV layer will appear asking for a supervisor's code; a Customer Care manager will be required to approve, via code, a permanent suspension of bidding rights (“Deactivate an Account”). Exit: the deactivation is not authorized without the required supervisor/manager authorization code.

3. If an auction participant becomes subject to the escalation policy, they cannot bid again until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status; the only way for a customer to have their account removed from Review Status is by updating their account with a credit card, and they may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until their order cancel rate falls below 10%. Exit: the account remains in Review Status and cannot bid until the credit card update is completed and the order cancel rate condition is met.

4. If Amazon Payments and PayPal customers have a history of non-payment (whose auction orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days), they will be subjected to an escalation process; when these customers contact the call center, they will simply be reminded that winning incurs an obligation to pay. Exit: the customer is reminded that winning incurs an obligation to pay and remains subject to the escalation process.

postconditions.content: The Customer Service Representative has handled customer complaints / concerns and researched bidding issues.
The Customer History Page has been used by the Customer Service Representative to aid in troubleshooting customer service issues.
Customer search results have been displayed with Last Name, First Name, City, ST, Zip, Phone, and E-mail address.

If an account was suspended or placed in Review Status, the customer can log in and change account settings, but may not bid, and the system will not generate orders for any auctions-in-progress that the customer may win.
If an account was deactivated, a supervisor's authorization code was required, and a pop-up DIV layer appeared asking for the supervisor's code.

If the account is in Review Status and subject to the escalation policy, the customer cannot bid again until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status; the only way to remove the account from Review Status is by updating the account with a credit card, and PayPal or Amazon Payments may not be used again until the order cancel rate falls below 10%.

goal.content: To investigate and resolve customer inquiries regarding auction bids, orders, and account activity by accessing relevant reports and data.

preconditions.content: The Customer Service Representative must be logged into the Auction Administration system.
The 'Customer Ranking Report' or 'Inventory Performance & Aging Report' mockups must be accessible within the administration interface to view customer data and auction details.

trigger.content: A customer contacts the Customer Service Representative with an inquiry regarding their auction bids, orders, or account activity.

main_flow.content: The Customer Service Representative navigates to the 'Auction Admin Main Menu Page'.
The representative selects the 'Customer Ranking Report' or 'Inventory Performance & Aging Report' from the main menu options.
The system displays the report interface, allowing the representative to filter data by criteria such as 'Order Date', 'Retail Category', 'Prod Type', or 'Gemstone'.
The representative enters specific search parameters related to the customer's inquiry (e.g., Member ID, Email Address, or Auction Item details) and submits the query.

The system generates a detailed view showing relevant metrics such as 'Total Items Bid On', 'Gross Winnings', 'Cancelled Orders', 'Return Rate', and 'Net Kept Units' for the selected customer or inventory items.
The representative reviews the displayed data to identify the status of bids, orders, or inventory aging issues causing the inquiry.
The representative uses the gathered information to address and resolve the customer's inquiry.

alternative_flow.content: If the customer inquiry is related to specific item details or auction creation, the representative may navigate to the 'Create New Auctions Page' instead of a report.

If the initial search in the report yields no results, the representative can adjust the filter criteria, such as changing the 'Order Date', 'Retail Category', or 'Gemstone' selections, and resubmit the query.
If the inquiry requires checking general site navigation or customer-facing page status, the representative may consult the 'Site Diagram' to verify page availability or structure.

exception_flow.content: If the search query returns no results, the system displays a 'No Results Search Page' or an empty data grid, requiring the representative to adjust filters.
If the customer inquiry involves an item that is not available for auction (e.g., missing image or location), the report will flag this status, potentially preventing standard resolution steps.
If the representative attempts to access restricted administrative functions without proper permissions, the system denies access via the 'User Access Mgmt Page' controls.

postconditions.content: The Customer Service Representative has successfully identified the status of the customer's bids, orders, or account activity based on the report data.
The specific metrics related to the inquiry (such as 'Total Items Bid On', 'Gross Winnings', 'Cancelled Orders', or 'Auction Available' status) have been retrieved and reviewed.
The representative possesses the necessary information to address the customer's inquiry regarding auction performance or inventory aging.

trigger.content: A Customer Service Representative needs to troubleshoot a customer service issue regarding an auction.

The representative searches for the customer's account using their email address, phone number, or name.

The representative examines the Order History section to view order dates, auction sequences, item numbers, amounts, and status.
The representative examines the Bid History section to view closing dates, auction sequences, item numbers, last bids, smart bids, and winning bids.

alternative_flow.content: If the Customer Service Representative determines the account needs to be suspended or deactivated, they must obtain a supervisor's authorization code via a pop-up DIV layer to proceed.

If the customer is subject to the escalation policy (more than three unpaid orders in twelve months and >10% cancellation rate), the representative cannot simply unlock the account; the customer must update their account with a credit card to be removed from Review Status.

If a customer's account is in 'Review Status' due to unpaid auction winnings (orders expired after 7 days), the Customer Service Representative may unlock the account only if the customer has not exceeded the limit of three unpaid orders (unless the rate is below 10%).

If the customer is subject to the escalation policy (more than three unpaid orders in twelve months and >10% cancellation rate), the Customer Service Representative cannot simply unlock the account; the exception path requires the customer to update their account with a credit card to be removed from Review Status.

preconditions.content: The user is logged in as “Auctioneer!”

trigger.content: The Auctioneer selects “Edit Auction Event Profiles” from the Administration Menu to manage auction event profiles.

The auction event profile provides a common set of characteristics to a group of product, which makes scheduling groups of product easier and faster, provides consistency, and reduces data entry errors.

main_flow.content: The Auctioneer selects an existing auction event profile from the list or chooses to create a new one.

postconditions.content: The auction event profile is successfully updated in the system with the new configuration settings.

goal.content: To create and edit auction event profiles that provide a common set of characteristics to a group of products, making scheduling groups of product easier and faster, providing consistency, and reducing data entry errors.

preconditions.content: The Auctioneer is logged in and has accessed the Auction Administration page.
The Auctioneer wishes to create a new promotional event or edit an existing profile.

trigger.content: The Auctioneer accesses the Auction Event Profiles Page to create a new promotional event or edit an existing profile.

main_flow.content: The Auctioneer accesses the Auction Event Profiles Page.
To create a new profile, the Auctioneer tabs or clicks into the “Create New Profile” field and enters a new profile name, then clicks on “Create.”

The Auctioneer fills in the 2nd column, which is always the upper range of the cost tier. The system automatically fills in the lower range of the subsequent cost tier by adding $0.01 to the last value entered by the auctioneer, until all fields are completed.
Working horizontally and adjacent to each cost tier, the Auctioneer chooses a radio button for either “amount” or “% of cost”, and fills in the appropriate field.
Any % of cost values under 100% automatically appear in BOLD RED as a warning to the Auctioneer. This does not prevent the Auctioneer from proceeding.
The Auctioneer designates a bid increment for all items in the cost tier.
The Auctioneer designates an auction duration to all items within the cost tier.
The Auctioneer chooses one of the radio buttons at the bottom to specify what products will be eligible to use the profile (e.g., “Apply to Gemstones Only”).
The Auctioneer finishes profile creation by clicking on the “Apply” button.

To edit an existing profile, the Auctioneer accesses the page and chooses the profile she wishes to edit from the list. Once she clicks on the profile name, the previously-entered data is displayed for modification.

use_case_name: Respond to a Second-Chance Purchase Offer

goal.content: The customer wants to respond to a Second-Chance email offer to purchase the item at their last bid price.

preconditions.content: The customer is the second-place finisher in an auction whose winning order was cancelled due to non-payment within 7 days/168 hours, and the item is in hold status.
The customer's last bid price is equal to or greater than the item's unit cost.
The customer does not have two accounts that are essentially bidding against themselves (matches found on Customer Name, Phone Number, Email Address, Member ID, or Billing/Shipping Addresses).

trigger.content: The customer receives a Second-Chance email offer to purchase the item at their last bid price.

main_flow.content: After the customer receives the Second-Chance email offer, the customer responds by navigating to the JTVauctions.com website and accessing their account history page.
The system presents the Returning Winners Payments Page that lists the item(s) won and prompts the customer to complete the transaction by choosing a checkout option.
The system provides the customer with three distinct checkout options: 'Check out with PayPal', 'Check out with Amazon', or 'Checkout Later'.
The customer reviews the list of items won but not yet paid for, which includes Item #, Description, Auction Number, Amount owed, auction ending time, and a 'Pay Now' checkbox.

Within three days from the time the Second-Chance email is sent, the customer chooses a payment type by clicking one of the three logo buttons: PayPal, Amazon Payments, or Checkout Later, to respond to the offer.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 4: instead of selecting PayPal or Amazon Payments to pay immediately, the customer selects the 'Checkout Later' option; the system displays a confirmation message stating the customer has 7 days (168 hours) to pay before the order is cancelled and provides options to 'Return to Payments' or go to the 'JTVauctions Homepage'.

exception_flow.content: At Step 4, if the customer does not respond to the Second-Chance email within 72 hours after it is sent, the item is returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction.

At Step 4, if the customer selects 'Checkout Later' and does not complete payment with Amazon or PayPal before the 7-day (168-hour) payment window expires, the order is cancelled and the item is placed into 'Hold' status.

At Step 4, if the customer fails to complete the transaction/payment, the Non-Payment Procedure and Locked Accounts applies: the system handles non-payment by locking accounts and defines an escalation policy for reviewing locked-account status; users who fail to complete transactions may have their accounts suspended.

postconditions.content: The item is removed from 'hold' status and an order is generated for shipment.
The transaction is completed without requiring any further action from the customer.

Upon completing the Amazon or PayPal checkout process, the user is returned to a Thank You page, which uses the global header and footer, and includes a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.
When an order is won with an alternative payment method (PayPal or Amazon Payments), it is placed in a Hold status until payment is received.
