use_case_name: Respond to a Second-Chance Purchase Offer

goal.content: To offer to sell the item to the 2nd-place finisher at their last bid price and enable them to accept, pay for, or decline the offer within three days from the time the email is sent.

preconditions.content: The Customer is the 2nd-place finisher for the auction, and there is a second-place finisher to receive the 2nd-Chance email.
The original winner’s order was cancelled after non-payment within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time, and the item was placed into a “hold” status.
The 2nd-place finisher’s bid is not below the item’s unit cost.

No matches are found between the 2nd-Chance recipient’s account data and the Winner’s account data on Customer Name, Customer Phone Number, Customer Email Address, Customer Member ID, or Customer Billing and/or Shipping Addresses.

The Customer has received the automated 2nd-Chance email offering to sell the item to the 2nd-place finisher at their last bid price, with three options: Credit Card Option, PayPal or Amazon Payments Option, and Decline Option.
The Customer is responding within 72 hours after the 2nd-Chance email is sent.

trigger.content: The Customer clicks one of the response options in the automated 2nd-Chance email: the "I accept, pay with my On File credit card" button, the "Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments" button, or the "No Thanks" button.

main_flow.content: The Customer clicks the “I accept, pay with my On File credit card” button.
This action triggers an automated process to generate an order and ship the item.
No further action by the customer is needed.

alternative_flow.content: At main flow step 1, if the Customer clicks the “Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments” button: the user will be given three days from the time the email is sent to accept the offer; clicking this button will generate the order and load the Sign-In page; after signing in, the user will be taken to the Returning Winners Payments Page where they can pay for the order.
At main flow step 1, if the Customer clicks the “No Thanks” button (Decline Option), this releases the item from a hold status back into auction available inventory.

At main flow step 1, if the customer does not respond to the 2nd-Chance email within 72 hours after the email is sent, the item will be returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction.

exception_flow.content: Exception path 1: If the customer does not respond to the 2nd-Chance email within 72 hours after the email is sent, the item will be returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction; the use case exits.
Exception path 2: If the 2nd-place finisher’s bid is below the item’s unit cost, the 2nd-Chance email will not be sent; the offer is not made and the use case exits.

Exception path 3: If matches are found between the 2nd-Chance recipient’s account data and the Winner’s account data on any of Customer Name, Customer Phone Number, Customer Email Address, Customer Member ID, or Customer Billing and/or Shipping Addresses, the 2nd-Chance email will not be sent; the offer is not made and the use case exits.

postconditions.content: If the Customer accepted the offer using the “I accept, pay with my On File credit card” button, an automated process generates an order and ships the item, and no further action by the customer is needed.

If the Customer accepted the offer using the “Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments” button, the order is generated; clicking this button loads the Sign-In page, and after signing in the Customer is taken to the Returning Winners Payments Page where they can pay for the order.
If the Customer selected the “No Thanks” button (Decline Option), the item is released from a hold status back into auction available inventory.

use_case_name: Respond to a Second-Chance Purchase Offer

goal.content: To allow the second-place finisher to accept or decline a purchase offer for an item that was previously won but cancelled due to non-payment, thereby enabling faster inventory turnover and improved customer experience.

preconditions.content: An auction has ended and the winning bidder did not pay within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time.
The order for the winning bidder has been cancelled and the item is placed into a 'hold' status.
A second-place finisher exists for the auctioned item.
The second-place finisher’s bid is at or above the item’s unit cost.
An automated email offering the item to the second-place finisher at their last bid price has been triggered and sent.

trigger.content: The customer receives an automated email offering to sell the item at their last bid price after the original winning bidder’s order was cancelled due to non-payment.

main_flow.content: The customer receives an automated email offering to purchase the item at their last bid price, with three response options: Credit Card Option, PayPal or Amazon Payments Option, and Decline Option.
If selecting the Credit Card Option, the customer clicks 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card' button within three days of email receipt.
Clicking the Credit Card Option button triggers an automated process to generate an order and ship the item; no further action by the customer is needed.
If selecting the PayPal or Amazon Payments Option, the customer clicks 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button within three days of email receipt.
Clicking the PayPal or Amazon Payments button generates the order and loads the Sign-In page.
After signing in, the customer is taken to the Returning Winners Payments Page where they can pay for the order.
If selecting the Decline Option, the customer clicks the 'No Thanks' button.
Clicking the 'No Thanks' button releases the item from hold status back into auction available inventory.

alternative_flow.content: If the customer does not respond to the 2nd-Chance email within 72 hours after the email is sent, the item will be returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction.

exception_flow.content: The email will not be sent if the 2nd-place finisher's bid is below the item's unit cost.
2nd-Chance emails will not be sent to recipients who have two accounts and are essentially bidding against themselves.
Before sending the email, the system should compare the 2nd-Chance recipient's account data to the Winner's account data.
The email will not be sent if matches are found on any of: Customer Name, Customer Phone Number, Customer Email Address, Customer Member ID, or Customer Billing and/or Shipping Addresses.

postconditions.content: If the customer accepts via Credit Card Option, an order is generated and the item is shipped; no further action by the customer is needed.
If the customer accepts via PayPal or Amazon Payments Option, the order is generated and the customer pays for it on the Returning Winners Payments Page after signing in.
If the customer declines via the 'No Thanks' button, the item is released from hold status back into auction available inventory.
If the customer does not respond within 72 hours after the email is sent, the item is returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction.

The Auction Admin’s '2nd-Chance Report' is updated to reflect: number of emails sent over the past week, number of acceptances, number of actual payments made, revenue generated from each, total revenue, total COGS, and gross margin percentage.

goal.content: To unlock a customer's "Review Status" account so that the customer can bid again after nonpayment.

preconditions.content: The customer's account is in "Review Status" because the system automatically locked it after a PayPal or Amazon Payments customer allowed their order(s) to expire.
The customer's order(s) were automatically cancelled after 7 days (168 hours).
The customer has had orders cancelled and has not paid up to three times.
The customer has contacted the call center.
If the customer is subject to the escalation policy, the customer has updated their account with a credit card.

trigger.content: A customer whose account is in Review Status contacts the call center after nonpayment.

main_flow.content: The Customer Service Representative accesses the Customer History page to troubleshoot the customer's account issue.
The Customer Service Representative searches for the customer by customer e-mail address, phone number, or customer name.
The Customer Service Representative reviews the customer's Order History and Account Notes.

The Customer Service Representative identifies that the account is in "Review Status" because the system automatically locked it when the PayPal or Amazon Payments customer allowed their order(s) to expire.
The Customer Service Representative verifies that the customer has had orders cancelled and has not paid up to three times.
If the customer is subject to the escalation policy, the Customer Service Representative confirms that the customer has updated their account with a credit card.
The Customer Service Representative unlocks the "Review Status" account to restore the customer's bidding privileges.

alternative_flow.content: When an auction participant becomes subject to the escalation policy, they cannot bid again until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status; the only way for a customer to have their account removed from Review Status is by updating their account with a credit card.
They may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until their order cancel rate falls below 10%.

Customers cannot unlock the account themselves by paying for the orders, because the orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days (168 hours), so that this product may be returned to the inventory pool and re-auctioned.

Customer Care reps should be able to place auction customers in a “Review” status at the customer’s request or upon evidence of fraudulent or other undesirable activity; a Customer Care manager will be required to approve, via code, a permanent suspension of bidding rights (“Deactivate an Account”).
Deactivating accounts will require a supervisor's authorization code; a pop-up DIV layer will appear, asking for a supervisor's code.

exception_flow.content: If the customer is subject to the escalation policy and has not updated their account with a credit card, the account cannot be removed from Review Status and bidding privileges cannot be restored; exit: the account remains in Review Status and the customer cannot bid again until the account is updated with a credit card.

If the customer subject to the escalation policy attempts to continue using PayPal or Amazon Payments, they may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until their order cancel rate falls below 10%; exit: the customer must use a credit card, and the account remains subject to the escalation policy until the cancel rate condition is met.

If the customer attempts to unlock the account themselves by paying for the orders, the account cannot be unlocked that way because the orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days (168 hours) so the product may be returned to the inventory pool and re-auctioned; exit: the customer remains in Review Status unless a Customer Service Representative unlocks the account.

If evidence of fraudulent or other undesirable activity requires permanent suspension of bidding rights (“Deactivate an Account”), a Customer Care manager must approve via code; exit: permanent suspension/deactivation is not completed without the required manager approval.

The customer is allowed to bid again.

goal.content: The Auctioneer wants to review the auction performance and history of a specific SKU, including scheduled sales, churn rate, and past bid results.

preconditions.content: The Auctioneer is logged into the Auction Administration Application and is operating within the Auction Administration workspace.

trigger.content: The Auctioneer opens the Auction Admin Main Menu page to initiate reviewing SKU auction performance.

main_flow.content: The Auctioneer opens the Auction Admin Main Menu page to access system functions.
From the Auction Administration Main Menu, the Auctioneer selects 'SKU History' via the 'GO' button under the Administration Menu.
The Auctioneer enters the Product ID and clicks on 'Go.'

The system displays the search results in two sections: a Top Section showing product details (ID, description, type, cost, price, image, auction history summary, quantities) and a Bottom Section displaying detailed auction history data on separate lines.

The system displays a list of performance metrics for the reviewed SKU, including Gross Product Sales, Total Product cost, Product Gross Margin (with negative values in red), Average Price Point, Total Auctions Scheduled, Churn Rate (calculated as auctions scheduled minus auctions won, divided by auctions scheduled), Unique SKUs, Unique Winners, Total # of Bidders, Total Bids on All Won, Average Bids per Auction Won, Gross Sales per Unique Customer, Cancelled Orders, New Registrations, and New Customers.
The Auctioneer reviews the selected SKU's auction history and performance metrics, including scheduled sales, churn rate, and bid-related results.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 1: instead of opening the Auction Admin Main Menu, the Auctioneer may already be engaged in a related workflow such as Customer History Page or View/Edit Scheduled Auctions and pivot directly to SKU review without returning to the main menu.

Diverges from Step 4: from the Bottom Section auction history list, the Auctioneer may click the Winner / High Bidder link to view that customer's individual history page, providing a drill-down into specific bidder details while reviewing the SKU's past bid results.

Diverges from Step 4: while the search results are displayed, the Auctioneer can rearrange item attribute columns from their default settings, customizing the view without changing the SKU auction performance review outcome.

goal.content: To suspend a customer account (placing it in 'Review' status) or deactivate a customer account.

preconditions.content: The Customer Service Representative is logged into the Auction Administration workspace and has accessed the Customer History page.
The Customer Service Representative has identified the target customer account by searching using the customer's email address, phone number, or name.
The Customer Service Representative has Administrator-level access required to be granted permission to place a customer account in Review status or deactivate it.

trigger.content: After identifying the customer account, the Customer Service Representative initiates the use case by clicking 'Place Account in Review Status' or 'Deactivate an Account' on the Customer History page.

main_flow.content: The Customer Service Representative selects the suspension option by clicking the 'GO' button next to 'Place Account in Review Status' in the Results section of the Customer History page.

postconditions.content: The selected customer account is placed in 'Review' status (suspended); the customer can still log in and change settings but cannot bid or generate orders.

use_case_name: Associate Related Surveillance Tracks and Points

goal.content: To associate related surveillance tracks and points by indicating an association between a track/point and another track/point, such as associating a reported Subsurface surveillance fix or other ASW point with an existing track.

preconditions.content: A track/point and another track/point to be related through an association are present. For the Subsurface surveillance/ASW variant, this is a reported Subsurface surveillance fix or other ASW point and an existing track, and further refined information concerning that point has become available.
No interface track-to-point or point-to-point correlation is available, and the J7.2 message is not used to correlate one track/point with any other point.

trigger.content: The use case is triggered when C2 JU is handling a track/point and another track/point that are to be related through an association, or when further refined information becomes available concerning a reported Subsurface surveillance fix or other ASW point.

main_flow.content: C2 JU sends a J7.7 message with ACT = 0 (Associate Data message) to indicate an association between a track/point and another track/point; for Subsurface surveillance data, the C2 JU operator performs this association manually because automated correlation procedures for Air, Surface, or Land tracks are not applied to Subsurface tracks.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 1: when C2 JU receives a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 and none of the following restrictions apply (tracks are of different E/C or have existing E/C conflict; one track simulated and other live; both tracks locally derived real-time tracks), C2 JU shall automatically accept the requested correlation.

exception_flow.content: If the two tracks to be manually associated are of a different E/C, manual correlation shall not be performed.
If one track is simulated and the other is live, manual correlation shall not be performed.
If both tracks are remote, manual correlation shall not be performed.

postconditions.content: The association between a track/point and another track/point is indicated by the use of the J7.7 message.

use_case_name: Associate Related Surveillance Tracks and Points

goal.content: To enable the C2 JU to manually correlate subsurface surveillance data and associate related tracks or points by using the J7.7 Track Association message when two Track Numbers (TNs) are determined to report information for the same target.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU has identified two tracks that are eligible for correlation, meaning they may represent the same object and require resolution of dual designations.
The C2 JU is capable of transmitting and receiving all response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks held locally by their system.

No automatic correlation restrictions apply — specifically: (a) no Identity (ID) conflict exists between the two tracks; (b) if Mode II codes differ, the local Mode II code is not current or inhibition capability is not active; (c) both tracks are not locally derived real-time tracks being updated with local positional data; (d) neither track has Strength field set to a value greater than 1 unless set to No Statement.

If one of the tracks is a remote report being tested for correlation and is a J2.0 Indirect PPLI message with Originator E/C field set to 0 (Surface) or 3 (Air), it shall be processed for correlation like a J3.2 air or J3.3 surface (maritime) track with TQ = 7.
Subsurface tracks are excluded from correlation with IUs, so any track involved must not be subsurface.

trigger.content: The C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation and initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU determines that two Track Numbers (TNs) are being used to report information for the same target and initiates a J7.7 Track Association message.
The C2 JU transmits the J7.7 Track Association message to request manual correlation of the subsurface surveillance data.
If the receiving C2 JU receives a J7.2 message with RV field set to value 3, it shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the specified restrictions applies.
Upon acceptance of the manual correlation, the resulting track shall not be subject to automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.

alternative_flow.content: If a correlation is not found, the C2 JU shall integrate the received J2 PPLI report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.

If 32 messages are not received subsequent to this action and the receiving C2 JU still has no local data, the C2 JU assumes no responsibility for reporting the subject IU on the Surveillance Network PG.
If the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system’s decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated.
After decorrelation, the C2 JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field shall both be reported as No Statement.

If a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, the C2 JU shall assume R2 of an IU (including C2 and non-C2 JUs and forwarded FUs and RUs) in accordance with real-time track reporting rules.
If a J2 PPLI message, other than J2.0, is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, the C2 JU shall assume R2 of an IU.
If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FU for a FU, SU, or other IU, the C2 JU shall assume R2 of an IU.
If the Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0, the C2 JU shall assume R2 of an IU.
A C2 JU assuming R2 of an IU reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG; the type of surveillance message depends upon the Environment/Category of the IU being reported.
The Identity shall be reported as Friend; the Track Number, Platform and Platform Activity values received in previous PPLI messages shall be reported.
The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator shall be reported as value 1, and shall be maintained if another C2 JU assumes R2 of the IU.
When the RV field is set to value 0 in a J7.2 Correlation message, it indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable.
When the RV field is set to value 1 in a J7.2 Correlation message, it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.

Receiving IUs desiring to reverse the requested correlation use the RV field to determine if a reverse correlation request should be originated or if the original correlation request should be rejected.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.

use_case_name: Clear Exercise Surveillance Data on an Exercise Status Order

goal.content: C2 JU wants to clear Exercise Surveillance Data on an Exercise Status Order by using the J7.0 (ACT = 6) Exercise Status Order message to rapidly clear the Exercise Indicator and all artificial data from exercise tracks.

preconditions.content: The J7.0 (ACT = 6) Exercise Status Order message is a valid Information Management data type used for the exchange of surveillance data.
C2 JU's database contains tracks with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1, and data concerning those tracks is considered artificial for exercise purposes.

trigger.content: A JU receives a J7.0 (ACT = 6) Exercise Status Order message.

main_flow.content: Upon receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 6) message, C2 JU applies the order to all tracks in its database with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1.
For those tracks, C2 JU automatically sets the Identity Amplifying Descriptor to Exercise Friend.
C2 JU breaks any locally originated engagement involving the TN by transmitting a J10.2 (WES = 8) message to report the engagement broken.

C2 JU terminates any locally originated Command message with Command values 2, 3, 5, or 7 involving the TN by transmitting a J9.0 message with the Command field set to value 4 (Cease Engage), or value 5 (Hold Fire) if the Engagement Status field is set to value 4 (Firing).
For those tracks, C2 JU automatically sets all data fields that may contain artificial information to the No Statement, default value, or actual values if held in database.
For those tracks, C2 JU sets the Exercise Indicator to value 0.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 4: When C2 JU terminates a locally originated Command message involving the TN and the Engagement Status field is set to value 4 (Firing), it may transmit a J9.0 message with the Command field set to value 5 (Hold Fire).

exception_flow.content: At main flow Step 5, when a data field on an exercise track is one of the fields that shall not be considered artificial for exercise purposes—Track Number; Tracking Data (Latitude, Longitude, Altitude/Elevation/Depth, Course, Speed, Minute, Hour, and Track Quality); Simulation Indicator; Environment/Category; Status Data on Air Tracks (Fuel Function, Fuel, Time Report Function, Minute, and Hour); or Status Data on Surface (Maritime) Tracks (Flight Deck Status, Landing/Approach Condition, and associated Time Report Function, Minute, and Hour)—C2 JU does not treat that field as artificial exercise data.
After main flow Step 6, when a subsequent message is received with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1, C2 JU discards that message.
After main flow Step 6, when C2 JU would originate a message with the Exercise Indicator set to value 1, it does not originate that message until local operator action is taken to reenable the JU.

postconditions.content: For every track in the JU's database that had the Exercise Indicator set to value 1, the Exercise Indicator is set to value 0.
For those tracks, all data fields that may contain artificial information are set to the No Statement or default value, or to actual values if held in the database.

goal.content: Coordinate transmit filters with all IUs by identifying filters by filter number to minimize track management problems.

preconditions.content: The use of interface filters shall be coordinated with all IUs to minimize track management problems.
Filters are identified by filter number for coordination with other JUs.
If the C2 JU filters tracks/IUs on receipt, a transmit filter that duplicates the receive filter must be established.
For filtering of C2 IUs, the C2 IUs have the Simulation Indicator field set in their J2 PPLI message; active nonsimulated C2 IUs cannot be filtered.

trigger.content: A C2 JU requests or reports the insertion or deletion of transmit filters, including data forwarding filters, to coordinate with all IUs and minimize track management problems.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU requests or reports the insertion or deletion of transmit filters, including data forwarding filters, in J7.6 messages.
The C2 JU uses the Filter Unit Type field to indicate whether the filter applies to individual JU transmissions or forwarding unit transmissions of forwarded data.

For forwarding unit filters, the C2 JU requests or reports only those filters used for filtering transmissions originating on Link 16; filters for forwarding data from any other link to Link 16 are neither requested nor reported via Link 16.
The C2 JU identifies all filters by filter number for coordination with other JUs.
The C2 JU coordinates the use of interface filters with all IUs to minimize track management problems, using voice or other communications media.
The C2 JU requests or reports track filters in separate J7.6 messages from reference point and EW product filters.
When a transmit filter is activated, the C2 JU ceases reporting any track for which it has R2 and which meets the filter criteria.
The C2 JU applies filters to tracks initiated prior to filter activation as well as to tracks initiated while the filter is active.
The C2 JU ensures tracks are eligible for transmission on the interface only if they are not inhibited from transmission by any of the transmission filters currently set.
The C2 JU does not request or report the use of receive filters via Link 16.
The C2 JU may filter C2 IUs with the Simulation Indicator field set in their J2 PPLI message; active nonsimulated C2 IUs cannot be filtered.
The C2 JU does not filter any track or nonC2 IU with an EMG IND or FT IND set to the value of 1.

alternative_flow.content: At main flow step 0, if the transmit filter is a special processing filter, a JU filters data based on the setting of the Special Processing Indicator field.
At main flow step 0, if the transmit filter is a simulation filter, a JU filters data and IUs based on the setting of the Simulation Indicator field.

At main flow step 0, if the transmit filter is an environment/category filter, a JU filters tracks and nonC2 IUs from the space, air, surface (maritime), subsurface (maritime), and land (ground) environment/categories, as well as reference points and electronic warfare product information.

At main flow step 0, if the transmit filter is an ID filter, a JU filters tracks and nonC2 IUs based on their IDs; Exercise Indicator settings have no influence on ID filters, and Identity and Identity Amplifying Descriptor are filtered in the same manner.

At main flow step 0, if the transmit filter is a geographic filter, a JU filters tracks and nonC2 IUs based on their geographic location; maximum and minimum altitude values may also be defined for each filter to describe volumes; filters can be fixed geographically, slaved to the filtering JU or some other moving reference point, or move independently.

At main flow step 0, if the filter is a message label/sublabel filter, the J7.6 message shall not be used to request implementation/deletion or status of message label/sublabel filters, and this type of filter will not be reported in the J7.6 Filter Description Report; if implemented, the message label/sublabel filter shall only be used for the purposes described and shall not be used as a data filter.

At main flow step 0, filters requested or reported in J7.6 do not apply to any messages other than the J2, J3, and J12 (on Needline PG) series messages listed, except a simulation filter applies to C2 IUs.

At main flow step 9, if a system filters tracks/IUs on receipt, it must establish a transmit filter which duplicates the receive filter; when a receive filter is geographically defined, the transmit filter must, where possible, be defined to permit the area filtered for transmission to be slightly larger than the area filtered for reception so that tracks entering or leaving the filtered area may be displayed to the operator to prevent dual designations.
At main flow step 10, if a C2 IU is active nonsimulated, it cannot be filtered.

exception_flow.content: If the filter is a receive filter, the use of receive filters is neither requested nor reported via Link 16; exit by not requesting or reporting receive filters via Link 16.

If forwarding unit filters are for forwarding data from any other link to Link 16, they are neither requested nor reported via Link 16; exit by not requesting or reporting such forwarding unit filters via Link 16.

If filters requested or reported in the J7.6 messages are for messages other than the J2, J3, and J12 (on Needline PG) series messages listed, they do not apply, except a simulation filter applies to C2 IUs; exit by not applying those filters to other messages.
If any track or nonC2 IU has an EMG IND or FT IND set to the value of 1, it shall not be filtered; exit by not filtering that track or nonC2 IU.
If a C2 IU is active nonsimulated, it cannot be filtered; exit by not filtering active nonsimulated C2 IUs. C2 IUs with the Simulation Indicator field set in their J2 PPLI message may be filtered.

If the storage files of a JU are filled and all applicable filters have been used, acceptance of the new data shall not be required, regardless of its ID or priority; this procedure applies to both real-time and nonrealtime data. Exit by not requiring acceptance of the new data.

If a C2 JU is deactivating a receive filter, after initially achieving Active status or after returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, it shall not transmit air, surface, or land tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed; the minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds and for land tracks is 48 seconds. Exit by delaying track transmission until the minimum wait is satisfied.

postconditions.content: The use of interface filters has been coordinated with all IUs to minimize track management problems.
All filters are identified by filter number for coordination with other JUs.
For any system that filters tracks/IUs on receipt, a transmit filter duplicating the receive filter has been established.

When a receive filter is geographically defined, the transmit filter is defined, where possible, to permit the area filtered for transmission to be slightly larger than the area filtered for reception so that tracks entering or leaving the filtered area may be displayed to the operator to prevent dual designations.
Tracks are eligible for transmission on the interface only if they are not inhibited from transmission by any of the transmission filters currently set.
Filters apply to tracks initiated prior to filter activation as well as to tracks initiated while the filter is active.
When a transmit filter is activated by a unit, the unit has ceased reporting any track for which it has R2 and which meets the filter criteria.
Active nonsimulated C2 IUs are not filtered; C2 IUs with the Simulation Indicator field set in their J2 PPLI message may be filtered.
No track or nonC2 IU with an EMG IND or FT IND set to the value of 1 is filtered.

goal.content: To ensure filter management on the interface by coordinating transmit filters, including data forwarding filters, via voice coordination in addition to the filter message.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU must have correlated local sensor data for the track if it is reporting a TQ value on the Surveillance NPG obtained via a J12.6 Target Sorting message from a nonC2 JU, to avoid applying extrapolation rules.
Voice coordination capability must be available in addition to the filter message mechanism to ensure filter management on the interface.

trigger.content: A JU requests that a filter be implemented by another JU, or reports a filter which the JU has inserted into its TDS, or responds to a J7.1 (ACT = 0) message.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU determines the filter types and parameters for each type, specifying whether to filter inside or outside the defined area.
The C2 JU sends a J7.6 (ACT = 0) message to request that a filter be implemented by another JU, with the Filter Number field set to value 0.
If specific filters have been prearranged, the C2 JU specifies the filter number with all Filter Indicator fields of the J7.6 (ACT = 0) set to value 0.
The C2 JU performs voice coordination in addition to sending the filter message to ensure filter management on the interface.

alternative_flow.content: If specific filters have been prearranged, the C2 JU may implement the request by specifying the filter number with all Filter Indicator fields of the J7.6 (ACT = 0) set to value 0.
Instead of an implementation request, the C2 JU may send a J7.6 (ACT = 1) message to report a filter which the JU has inserted into its TDS or to respond to a J7.1 (ACT = 0) message.
The C2 JU may send a J7.6 (ACT = 2) Delete Filter Request/Report message to manage existing filters.

exception_flow.content: If a C2 JU reports a real-time track, it must report the position of the track extrapolated to the time of transmission; failure to do so would be an exception to proper reporting rules.
Nonreal-time data shall be identified as such and time tags shall be provided. Nonreal-time track positions shall not be extrapolated; attempting to extrapolate them would be an error.
A new filter report on a previously received filter number from a JU shall supersede prior filter data for that number. If this does not happen correctly, it represents a data consistency exception.

In the case of a line or area filter requiring multiple messages all with the same filter number, all of the messages must be treated as a single filter report. Failure to treat them as a single report constitutes an exception in filter description processing.

postconditions.content: Filter management on the interface has been ensured through the use of voice coordination in addition to the filter message.

Transmit filters, including data forwarding filters, have been coordinated between JUs as specified by the Filter Unit Type field indicating whether the filter applies to individual JU transmissions or forwarding unit transmissions of forwarded data.

If a J7.6 (ACT = 0) implementation request was sent, the requested filter types and parameters have been specified, including whether to filter inside or outside the defined area, with the Filter Number field set to value 0.
If specific filters were prearranged, the implementation request consisted of specifying the filter number with all Filter Indicator fields of the J7.6 (ACT = 0) set to value 0.

If a J7.6 (ACT = 1) Filter Description Report was sent, the filter number has been set to a value between 1 and 14, and if responding to a J7.1 (ACT = 0) message, the message(s) have been addressed to the JU requesting the filter information.

goal.content: The C2 JU manages and applies transmit filters to determine which surveillance tracks are eligible for transmission on the interface.

preconditions.content: The use of interface filters must be coordinated with all participating Information Units (IUs) to minimize track management problems.
Transmit filters must be identified by a filter number for coordination purposes.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU coordinates the use of interface filters with all participating Information Units (IUs) to minimize track management problems, potentially using voice or other communications media.
Transmit filters are identified by a filter number for coordination purposes with other JUs.
When a receive filter is established, the C2 JU establishes a corresponding transmit filter which duplicates the receive filter.

The C2 JU manages and applies transmit filters to determine which surveillance tracks are eligible for transmission; tracks are eligible only if not inhibited by any currently set transmission filters.

Upon activation of a transmit filter, the unit ceases reporting any track for which it has R² that meets the filter criteria and complies with rules for terminating transmission of applicable track data.
Management and reporting of Link 16 transmit filters are accomplished using J7.6 messages (Filter Implementation Request, Filter Description Report, Delete Filter Request/Report) and J7.1 messages.

alternative_flow.content: A special processing filter allows a JU to filter data based on the setting of the Special Processing Indicator field.
A simulation filter allows a JU to filter data and IUs based on the setting of the Simulation Indicator field.
The J7.6 (ACT = 2) message is used by a JU to request that a filter or all filters be deleted by an addressed JU, or to report deletion of one or all of its filters.
When a JU deletes a filter which it had reported, it should transmit a J7.6 (ACT = 2) message; remote filters shall be dropped when such a message is received.
Filter messages are nonredundant, and each JU should have the capability to drop remote filter reports from its own system.
The J7.1 (ACT = 0) message may be used by a JU to request information on a specific filter or all locally inserted filters.

postconditions.content: Upon activation of a transmit filter, the unit ceases reporting any track for which it has R² that meets the filter criteria and complies with rules for terminating transmission of applicable track data.
Filters apply to tracks initiated prior to filter activation as well as to tracks initiated while the filter is active.

use_case_name: Decorrelate Diverging Air or Surface Tracks

goal.content: The goal of the use case is to decorrelate any two air tracks or any two surface tracks.

preconditions.content: C2 JU has initiated real-time air or surface tracks.
The position or other data in a PPLI meet the system's decorrelation criteria.
A common local track exists upon receipt of a J2 or J3 message.

trigger.content: Automatic decorrelation tests are performed for each common local track upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on the track. A C2 JU receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) initiates decorrelation processing.

main_flow.content: C2 JU automatically tests the local track once for correlation against remote tracks, not against common local tracks, after the common local track (TN A) satisfies the criteria for automatic or manual decorrelation.
If the automatic correlation test fails, C2 JU assigns a new track number (TN B) to the local track and reports TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
C2 JU decorrelates the PPLI and local track data when the position or other data in the PPLI meet the system's decorrelation criteria.
After decorrelation, C2 JU initiates a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
In that report, C2 JU reports the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field as No Statement.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 3: when TN A is controlled by own unit (subject of a J10.5 Controlling Unit Report), decorrelation is manually initiated rather than automatic; upon manual decorrelation, C2 JU alerts the operator to report termination of control on TN A.

Diverges from Step 3: when TN A has been paired by own unit (subject of a J10.6 message), C2 JU decorrelates and alerts the operator as a cue to terminate the pairing on TN A and initiate the pairing on TN B if appropriate.

Diverges from Step 3: when selecting the TN to be dropped during decorrelation, if a TN has any of the OCCs listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(6 7), C2 JU excludes it from automatic selection; absent such a selection constraint, C2 JU selects the higher TN as the TN to be dropped.

Diverges from Step 3: when own unit has R² for the Dropped TN, C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message for the Dropped TN; if the Dropped TN is subsequently reported by another IU after transmission, C2 JU retains it as a remote track and does not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for 60 seconds after transmission.

exception_flow.content: At Step 1, if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions — (1) an Identity (ID) difference constituting a conflict; (2) different Mode II codes with the local Mode II code current; (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks; or (4) either track has its Strength field set to a value greater than 1 — C2 JU shall not automatically correlate the two tracks. These restrictions do not apply to manual correlation, and no other correlation restrictions shall be applied for two tracks that pass the specified correlation tests. Exit: automatic correlation is inhibited; manual correlation remains permitted.

At Step 1, when an initialization parameter or operator-selectable capability is set to inhibit the automatic restriction for ID conflicts or Mode II code mismatches, subject to interface coordination and promulgation to all C² IUs, the automatic restriction is inhibited. If no specific interface direction exists, all IUs restrict automatic correlation by default. Exit: the restriction is either inhibited by the configured override or applied by default.

At Step 1, if the automatic correlation test fails during decorrelation execution, C2 JU assigns a new Track Number (TN B) to the local track and reports TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message. Exit: the track is reported under TN B.

At Step 4, if an operator action has selectively released a new local track for reporting, C2 JU shall transmit it regardless of the results of correlation testing. Exit: the released track is transmitted.

postconditions.content: C2 JU assigns a new Track Number (TN B) to the local track.
C2 JU initiates a surveillance track report with locally held data using the new track number.
In the post-decorrelation surveillance track report, the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field are reported as No Statement.
C2 JU reports the new Track Number (TN B) in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.

use_case_name: Decorrelate Diverging Air or Surface Tracks

goal.content: The use case decorrelates any two air tracks or any two surface tracks that meet the decorrelation criteria, thereby minimizing the occurrences and duration of dual designations.

preconditions.content: The two tracks to be decorrelated are either any two air tracks or any two surface tracks.
The C2 JU has an automatic decorrelation capability for real-time air or surface tracks it initiates, or it is performing manual decorrelation, which C2 JUs may also do.
The tracks meet the applicable decorrelation criteria.

trigger.content: When the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system's decorrelation criteria, the C2 JU shall decorrelate the PPLI and local track data.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU performs automatic decorrelation tests for each common local track upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on the track.

The C2 JU determines that the common local track (TN A) satisfies the criteria of an automatic or manual decorrelation when, on receipt of 2(1-5, 1) consecutive remote track reports, the remote track falls outside a distance of 1.5(1.0-2.0, 0.1) times the maximum correlation distance calculated in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f(3).
After it has been determined that the common local track (TN A) satisfies the criteria of an automatic or manual decorrelation, the C2 JU executes the decorrelation.
If TN A has been correlated with an Index Number by own unit, the C2 JU assesses whether the Index Number should remain with TN A or B, and transmits J12.5 messages as appropriate.
After decorrelation, the C2 JU initiates a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.

alternative_flow.content: C2 JUs may also perform manual decorrelation in addition to automatic decorrelation.
If the C2 JU has a capability to require manual confirmation of automatic decorrelations, manual confirmation of automatic decorrelations is required.

If TN A is the subject of a handover which is in progress, i.e., a TN in a J10.3 Handover message, the decorrelation shall be delayed until the handover process is completed or terminated; then the decorrelation shall be executed and an operator alerted as a cue to report control in the J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message as appropriate; operator display of the pending decorrelation shall be provided.

exception_flow.content: 1. If TN A is controlled by own unit; i.e., is the subject of own unit reported J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message, do not automatically decorrelate; exit the automatic decorrelation path. If manually decorrelated, alert the operator as a cue to report termination of control TN A if appropriate. Report commencement of control of TN B using the J10.5 message only if initiated by operator action.

postconditions.content: The PPLI and local track data are decorrelated.
After decorrelation, the C2 JU has initiated a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
If TN A had been correlated with an Index Number by own unit, whether the Index Number should remain with TN A or B has been assessed, and J12.5 messages have been transmitted as appropriate.

If TN A was the subject of a pending J9.0 Command message which own unit originated or to which own unit was preparing a reply, operator display of new track status on TNs A and B has been provided before release of the J9.0 reply, and the reply is relative to TN A.

If TN A was the subject of a handover in progress, the handover process has been completed or terminated, the decorrelation has been executed, and the operator has been alerted as a cue to report control in the J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message as appropriate; operator display of the pending decorrelation has been provided.

If TN A was controlled by own unit and was manually decorrelated, the operator has been alerted as a cue to report termination of control TN A if appropriate, and commencement of control of TN B using the J10.5 message has been reported only if initiated by operator action.

use_case_name: Decorrelate Diverging Air or Surface Tracks

goal.content: To decorrelate diverging air or surface tracks when a C2 JU determines that two previously correlated tracks are no longer the same track.

preconditions.content: Two tracks (air or surface) have been previously correlated by the C2 JU.
The C2 JU has determined that the two previously correlated tracks are no longer the same track (i.e., they are diverging).
The C2 JU is capable of automatically initiating and deactivating track correlation capabilities without operator action, as required for real-time track reporting and difference resolution.

trigger.content: A C2 JU determines that two previously correlated air or surface tracks are no longer the same track (i.e., they are diverging).

alternative_flow.content: If the C2 JU holds locally derived data for Platform, Platform Activity, or Specific Type fields that differ from the values accepted for retransmission, it shall report the locally derived data instead of retransmitting the previously correlated track identity.
If the Special Interest Indicator is set to value 1 for either diverging track, it shall be retransmitted as value 1 by any JU assuming R², regardless of locally derived data.

For real-time tracks, the position reported after decorrelation shall be extrapolated to the time of transmission; for nonreal-time tracks, positions shall not be extrapolated and must include time tags.
Velocity (course and speed) for air or surface tracks shall be reported in data miles per hour of ground speed and degrees with respect to true north.
Tracking Data including Latitude, Longitude, Altitude/Elevation/Depth, Course, Speed, Minute, Hour, and Track Quality shall be provided for each decorrelated track if applicable.

exception_flow.content: If the C2 JU is deactivating a receive filter, it shall not transmit air, surface, or land tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed.
The minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks after achieving Active status or returning from Inactive status or TDS Failure is 12 seconds; for land tracks, it is 48 seconds.
Under conditions where nonreal-time tracks are irregularly reported, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.

When an Air Platform value of 6 (Tanker), 7 (Tanker Boom Only), or 8 (Tanker Drogue Only) is held locally and a different value is received during difference resolution, an operator alert in this situation is optional.

postconditions.content: The diverging air or surface tracks are reported as separate entities with their respective Environment/Category, Identity, and Exercise Indicator values resolved.

A J3.X or J7.0 (ACT = 1) message is generated containing the appropriate evaluation of the Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator fields for the decorrelated tracks.

If the C2 JU accepted a remote ID change during the resolution, it retains the received values of the Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator fields for retransmission.
For each decorrelated real-time track, the position is reported extrapolated to the time of transmission.
For any decorrelated nonreal-time track, the data is identified as such, time tags are provided, and the track position is not extrapolated.
Tracking Data including Latitude, Longitude, Altitude/Elevation/Depth, Course, Speed, Minute, Hour, and Track Quality is included in the report for the decorrelated tracks.

use_case_name: Decorrelate Diverging Air or Surface Tracks

goal.content: To decorrelate any two air tracks or any two surface tracks when a common local track satisfies the criteria for automatic or manual decorrelation, resulting in the assignment of a new TN to the local track.

preconditions.content: The C² JU has initiated real-time air or surface tracks.
The C² JU possesses an automatic decorrelation capability.
A common local track exists for which decorrelation criteria are being evaluated.

trigger.content: Receipt of each J2 or J3 message on a common local track initiates automatic decorrelation tests.

main_flow.content: Automatic decorrelation tests shall be performed for each common local track upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on the track.

Common local tracks shall be decorrelated if, on receipt of 2(1-5, 1) consecutive remote track reports, the remote track falls outside a distance of 1.5(1.0-2.0, 0.1) times the maximum correlation distance calculated in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f(3).
After it has been determined that a common local track (TN A) satisfies the criteria of an automatic or manual decorrelation, the decorrelation shall be executed as follows:
The local track shall be automatically tested once for correlation against remote tracks (not common local tracks) in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and g.
If the automatic correlation test fails, assign a new TN (TN B) to the local track and report TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.

alternative_flow.content: If the C² JU receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) has an OCC on the Dropped TN as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(7) and the received RV field is set to value 0, the reverse correlation shall be transmitted if the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint; however, if both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(7) and the received RV field is set to value 1, the correlation shall be rejected.
When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.

C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict; (2) One track is simulated and the other is live; or (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.

exception_flow.content: If the two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict, automatic correlation shall be restricted unless inhibited by operator-selectable capability.
If the two tracks have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current, automatic correlation shall be restricted unless inhibited by operator-selectable capability.
If both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data, automatic correlation shall be restricted.

If either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1, systems shall not inhibit correlation; however, if Strength is set to No Statement, correlation may proceed without inhibition based on this criterion.
After acceptance of a manual correlation, the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.

postconditions.content: A new TN (TN B) is assigned to the local track and reported in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
The Retained TN and the Dropped TN decorrelate, i.e., when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the tracks would decorrelate; in this case the correlation shall be rejected.
If both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
An operator alert is provided as a cue to conduct voice coordination when a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation.
After acceptance of a manual correlation, the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.

use_case_name: Decorrelate Diverging Air or Surface Tracks

goal.content: The C2 JU automatically or manually decorrelates air or surface tracks that were previously correlated but have diverged beyond specified criteria, ensuring accurate track separation and preventing false associations.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU must have an automatic decorrelation capability for real-time air or surface tracks.
Automatic decorrelation tests shall be performed for each common local track upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on the track.

Common local tracks shall be decorrelated if, on receipt of consecutive remote track reports, the remote track falls outside a specified distance threshold (1.5 times the maximum correlation distance).
The C2 JU must be capable of performing correlation and decorrelation of local track data with respect to received remote data to prevent dual designations.
If a manual correlation was previously accepted, the resulting track shall not be subject to automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.

trigger.content: The C2 JU initiates decorrelation of diverging air or surface tracks upon receipt of consecutive remote track reports (J2 or J3 messages) where the remote track falls outside a specified distance threshold (1.5 times the maximum correlation distance).

main_flow.content: After determining that a common local track satisfies the criteria for automatic or manual decorrelation, the local track is automatically tested once for correlation against remote tracks (excluding common local tracks) in accordance with specified correlation paragraphs.
If the automatic correlation test fails, a new Track Number (TN) is assigned to the local track, and this new TN is reported in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
The Retained TN and the Dropped TN are decorrelated, meaning that if subjected to the decorrelation criteria again, the tracks would decorrelate, and the correlation is rejected.

alternative_flow.content: C² JUs may perform manual decorrelation and may have a capability to require manual confirmation of automatic decorrelations.
If the automatic correlation test fails during decorrelation execution, a new Track Number (TN) is assigned to the local track and reported in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
When a C² JU recognizes two tracks eligible for correlation, it shall initiate action either automatically or manually to resolve the dual designation by transmitting a J7.2 Correlation message.

Receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.
C² JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with RV=2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2 minutes.
When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
After acceptance of a manual correlation, the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.

exception_flow.content: If the automatic correlation test fails during the execution of decorrelation, a new Track Number (TN) is assigned to the local track and reported in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
The Retained TN and the Dropped TN will decorrelate; if subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the tracks would decorrelate, and in this case the correlation shall be rejected.

If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 0, the reverse correlation shall be transmitted if the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint; if both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 1, the correlation shall be rejected.

C² JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2 minutes.
When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.

C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless restrictions apply (e.g., different E/C, one simulated/one live, both locally derived real-time tracks), in which case the correlation shall be rejected.

C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if they have an Identity (ID) difference constituting a conflict, different Mode II codes (with local code current), both are locally derived real-time tracks, or either track has Strength > 1.

postconditions.content: After decorrelation, a new Track Number (TN B) is assigned to the local track and reported in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
The Retained TN and the Dropped TN are decorrelated such that if subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the tracks would decorrelate, and the correlation shall be rejected.

If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 0, the reverse correlation shall be transmitted if the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint; if both Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.

use_case_name: Initiate and Clear Surveillance Track Alerts

goal.content: The C2 JU wants to initiate and clear force tell or emergency surveillance alerts on tracks, land (ground) points, subsurface contacts, and electronic warfare product information.

preconditions.content: A Force Tell (FT) or Emergency (EMG) alert condition is known to exist for the targeted surveillance entity, and the appropriate condition exists to set or clear the EMG IND or FT IND indicators via J3 messages.

The targeted surveillance entity exists with an assigned Track Number and defined Environment/Category type. For tracks, prior J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages containing EMG IND or FT IND values have been received; for land (ground) points or subsurface contacts, J3.5 (PTI = 0) Land Point messages or J5.4 Acoustic Bearing/Range messages have been received; and for electronic warfare product information, EW detections have been determined eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG.

The C2 JU possesses R² (Responsibility) authority over the specific track number (TN) or point for the targeted entity, allowing it to directly set or clear the EMG IND or FT IND in the corresponding J3 message.

trigger.content: The C2 JU initiates or clears a force tell or emergency alert on a track, land (ground) point, subsurface contact, or electronic warfare product information.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU determines that a force tell or emergency alert is to be initiated on a selected surveillance entity (track, land (ground) point, subsurface contact, or electronic warfare product information).

The C2 JU uses the J3 message appropriate to the selected entity: a J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 track message; a J3.5 (PTI = 0) Land (Ground) Point message or J5.4 Acoustic Bearing/Range message for land points or subsurface contacts; or a J3.7 message for electronic warfare product information.
The C2 JU sets the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in that message to initiate the alert.
The set EMG IND or FT IND allows the message to override all operator-controllable data filters.
All receiving JUs accept the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J3.x message containing the set indicator.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from main flow Step 1 when the C2 JU determines that an existing alert is to be cleared rather than initiated: the C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message terminating the alert and sets the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND field in subsequent J3 messages to value 0.

Diverges from main flow Step 1 when the C2 JU needs to clear an existing alert: alternatively, the alert may be cleared by reception of a J3.X message (e.g., J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5) with the EMG IND and/or FT IND set to value 0.

exception_flow.content: If the selected target is a Reference Point, line, area, or Space/Ballistic Missile Track and the requested alert is an emergency alert, the emergency alert shall not be initiated; emergency alerts are prohibited or not used on those target types.
If the message being considered is a J3.1 Emergency Point message, alerts are not used for that message because these points cannot be filtered.
If operator-controllable filtering would otherwise apply, any track or non-C² IU with an EMG IND or FT IND set to the value of 1 shall not be filtered.

If a receiving JU's storage files are filled and all applicable filters have been used, acceptance of the new alert data shall not be required, regardless of its ID or priority; this applies to both real-time and non-real-time data.

postconditions.content: Following successful initiation, all receiving JUs have accepted the alert in their databases.
For a force tell alert, the JU whose force tell status is being changed has accepted the change and its J2 message reports that change.
For an alert termination, other receiving JUs have cleared the alert indicator in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 4) message.

use_case_name: Initiate and Clear Surveillance Track Alerts

goal.content: The C2 JU wants to initiate and clear force tell or emergency surveillance alerts on tracks, land (ground) points, subsurface contacts, and electronic warfare product information.

preconditions.content: A Force Tell (FT) or Emergency (EMG) alert condition is known to exist for the targeted surveillance entity, and the appropriate condition exists to set or clear the EMG IND or FT IND indicators via J3 messages.

The targeted surveillance entity exists with an assigned Track Number and defined Environment/Category type. For tracks, prior J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages containing EMG IND or FT IND values have been received; for land (ground) points or subsurface contacts, J3.5 (PTI = 0) Land Point messages or J5.4 Acoustic Bearing/Range messages have been received; and for electronic warfare product information, EW detections have been determined eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG.

The C2 JU possesses R² (Responsibility) authority over the specific track number (TN) or point for the targeted entity, allowing it to directly set or clear the EMG IND or FT IND in the corresponding J3 message.

trigger.content: The C2 JU initiates or clears a force tell or emergency alert on a track, land (ground) point, subsurface contact, or electronic warfare product information.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU determines that a force tell or emergency alert is to be initiated on a selected surveillance entity (track, land (ground) point, subsurface contact, or electronic warfare product information).

The C2 JU uses the J3 message appropriate to the selected entity: a J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 track message; a J3.5 (PTI = 0) Land (Ground) Point message or J5.4 Acoustic Bearing/Range message for land points or subsurface contacts; or a J3.7 message for electronic warfare product information.
The C2 JU sets the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in that message to initiate the alert.
The set EMG IND or FT IND allows the message to override all operator-controllable data filters.
All receiving JUs accept the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J3.x message containing the set indicator.

postconditions.content: Following successful initiation, all receiving JUs have accepted the alert in their databases.
For a force tell alert, the JU whose force tell status is being changed has accepted the change and its J2 message reports that change.

use_case_name: Initiate and Clear Surveillance Track Alerts

goal.content: To ensure accurate, non-redundant, geospatially valid track representation via correlation/resolution of surveillance tracks by initiating action to resolve dual designations and clearing alerts when conditions are met.

preconditions.content: The system must be capable of receiving and processing J3 messages containing Force Tell and Emergency Indicators.
Track alerts (Force Tell and Emergency) must have been previously set via J3 messages to indicate force tell and/or emergency conditions.
The C2 JU must have the capability to manage its database to avoid saturation by force tell and emergency alerts, particularly if it has limited track capacity (e.g., F-15).
The indicators for track alerts must be set or cleared in accordance with the specifications in paragraph 4.7.1.4 (referenced but not provided in context).

trigger.content: A C2 JU shall assume R² of an IU (including C² and nonC² JUs and forwarded PUs and RUs) in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C² JU has correlated local sensor data, when: a. A J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, or b. A J2 PPLI message, other than J2.0, is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or c. A J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU, or d. The Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.

main_flow.content: When a C² JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
The message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.

If a correlation is found with a track for which the C² JU has R², the J7.2 Correlation message shall be transmitted with the Response Value (RV) field set to value 1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), and with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
The C² JU shall cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.

alternative_flow.content: If the receiving IU has any constraint which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation, it shall set the Response Value (RV) field to value 0 in its J7.2 message to indicate that a reverse correlation would be acceptable.
If the receiving IU indicates in its J7.2 message that a reverse correlation request should be rejected (RV = 2), the originating JU shall reject the original correlation request.
When the RV field is set to value 3 in the J7.2 message, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.

If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.

If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.

exception_flow.content: If the receiving IU has any constraint which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation, it shall set the Response Value (RV) field to value 0 in its J7.2 message to indicate that a reverse correlation would be acceptable.

use_case_name: Initiate and Clear Surveillance Track Alerts

goal.content: Enable the C2 JU to initiate and clear surveillance track alerts (force tell and emergency) by setting or clearing appropriate alert indicators in J-series messages.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU must have the capability to initiate/terminate a force tell alert on another JU by setting/clearing the FT IND in a J7.0 (ACT = 4) message.
For tracks, the initiating JU must possess R² capability to set EMG IND or FT IND in J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages; otherwise, it must use J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4).
For land (ground) points or subsurface contacts, the initiating JU must possess R² capability to set EMG IND or FT IND in J3.5 (PTI = 0) or J5.4 messages; otherwise, it must use J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4).
For Electronic Warfare Product Information, the initiating JU must possess R² capability to set EMG IND or FT IND in the J3.7 message; otherwise, it must use J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4).

trigger.content: The C2 JU operator initiates an action to set or clear the emergency (EMG IND) or force tell (FT IND) alert indicators for a surveillance track.

main_flow.content: A JU with R² capability initiates an emergency or force tell alert on a surveillance track by setting the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in the J3.2 Air Track, J3.3 Surface Track, J3.4 Subsurface Track, or J3.5 Land Point/Track message.
All receiving JUs accept the alert indicator set by the initiating JU in their databases upon receipt of the J3.X track message.
A JU with R² capability terminates an emergency or force tell alert by transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message to terminate the alert.
After sending the J7.0 termination message, the initiating JU sets the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND field to 0 in subsequent J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages for that track.

goal.content: To exchange surveillance information on the Link 16 network by transmitting ballistic missile track/point data that is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU is participating in the exchange of J3 Surveillance messages on the Link 16 network.
The C2 JU has detected data points via its local sensors that constitute ballistic missile surveillance tracks.

trigger.content: The C2 JU detects data points via its local sensors that constitute ballistic missile surveillance tracks.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU determines whether the data points being detected by its local sensors are currently reported on the interface and if there are any conflicts between locally derived information and information reported on the interface.
To accomplish this, the C2 JU continuously correlates locally derived ballistic missile tracks with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.
The C2 JU reports on all uncorrelated local ballistic missile tracks.
For these uncorrelated tracks, the C2 JU assumes R² in accordance with the R² rules specified in paragraph 4.4.6.15.
The source of the ballistic missile track/point data is provided (Source TN).
The C2 JU time tags the ballistic missile data.
The C2 JU reports the position and associated parameters of the track valid at the time tagged.

Positional data for the ballistic missile tracks is reported in the Space Track message as X, Y, Z position in earth-centered, earth-fixed (ECF) Cartesian coordinates defined by the World Geodetic System-84 (WGS-84) Reference Frame.
Velocity of the ballistic missile tracks is reported as the rate of change along the X, Y, Z axis.
