goal.content: To publish electronic warfare surveillance products, namely lines of bearing (LOBs), fixes, and areas of probability (AOPs), via the J3.7 EW Product Information message on the Surveillance Network PG.

preconditions.content: EW detections eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG have been determined, either manually or through automatic association with predetermined reporting criteria.
The originating unit for the J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report to be published retains reporting responsibility.
Transmission of the EW Product is not inhibited by the applicable ENV, ID, GEO, SP, and SIM flags.

trigger.content: An EW detection is determined to be eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG, either manually or through automatic association with predetermined reporting criteria.

main_flow.content: The EW-capable C2 JU determines which EW detections are eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG, either manually or through automatic association with predetermined reporting criteria.
The C2 JU transmits lines of bearing (LOBs), fixes, or areas of probability (AOPs) via the J3.7 EW Product Information message on the Surveillance Network PG.
The C2 JU may amplify LOBs, fixes, and AOPs by the J6.0 Amplification message on the Surveillance Network PG.
The C2 JU reports EW association using the J7.7 message.
The C2 JU may use the J7.2 message to correlate EW AOPs with surveillance tracks, but the J7.2 message shall not be used to correlate EW LOBs and fixes with surveillance tracks.
When the C2 JU drops or ceases reporting EW information that it has been reporting on the interface, it transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

alternative_flow.content: A1. At step 0, the determination of which EW detections are eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG may be performed manually or through automatic association with predetermined reporting criteria.
A2. At step 1, if data are available, additional continuation words may be added to the minimum required word sequences to amplify EW reports.

A3. At step 1, when SIM = 1 and the applicable ENV, ID, GEO, and SP flag combination matches a defined inhibition condition, the EW Product is inhibited from transmission (e.g., SIM=1, ENV=0, ID=0, GEO=0, SP=0 inhibits any EW Product with Simulation status).

A4. At step 1, if an AOP results from two or more previously reported fixes of differing TNs, assign a new TN not one of the TNs assigned to the fixes and use the new TN for all subsequent updates; if a fix is changed to an AOP, use the TN of the previously reported fix for the new AOP.

A5. At step 1, a JU with R^2 shall initiate an emergency or force tell alert on EW Product information by setting the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in the J3.7 message, and all receiving JUs shall accept the alert in their databases.

A6. At step 1, the JU with R^2 shall terminate an emergency or force tell alert by transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message terminating the alert and setting the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in subsequent J3.7 messages to 0; all receiving JUs shall terminate the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message; optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.7 message with the EMG and/or FT IND set to value 0.
A7. At step 4, the J7.2 message may be used to correlate EW AOPs with surveillance tracks, but the J7.2 message shall not be used to correlate EW LOBs and fixes with surveillance tracks.

A8. At step 5, the transmission of EW product information shall be terminated when the information is no longer valid or time-related update requirements are not met; the information may be purged in accordance with system design.

A9. At step 5, when a JU drops or ceases reporting EW information that it has been reporting on the interface, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message; the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted on remote reports, and remote reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria.

exception_flow.content: E1. If SIM = 1 and the applicable ENV, ID, GEO, and SP flag combination matches a defined EW Product inhibition condition, inhibit transmission of that EW Product and exit this use case for that EW Product.

E2. If the EW product information is no longer valid or time-related update requirements are not met, terminate transmission of that EW product information; the information may be purged in accordance with system design; exit this use case for that EW product information.
E3. If the C2 JU drops or ceases reporting EW information that it has been reporting on the interface, transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and exit this use case for that EW information.

E4. If the EW information being dropped or ceased is a remote report, do not transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on remote reports; remote reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria; exit this exception without transmitting J7.0 (ACT = 0).

E5. If correlation of EW LOBs or fixes with surveillance tracks is attempted via the J7.2 message, do not use J7.2 for that correlation because J7.2 shall not be used to correlate EW LOBs and fixes with surveillance tracks; report EW association using the J7.7 message and exit this exception.

goal.content: To report EW detections such as LOBs, AOPs, or fixes derived from various sources via the J3.7 EW Product Information message on the Surveillance Network PG.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU must be EW-capable and capable of generating and managing track numbers.

The C2 JU must have determined which EW detections are eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG, either manually or through automatic association with predetermined reporting criteria.

trigger.content: An EW-capable C2 JU determines which EW detections are eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU determines which EW detections are eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG, either manually or through automatic association with predetermined reporting criteria.
The C2 JU reports Line of Bearing (LOB) data derived from sources such as ES, jam strobes, or radio direction finding (RDF) equipment using the J3.7 EW Product Information Message.
The C2 JU sets the Fix or Bearing Descriptor (FIX BRG) field in the J3.7I word to describe the reported LOB.
If additional data is available, the C2 JU adds continuation words to the minimum required word sequences to amplify the EW report.
The C2 JU transmits the J3.7 EW Product Information message containing the surveillance products (LOBs, fixes, and AOPs) on the Surveillance Network PG.

exception_flow.content: If the C2 JU determines that a track's simulation status needs to be changed (e.g., due to operator error), the track shall be dropped using the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, and a new track shall be reported.

The one exception to dropping the track for a simulation status change is if the change is from live to simulated and the track is being received from an FJU; in this case, the change shall be accepted without dropping the track.

If applicable, LOBs, fixes, and AOPs are amplified by the J6.0 Amplification message on the Surveillance Network PG.

goal.content: To report Electronic Warfare product information, including EW Fixes, Areas of Probability (AOP), and Lines of Bearing (LOB), while retaining reporting responsibility for the originated data.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU must have generated or received EW product information (such as an EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report) that it intends to publish.

If the C2 JU is initiating a new J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report, it must assign a Track Number (TN) not known to be in use on the interface, even if believed to concern the same emitter currently reported by another unit — unless it is originating a report on a fix/AOP/LOB already reported by itself or received via J14.0 message from another unit.

For reporting an Area of Probability (AOP), the C2 JU must have organic data, exchange of LOBs, analysis of EW fix data, or a combination thereof to define an area with 95% probability (2 sigma) of emitter location.

If reporting a bearing origin for an EW LOB, the C2 JU must determine whether the origin is its own unit, another existing IU/track/point, or a designated position, and set corresponding fields accordingly (Bearing Origin field, Origin TN field, and J3.7C2 word).
The C2 JU must retain reporting responsibility for any J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report it originates; it is illegal to assume reporting responsibility for another unit’s such report.

trigger.content: The C2 JU originates a J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report and retains reporting responsibility for it.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU determines which EW detections are eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG, either manually or through automatic association with predetermined reporting criteria.
If reporting a Line of Bearing (LOB), the C2 JU uses the J3.7 EW Product Information Message and sets the Fix or Bearing Descriptor (FIX BRG) field in the J3.7I word as required.
If reporting an Area of Probability (AOP), the C2 JU transmits using a J3.7I/J3.7C1/J3.7C2 word sequence as a minimum, with the FIX BRG field set to value 1 in the J3.7I word.

For AOP reporting, the J3.7I word contains the time the AOP was valid and the J3.7C2 word defines the AOP; if resulting from previously reported LOBs, it shall be assigned a new TN not one of the TNs assigned to the LOBs.

If reporting bearing origin for an EW LOB, the C2 JU sets the Bearing Origin field and Origin TN field according to whether the origin is its own unit, another existing IU/track/point, or a designated position, and transmits the J3.7C2 word containing latitude and longitude of the bearing origin.
The C2 JU retains reporting responsibility for the originated J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report; it is illegal to assume reporting responsibility for another unit’s such report.

If initiating a new J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report, the C2 JU assigns a TN not known to be in use on the interface — unless originating a report on a fix/AOP/LOB already reported by itself or received via J14.0 message from another unit, in which case it assigns the same TN referenced in the J3.7 message contained in the J14.0 message.

Upon termination of EW product information (when no longer valid or update requirements not met), the C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message if it had been reporting on the interface; remote reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria.

exception_flow.content: If a C2 JU attempts to assume reporting responsibility for another unit's J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report, this is illegal and constitutes an exception condition — the system must reject such assumption of responsibility.

If a C2 JU initiates a new J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report using a Track Number (TN) already known to be in use on the interface (and not covered by the J14.0 message exception), this violates protocol — the system must flag or reject the duplicate TN assignment.

If an AOP is generated from previously reported LOBs but is assigned one of the original LOBs’ TNs instead of a new TN, this violates the rule that ‘an AOP resulting from previously reported LOBs shall be assigned a new TN’ — the system must enforce TN reassignment.

If an AOP results from two or more previously reported fixes of differing TNs but is assigned one of those existing TNs instead of a new TN, this violates the rule requiring a new TN — the system must detect and prevent this misassignment.

If a fix is changed to an AOP but the system fails to retain the previously reported fix’s TN for the new AOP (as required when changing fix to AOP), this constitutes an exception — the system must ensure TN continuity in this specific transition.

postconditions.content: The C2 JU retains reporting responsibility for the J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report it originated.
If an AOP was reported resulting from previously reported LOBs, a new Track Number (TN) not assigned to any of the original LOBs has been assigned to the AOP.
If an AOP resulted from two or more previously reported fixes of differing TNs, a new TN not one of the TNs assigned to the fixes has been assigned to the AOP.
If a fix was changed to an AOP, the TN of the previously reported fix is retained and used for all subsequent updates of the AOP.

If bearing origin was reported for an EW LOB, the Bearing Origin field, Origin TN field, and J3.7C2 word have been transmitted according to whether the origin was own unit, another existing IU/track/point, or designated position.

Upon termination of EW product information transmission, if the C2 JU had been reporting on the interface, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message has been transmitted; remote reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria.

use_case_name: Publish Subsurface Surveillance and Acoustic Contact Reports

goal.content: The C2 JU wants to publish subsurface surveillance and acoustic contact reports containing bearings, ranges, and track data—including position, velocity, identity, and time—derived from ASW sensors, including reporting a track as a DATUM when contact is lost.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU is in Active status, having either initially achieved Active status or returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
The C2 JU has correlated local sensor data.
For a new local track to be reported, automatic correlation has been attempted and has failed on the initial correlation test or on the next test following an initial tentative correlation.

trigger.content: The use case starts when the C2 JU has tactically significant information derived from ASW sensors—such as bearings, ranges, or tracks—that requires reporting, or when it determines that a Subsurface IU is no longer active and it holds local data on that IU.

main_flow.content: C2 JU uses J3.4 messages for subsurface surveillance track data and J5.4 messages for acoustic bearing/range data derived from ASW sensors.
For subsurface surveillance track reporting, C2 JU provides the source of track data (Source TN).

C2 JU reports established local subsurface surveillance tracks with all known parameters at the next reporting opportunity in a J3.4 message, including geodetic latitude and longitude, depth when available, velocity as course and speed, identity via the Identity field or J3.4I message, discrete identifier codes in the J7.5 message, and time of contact acquisition/loss/datum establishment in the J3.4C1 word, with all data time tagged.

When reporting acoustic bearing and range, C2 JU uses the J5.4 Acoustic Bearing/Range message, sets the BRT field to value 0 (Bearing and Range), populates the Bearing 1, ASW field with the bearing from the detecting sensor origin, and populates the Range field with the range.

When contact is lost and the operator decides to report the track as a DATUM, the C2 JU reports a J3.4 message using the same Reference TN as the lost-contact track, with DRT set to 4 (DATUM), ASW Time Function set to 3 (Time Contact Lost) or 1 (Time Datum Established), and last known position and depth; the DATUM does not move, retains last known course and speed only for DATUM Error and ASW search calculations, and shall only be dropped or purged by operator action.
C2 JU transmits the surveillance information in Network PGs.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 3: C2 JU uses the J7.0 Track Management (ACT = 1) Difference Report message to report changes in track parameters without retransmitting full track data.

Diverges from Step 3: when contact is lost, the decision to report a track as a DATUM is an operator function; C2 JU reports the DATUM in a J3.4 message with the same Reference TN as the track for which contact was lost and with Data Report Type (DRT) set to 4 (DATUM).

Diverges from Step 4: when passive bearings are ambiguous, C2 JU sets Bearing Report Type (BRT) to value 1 and reports using both the Bearing 1, ASW and Bearing 2, ASW fields of the J5.4E0 and J5.4C1 words, with the origins of both bearings being the same.
Diverges from Step 4: when reporting range to an ASW contact without a bearing, C2 JU sets BRT to value 3 (Range Only) instead of the bearing-and-range report covered in Step 4.

Diverges from Step 3: when an Emergency (EMG) or Force Tell (FT) alert is active, C2 JU sets the EMG IND or FT IND to 1 in the J3.4 Subsurface Track message; this is triggered by a J7.0 message (ACT=3 for EMG, ACT=4 for FT).

Diverges from Step 4: when an Emergency (EMG) or Force Tell (FT) alert is active, C2 JU sets the EMG IND or FT IND to 1 in the J5.4 Acoustic Bearing/Range message; this is triggered by a J7.0 message (ACT=3 for EMG, ACT=4 for FT).

exception_flow.content: Diverges from main flow Step 3 when C2 JU finds a correlation with a track for which it has R² responsibility: C2 JU transmits a J7.2 Correlation message with Response Value (RV) set to 1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), ceases reporting the track, and transmits a J7.0 Drop Track message. Exit: C2 JU ceases reporting that track and sends the drop-track message.

Diverges from main flow Step 3 when C2 JU determines that a Subsurface IU is no longer active on the interface and C2 JU also holds local data on that IU: C2 JU assumes R² by reporting a J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track message using the inactive IU address as the reference TN; when assuming R² under these conditions, C2 JU reports Identity as Friend, maintains previous Track Number/Platform values, and sets the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator to value 1. Exit: the inactive IU is reported as a subsurface track under assumed R².

Diverges from main flow Step 3 when an inactive IU that C2 JU is reporting under assumed R² returns to the interface as an Active IU: C2 JU ceases reporting the IU and does not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message. Exit: C2 JU stops reporting that IU without sending a drop-track message.

Diverges from main flow Step 3 when contact is regained after a DATUM has been reported: C2 JU reports a J3.4 message with Data Report Type (DRT) set to value 0, 1, or 2 using the same TN as the DATUM, or assigns a new TN depending on operator action. Exit: C2 JU reports the regained contact via J3.4 with DRT set to 0, 1, or 2.

postconditions.content: The C2 JU has published a subsurface surveillance or acoustic contact report containing bearings, ranges, and track data derived from ASW sensors.
All reported subsurface surveillance and acoustic data in the published report are time tagged.
The C2 JU holds R² for the reported subsurface track using the assigned Track Number.
If a track is reported as a DATUM after contact is lost, the track does not move; last known course and speed are retained only for calculation of DATUM Error and ASW search data.
A reported DATUM remains in the system until it is dropped or purged by operator action.

use_case_name: Publish Subsurface Surveillance and Acoustic Contact Reports

goal.content: To report subsurface surveillance tracks and acoustic bearings/ranges derived from ASW sensors via J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track and J5.4 Acoustic Bearing/Range messages.

preconditions.content: Tactically significant subsurface surveillance information derived from ASW sensors (bearings, ranges, or tracks) is available to be exchanged.
For subsurface track reporting, the source of track data is available for the Source TN and all data to be reported are time tagged.

For acoustic bearing/range reporting, bearing/range information derived from ASW sensors is available, and the position of the acoustic bearing origin and the applicable Origin TN for the detecting sensor are known.

Where a subsurface track is reported under a Track Number, the C2 JU has assumed reporting responsibility for that Track Number because it was the first JU to report the contact, or one of the allowed exceptions applies (a J7.0 Drop Track message containing the TN has been received, or a J3.4 message containing the TN has not been received for two consecutive periodic updates).

trigger.content: Tactically significant subsurface surveillance information derived from ASW sensors—an established local track at the next reporting opportunity or acoustic bearing/range information—is to be exchanged.

main_flow.content: C² JU provides the source of track data as the Source TN.
C² JU time tags all Subsurface surveillance track data.
C² JU reports established local tracks with all known parameters at the next reporting opportunity using the J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track message.
C² JU reports the geodetic latitude and longitude for each Subsurface surveillance track in the J3.4 message and specifies depth when available.
C² JU reports the velocity of Subsurface surveillance tracks as course and speed, with speed in data miles per hour of ground speed and course in degrees with respect to true north.
C² JU exchanges track identity using the Identity field and may report Platform and Platform Activity in the J3.4I message.
C² JU uses the J5.4 Acoustic Bearing/Range message to exchange information on bearings (ambiguous and resolved) and/or range derived from ASW sensors.
C² JU sets the J5.4E0 Latitude and Longitude fields to the position of the acoustic bearing origin and reports bearings from the detecting sensor origin.

If the detecting sensor is integral to the reporting JU, C² JU sets the J5.4C2 Origin TN field to the TN of the reporting JU (a towed array is considered integral to the ship); if the detecting sensor is integral to another unit, track, or point being reported, C² JU sets the Origin TN field to the TN of the detecting unit, track, or point.

alternative_flow.content: 2a. If contact is lost and the operator decides to report the track as a DATUM, C² JU reports a J3.4 message with the same Reference TN as the track for which contact has been lost, sets Data Report Type (DRT) = 4 (DATUM), sets ASW Time Function = 3 (Time Contact Lost) or 1 (Time Datum Established), sets Hour and Minute to the truncated time contact was lost or DATUM established, and includes Latitude, Longitude, and 15 Meters Depth; the decision to report a DATUM is an operator function.
2b. If contact is regained after a DATUM, C² JU reports a J3.4 with DRT set to value 0, 1, or 2 using the same TN as the DATUM, or a new TN depending on operator action.

2c. If another JU has already reported the contact under a Track Number and either a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message containing the TN is received or a J3.4 message containing the TN has not been received for two consecutive periodic updates, C² JU may report the contact using that track number.

2d. If C² JU believes a contact is the same contact reported by another JU using a different TN, C² JU may report it using a different TN; when this is done, only locally derived data shall be reported in the J3.4 message, and the J3.4 messages shall not contain data derived only by the reception of remote data from other IU(s) reporting the same contact.

2e. If C² JU determines that a Subsurface IU is no longer active on the interface and C² JU also holds local data on the IU, C² JU assumes R² by reporting a J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track message using the inactive IU address as the reference TN.
2f. If further refined information concerning a subsurface fix or one of the other ASW points may result in a Subsurface surveillance track, C² JU reports the track with a new TN.

2g. When associating Subsurface surveillance data, C² JU performs manual correlation of Subsurface surveillance data; the correlation procedures specified for Air, Surface (Maritime), or Land (Ground) tracks are not applied to Subsurface tracks.
2h. If operational necessity requires a shorter wait time or none at all, an override is allowed; system design should also allow for longer wait times.

exception_flow.content: 1. If contact is lost while reporting a Subsurface surveillance track and the operator decides to report the track as a DATUM, C² JU reports a J3.4 message with the same Reference TN as the track for which contact has been lost, sets Data Report Type (DRT) = 4 (DATUM), sets ASW Time Function = 3 (Time Contact Lost) or 1 (Time Datum Established), sets Hour and Minute to the truncated time contact was lost or DATUM established, and includes Latitude, Longitude, and 15 Meters Depth; the decision to report a DATUM is an operator function. Exit: the DATUM report is sent as a J3.4 message.

2. If contact is regained after a DATUM, C² JU reports a J3.4 with DRT set to value 0, 1, or 2 using the same TN as the DATUM, or a new TN depending on operator action. Exit: contact reporting resumes with the selected DRT and TN.

3. If C² JU is not the first JU to report a contact and neither allowed exception occurs (a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message containing the TN is received, or a J3.4 message containing the TN is not received for two consecutive periodic updates), C² JU shall not report the contact using that track number. Exit: C² JU may report what it believes to be the same contact using a different TN, and when this is done only locally derived data shall be reported in the J3.4 message.

4. If C² JU determines that a Subsurface IU is no longer active on the interface and C² JU also holds local data on the IU, C² JU assumes R² by reporting a J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track message using the inactive IU address as the reference TN. Exit: the J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track message using the inactive IU address as the reference TN is sent.

postconditions.content: Subsurface surveillance track information has been reported using the J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track message.
Acoustic bearing/range information derived from ASW sensors has been exchanged using the Acoustic Bearing/Range message.

For reported Subsurface surveillance tracks, the source of track data has been provided as the Source TN; established local tracks have been reported with all known parameters at the next reporting opportunity; and all data have been time tagged.
The information on the track is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible, and the proper rules for reporting a track have been followed.

For the Acoustic Bearing/Range report, the J5.4E0 Latitude and Longitude fields have been set to the position of the acoustic bearing origin, and bearings have been reported from the detecting sensor origin.

For the Acoustic Bearing/Range report, if the detecting sensor is integral to the reporting JU, the J5.4C2 Origin TN field contains the TN of the reporting JU (a towed array is considered integral to the ship); if the detecting sensor is integral to another unit, track, or point being reported, the Origin TN field contains the TN of the detecting unit, track, or point.

If contact was lost and the operator decided to report the track as a DATUM, a J3.4 message has been reported with the same Reference TN as the track for which contact has been lost, DRT = 4 (DATUM), ASW Time Function = 3 (Time Contact Lost) or 1 (Time Datum Established), Hour and Minute set to the truncated time contact was lost or DATUM established, and Latitude, Longitude, and 15 Meters Depth included.
If contact was regained after a DATUM, a J3.4 message has been reported with DRT set to value 0, 1, or 2 using the same TN as the DATUM, or a new TN depending on operator action.

If C² JU determined that a Subsurface IU is no longer active on the interface and C² JU also holds local data on the IU, C² JU has assumed R² by reporting a J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track message using the inactive IU address as the reference TN.

When C² JU reported what it believes to be the same contact using a different TN, only locally derived data have been reported in the J3.4 message, and the J3.4 messages do not contain data derived only by the reception of remote data from other IU(s) reporting the same contact.
If C² JU was the first JU to report a contact, C² JU has assumed reporting responsibility for that Track Number.

use_case_name: Publish Subsurface Surveillance and Acoustic Contact Reports

goal.content: To exchange subsurface surveillance information and acoustic contact reports between JUs using the J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track message in accordance with Link 16 network requirements.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU is participating in the exchange of J3 Surveillance messages on the Link 16 network.
The C2 JU has achieved Active status, or has returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
Sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration have been performed for air, surface, or land tracks (if applicable).
The minimum wait time before transmitting tracks has elapsed: 12 seconds for air and surface tracks, or 48 seconds for land tracks.
Subsurface surveillance track information is available and meets reporting criteria for exchange between JUs involved in joint operations.
Acoustic bearing/range data derived from ASW sensors is available for reporting via J5.4 message if applicable.

trigger.content: The C2 JU acquires subsurface surveillance track data or acoustic contact information that meets the reporting criteria for exchange between JUs involved in joint operations.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU transmits surveillance information in Network PGs as defined for J3 Surveillance messages.
The C2 JU reports the geodetic latitude and longitude for each Subsurface surveillance track in the J3.4 message.
If available, the C2 JU specifies depth in the Subsurface surveillance reporting.
The C2 JU reports the velocity of Subsurface surveillance tracks as course and speed.
The speed is reported in data miles per hour of ground speed.
The course is reported in degrees with respect to true north.
The C2 JU exchanges Track identity using the Identity field.
Platform and Platform Activity may be reported in the J3.4I message to further amplify the identity of the reported track.
Discrete Identifier Codes (Special) are reported in the J7.5 message.
The time is set to the time contact was first acquired/time datum established, the time of current positional data, or the time contact was lost.
This time is reported in the Hour; Minute; and Time Function, ASW fields of the J3.4C1 word.

exception_flow.content: If Track Quality data is included in the report, the C2 JU must exclude it because Track quality is not applicable to Subsurface surveillance.

If the system detects potential overloading of the terminal-to-host interface or high TDS processor demands, the C2 JU may apply Message label/sublabel filters to inhibit specific messages from being forwarded to the Host TDS.
If data link overload conditions, system database overload, or undesired data entry risks are detected, the C2 JU may activate Data filters (transmit or receive filters) to inhibit the flow of data.

postconditions.content: Subsurface surveillance track information has been exchanged between JUs using the J3.4 Subsurface (Maritime) Track message.
Geodetic latitude and longitude for each Subsurface surveillance track have been reported in the J3.4 message.
Depth has been specified in the Subsurface surveillance reporting if available.
Velocity of Subsurface surveillance tracks has been reported as course and speed, with speed in data miles per hour of ground speed and course in degrees with respect to true north.
Track identity has been exchanged using the Identity field, with optional amplification via Platform and Platform Activity in the J3.4I message.
Discrete Identifier Codes (Special) have been reported in the J7.5 message in accordance with paragraph 4.7.6.5.
Time of contact acquisition, current positional data, or loss has been reported in the Hour; Minute; and Time Function, ASW fields of the J3.4C1 word.
Track quality data has not been included in the report, as it is not applicable to Subsurface surveillance.

use_case_name: Publish Subsurface Surveillance and Acoustic Contact Reports

goal.content: Enable C2 JU to publish accurate, timely, correlated subsurface surveillance and acoustic contact reports per MIL-STD-6016B.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU has initially achieved Active status, or has returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
Sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration have been performed for the tracks to be reported.
For air and surface tracks, a minimum wait time of 12 seconds has elapsed since achieving/returning to Active status; for land tracks, 48 seconds has elapsed.

trigger.content: The decision to report a DATUM shall be an operator function, or contact is lost requiring track reporting per established criteria.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU determines that a subsurface surveillance track or acoustic contact meets reporting criteria based on completeness, accuracy, timeliness, and proper rules for track reporting.
If reporting a DATUM due to lost contact, the C2 JU operator initiates the report as an operator function.

The C2 JU reports the DATUM in a J3.4 message with Reference TN set to the track for which contact was lost, and includes: Data Report Type (DRPT = 4), ASM Time Function = 3 (Time Contact Lost) or 1 (Time Datum Established), Hour and Minute of loss/establishment, and Latitude, Longitude, 15 Meters Depth, and Depth Contact at last known position.
For established local tracks, the C2 JU reports all known parameters at the next reporting opportunity, ensuring source data is provided via Source TN.
All reported data shall be time tagged.
For acoustic bearing/range information, the C2 JU uses J5.4 messages to exchange bearings (ambiguous and resolved) and/or range derived from ASW sensors, without requiring source frequency reporting.
In J5.4 messages, latitude and longitude fields are set to the position of the acoustic bearing origin.
If the detecting sensor is integral to the reporting JU, the Origin TN field contains the TN of the reporting JU; if integral to another unit, track, or point, it contains the TN of that entity.
Positional data (geodetic latitude and longitude) for each subsurface surveillance track is reported in the J3.x message, including depth when available.
Velocity of subsurface surveillance tracks is reported as course and speed in data miles per hour, with course in degrees relative to true north.
Track identity is exchanged using the Identity field; Platform and Platform Activity may also be reported in the J3.41 message per paragraph 4.4.9.1.1.
Discrete Identifier Codes (Special) are reported in the J7.5 message per paragraph 4.7.6.5.

Time reported is the time contact was first acquired/time datum established, current positional data time, or time contact was lost — reported in Hour, Minute, and Time Function, ASW fields of the J3.4C1 word.

alternative_flow.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which the C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (R2 = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the header word of the J2 PDL message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.

If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PDL information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geosetic Position Quality in the PDL message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PDL message shall be discarded.
Subsurface tracks shall not be correlated with IDs.

System design should allow for longer wait times as well as an override in cases where operational necessity requires a shorter wait time or none at all for reporting air and surface tracks after achieving Active status.

exception_flow.content: If the C2 JU is not in Active status (e.g., Inactive or TDS Failure), it shall not transmit air, surface, or land tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed.
For air and surface tracks, if less than 12 seconds have elapsed since achieving/returning to Active status, track transmission is prohibited unless overridden by operational necessity.
For land tracks, if less than 48 seconds have elapsed since achieving/returning to Active status, track transmission is prohibited unless overridden by operational necessity.

If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is transmitted for EW product information termination, remote reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria, but the J7.0 message itself shall not be retransmitted.

If Geosetic Position Quality in a PDL message is set to value 0 during correlation with an existing track having same TN, the surveillance track is accepted and the PDL message shall be discarded — this constitutes an exception to normal PDL acceptance logic.

use_case_name: Publish Subsurface Surveillance and Acoustic Contact Reports

goal.content: The C2 JU publishes subsurface surveillance and acoustic contact reports by exchanging tactically significant information derived from ASW sensors using J3.0, J3.4, and J5.4 messages to report bearings, ranges, tracks, and datum in accordance with specific reporting criteria and responsibility rules.

preconditions.content: The information on the subsurface track must be as complete, accurate, and timely as possible before reporting.

Proper rules for reporting a subsurface track must be followed, including providing source track data (Source TN), reporting established local tracks with all known parameters at the next opportunity, and time-tagging all data.

Reporting responsibility (R²) for a subsurface contact must be established; the first JU to report assumes responsibility unless a Drop Track message is received or no update is received for two consecutive periods.
Subsurface surveillance reports shall include geodetic latitude and longitude in the J3.4 message, and may include depth when available.
Velocity of subsurface tracks shall be reported as course (degrees true north) and speed (data miles per hour ground speed).
Time of contact acquisition, datum establishment, current position, or loss shall be reported in Hour, Minute, and Time Function fields of the J3.4C1 word.

trigger.content: A C2 JU detects or acquires a subsurface contact requiring reporting, or receives acoustic bearing/range data from ASW sensors that must be exchanged as tactically significant information.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU uses J3.0, J3.4, and J5.4 messages to exchange tactically significant information derived from ASW sensors to report bearings, ranges, and tracks.

When reporting a subsurface track, the C2 JU must provide the source of track data (Source TN), report established local tracks with all known parameters at the next opportunity, and ensure all data is time-tagged.

The first JU to report a contact assumes reporting responsibility (R²) for that Track Number; no other JU shall report the contact using that track number unless a Drop Track message is received or no update is received for two consecutive periods.

If the detecting sensor is integral to the reporting JU, the Origin TN field in the J5.4 message shall contain the TN of the reporting JU; if integral to another unit, it shall contain the TN of the detecting unit.
When contact is lost, the C2 JU may report the track as a DATUM in a J3.4 message with Data Report Type (DRT) = 4, including the last known position and time contact was lost.

alternative_flow.content: If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received containing the Track Number, another JU may report the contact using that Track Number.
If a J3.4 message containing the Track Number is not received for two consecutive periodic updates, another JU may assume reporting responsibility and report the contact using that Track Number.
Any other JU may report what it believes to be the same subsurface contact using a different Track Number, but shall only include locally derived data in the J3.4 message.

When contact is lost, the decision to report a DATUM is an operator function, and the DATUM is reported in a J3.4 message with Data Report Type (DRT) = 4, using the same Reference TN as the lost track.
In the DATUM report, the ASW Time Function is set to 3 (Time Contact Lost) or 1 (Time Datum Established), and Hour/Minute fields contain the truncated time contact was lost or DATUM established.
The DATUM report includes latitude, longitude, 15 meters depth, and depth contact fields set to the last known position of the contact.
Although last known course and speed are reported in the DATUM, the DATUM itself shall not move; these values are used only for DATUM Error calculation and ASW search planning.
If contact is regained, a J3.4 message with DRT set to 0, 1, or 2 shall be reported with the same TN as the DATUM, or a new TN depending on operator action.
A DATUM shall only be dropped or purged by explicit operator action.

When a JU determines a Subsurface Interface Unit (IU) is no longer active and holds local data on it, the JU assumes reporting responsibility by reporting a J3.4 Subsurface Track message using the inactive IU address as the reference TN.
If the inactive IU returns to active status, the JU holding reporting responsibility shall cease reporting the IU, but shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

exception_flow.content: If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received containing the Track Number, another JU may report the contact using that Track Number.
If a J3.4 message containing the Track Number is not received for two consecutive periodic updates, another JU may assume reporting responsibility and report the contact using that Track Number.

When contact is lost, the decision to report a DATUM is an operator function; if chosen, it is reported in a J3.4 message with Data Report Type (DRT) = 4, using the same Reference TN as the lost track.
In the DATUM report, the ASW Time Function is set to 3 (Time Contact Lost) or 1 (Time Datum Established), and Hour/Minute fields contain the truncated time contact was lost or DATUM established.

The DATUM report includes latitude, longitude, 15 meters depth, and depth contact fields set to the last known position of the contact; although last known course and speed are reported, the DATUM itself shall not move.
A DATUM shall only be dropped or purged by explicit operator action.
If contact is regained, a J3.4 message with DRT set to 0, 1, or 2 shall be reported with the same TN as the DATUM, or a new TN depending on operator action.

postconditions.content: The information on the subsurface track is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible.

Proper rules for reporting a subsurface track have been followed, including providing source track data (Source TN), reporting established local tracks with all known parameters at the next opportunity, and time-tagging all data.

Reporting responsibility (R²) for the subsurface contact has been established; the first JU to report assumes responsibility unless a Drop Track message is received or no update is received for two consecutive periods.
Subsurface surveillance reports include geodetic latitude and longitude in the J3.4 message, and may include depth when available.

goal.content: To resolve differences in Environment/Category, Identity, Exercise Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator field values for a track received from another unit.

preconditions.content: A track report has been received containing a PPLI Track Number.
The Identity Indicator in the received track report is set to value 1.
The new identity contained in the track report is Friend.
The locally held identity for the track is not Hostile.

trigger.content: A C2 JU elects to accept, automatically, changes in Environment/Category, Identity or Exercise Indicator received in a track report with the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1, provided the new identity is Friend and the locally held identity is not Hostile.

main_flow.content: The C2 JU accepts the changes in Environment/Category, Identity, or Exercise Indicator received in the track report.
The C2 JU evaluates the Platform/Platform Activity/Specific Type and Special Interest Indicator field values for difference resolution.

If a change in the ID of the track is accepted, the C2 JU includes the appropriate evaluation of the Platform/Platform Activity/Specific Type and Special Interest Indicator fields in the J3.X or J7.0 (ACT = 1) message.

When accepting a remote ID change, the C2 JU retains the received values of the Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator fields for retransmission and operator appreciation.

alternative_flow.content: If the C2 JU is a controlling unit, it shall follow the rules specified in paragraphs 4.7.1.2.2b and c regarding Platform/Platform Activity/Specific Type difference resolution.

If a Platform, Platform Activity or Specific Type value of 0 (No Statement) is received and a non-zero value is held locally, the C2 JU does not retain the received zero value during the resolution of differences.
If an Air Platform value of 6 (Tanker), 7 (Tanker (Boom Only)), or 8 (Tanker (Drogue Only)) is held locally and a different value is received, the C2 JU may optionally generate an operator alert.

exception_flow.content: If a Platform, Platform Activity or Specific Type value of 0 (No Statement) is received and a non-zero value is held locally, the C2 JU does not retain the received zero value during the resolution of differences.
If an Air Platform value of 6 (Tanker), 7 (Tanker (Boom Only)), or 8 (Tanker (Drogue Only)) is held locally and a different value is received, the C2 JU may optionally generate an operator alert.

postconditions.content: The C2 JU has accepted the changes in Environment/Category, Identity, or Exercise Indicator from the received track report.

preconditions.content: A C² JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

All C² JUs capable of reporting air or surface tracks shall have the capability to transmit and receive all the response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks, which are held locally by their system.

trigger.content: A C² JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

main_flow.content: The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² JUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
The message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

The receiving JUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving JU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
The originating JU indicates in the J7.2 message if it has any constraints which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation.

alternative_flow.content: The receiving JU may reject the requested correlation if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode I codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.

If the use of automatic restriction capability changes, all participating C² JUs will be informed through voice communication or other communications media. In lieu of specific interface direction, all JUs will restrict automatic correlation by default.

Systems shall have an initialization parameter and an operator selectable capability to inhibit automatic restriction. Use of this capability will be subject to interface coordination and must be promulgated to all C² JUs.
A C² JU shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the listed conditions exist. These restrictions do not apply to manual correlation.

exception_flow.content: If the two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict, the correlation shall be rejected.
If one track is simulated and the other is live, the correlation shall be rejected.
If both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, the correlation shall be rejected.
When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
An operator alert in the event of the rejection of an automatic correlation shall be a system option.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU is participating in the exchange of J3 Surveillance messages on the Link 16 network.

trigger.content: Receipt of a J7.1 (ACT = 1) message on a specific TN.

main_flow.content: The requesting JU initiates the J7.1 (ACT = 1 or 2) message with the specific TN in the Reference TN field and addressed to a specific Addressee TN(s) or to the collective address of 00177 octal.

Upon receipt of a J7.1 (ACT = 1) message on a specific TN, the JU that have originated surveillance amplification data on the track shall respond with the J6.0 Amplification message containing all available data.

Upon receipt of a J7.1 (ACT = 1) message on a specific TN, the JU controlling the TN shall transmit the appropriate J10 Weapons Coordination and Management messages and J13 Platform and System Status messages to include the J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message, the J10.2 Engagement Status message, and the appropriate J13 Platform and System Status messages.

All C2 JUs receiving a J7.1 (ACT = 1) message containing their own TN shall transmit J10.2 Engagement Status messages to report the status of all engagements they are conducting and a J13 Platform and System Status message to report their own status.

goal.content: To allow a C2 JU to filter tracks and nonC² IUs based on their geographic location by defining geographic filters such as circles, annuli, sectors, rectangles, lines, or nested rectangles.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU must have defined the geographic filter parameters (e.g., latitude/longitude origin, major/minor axes, bearings) according to the specific geometry type (Circle, Annulus, Sector, Rectangle, Line, etc.) as specified in Table 4.7-6.

Voice coordination must be established in addition to the filter message to ensure filter management on the interface.

trigger.content: A C2 JU decides to filter tracks and nonC² IUs based on their geographic location.

If the filter is a Line or Area requiring multiple messages, the C2 JU treats all messages with the same filter number as a single filter report.

Voice coordination is established in addition to the filter message to ensure proper filter management on the interface.

Filter management on the interface is ensured through the established voice coordination in addition to the transmitted filter message.

goal.content: A J7.3 message provides the capability for C² JUs to designate a geographic position and up to twenty characters of text on one or more C² JU's displays.

preconditions.content: The C2 JU has a geographic position to designate.

The target display unit(s) (one or more C² JU's displays) are available to receive the J7.3 message.
If addressing multiple JUs, the system is prepared to construct J7.3C1 Pointer Additional Addresses continuation words as needed.
If specifying operator positions by function within a JU, the pointer action data element is available for use.

trigger.content: The C2 JU initiates the transmission of a J7.3 message to designate a geographic position and up to twenty characters of text on one or more C² JU's displays.

If the message is addressed to one JU, the C2 JU places the specific address in the J7.3I Pointer initial word.

If more than five addresses are required, the C2 JU sends multiple J7.3C1 words.

The C2 JU uses the J7.3C2 and J7.3C3 words to provide amplifying textual information of up to twenty characters.
If specifying operator positions by function within a JU, the C2 JU uses the pointer action data element.
The C2 JU transmits the J7.3 message; since no TN is assigned to the pointer, it must be displayed and dropped by local procedure at the receiving unit(s).

postconditions.content: The geographic position and up to twenty characters of text are displayed on the designated C² JU's displays.

If addressed to multiple JUs, the J7.3I word contains one address and J7.3C1 Pointer Additional Addresses continuation words contain up to four additional addresses per word; multiple J7.3C1 words may be sent for more than five addresses.
If addressed to all JUs, the collective address is contained in the J7.3I word.
Amplifying textual information of up to twenty characters is provided via J7.3C2 and J7.3C3 words.

goal.content: To create a system-generated batch of vouchers with unique identification numbers, security protocols, and barcodes, and print them in a tear-off slip format for distribution.

preconditions.content: The VMU User must be an authorized user with system-level access to create vouchers.
The system must have the capability to generate unique voucher identification numbers with built-in security protocols.
The system must be configured to print vouchers in bar-code format, including batch number, voucher number, and security code.
The system must support printing vouchers as three tear-off portioned slips with sub-sections for partner use.
The management team must have defined the minimum quantity of vouchers that can be created at one time.

trigger.content: An authorized user initiates the creation of a minimum quantity of vouchers at one time.

main_flow.content: The VMU User initiates the creation of a voucher batch, specifying a quantity that meets or exceeds the minimum number defined by the management team.

The system formats the voucher data including Project code, Group batch code, Batch number, Voucher number, and Security code.
The system prepares the voucher output as three tear-off portioned slips with a sub-section tear-off for the partner.

The system includes validity date information on the vouchers, which can be amended only at the system level by an authorized user.

Voucher validity date and MRP are embedded in the printed output; validity date can only be amended at system level by authorized user post-printing.

use_case_name: Generate Treatment Quality and Trend Reports

goal.content: The MSIU Field Office User wants to generate treatment quality and trend reports as specified in the MSIU Project Document 'Programme Design Study'.

preconditions.content: The MSIU office has processed the collected claim forms from the VSP.

The system contains the treatment quality and trend data required for the reports, including frequencies of syndromes treated (with patient population sex and age), primary clients, notified partners, correctly documented cases, treatment errors, and provider comparisons.

trigger.content: The system generates reports on treatment quality and trends.

The system permits the report/print option according to the user's login permission.
The system passes data from the Database to the Reports module, including output from claim processing.

The system generates treatment quality and trend reports as specified in the MSIU Project Document 'Programme Design Study', including summaries of all providers, quarterly summary reports per provider and summarizing all providers, frequencies of syndromes treated, patient population sex and age, frequencies of primary clients and notified partners, numbers of correctly documented cases, cases with incorrect documentation, cases treated according to algorithms, cases with justified treatment alterations, treatment errors, provider comparisons regarding syndromes treated, documentation quality, and treatment behaviour, and quarterly and half-yearly time-trend reports for each provider and all providers combined.

Diverges from Step 4: the system generates an analytical, medical, or statistical report variant, rather than the standard report specified in the Programme Design Study.

postconditions.content: Treatment quality and trend reports have been generated as specified in the MSIU Project Document 'Programme Design Study'.

If the MSIU Field Office User has the specific 'User Login Permission' for printing, the system provides an option to print the generated report.

use_case_name: Generate Treatment Quality and Trend Reports

goal.content: To generate reports on treatment quality and trends based on client feedback and treatment data to monitor proper operation of the voucher scheme and support future planning by the MSIU Admin team.

preconditions.content: The MSIU team must have collected client feedback from clients who received treatment through the voucher system.
Data regarding syndromes treated, lab tests, and drugs details must be captured in the Client Feedback form.
Information from manual claim forms must have been entered into the computer database.
Mandatory information required for claims (such as thumb impression and voucher slip) must be complete in the system.

trigger.content: The MSIU Field Office User initiates the report generation process to monitor proper operation of the voucher scheme and support future planning.

main_flow.content: The MSIU Field Office User accesses the Reports module within the Voucher Management System.
The system retrieves treatment data, including Syndrome, Clinical Examinations, Diagnosis, Lab Test, and Drugs details, from the Database based on the MSIU Treatment Matrix.
The system retrieves Client Feedback data associated with the treated voucher cases from the Database.
The system aggregates the treatment quality metrics and trend data derived from the clinical information and client feedback.
The system generates the Treatment Quality and Trend Reports for the MSIU Admin team to review.

alternative_flow.content: If the user enters incorrect Voucher Numbers during data entry or report parameter selection, the system may fail to automatically populate details of syndromes treated, lab tests, drugs details, success of treatment, referral to treatment, or partner treated.
If mandatory information is incomplete (e.g., missing thumb impression or voucher slip), the system will not accept the claims, preventing the generation of reports based on that data.

exception_flow.content: If the mandatory information required for claims is not complete (e.g., missing thumb impression or voucher slip), the system will not accept the claims, thereby preventing the generation of reports based on that incomplete data.

If the user enters incorrect Voucher Numbers during data entry or report parameter selection, the system may fail to retrieve and populate details such as syndromes treated, lab tests, drugs details, success of treatment, referral to treatment, or partner treated, leading to incomplete or inaccurate reports.

postconditions.content: The system displays the generated Treatment Quality and Trend Reports to the MSIU Field Office User.
The reports contain aggregated data on treatment quality metrics derived from clinical information (Syndrome, Diagnosis, Lab Test, Drugs) and client feedback.
The reports provide trend analysis to support future planning by the MSIU Admin team.
The reports enable monitoring of the proper operation of the voucher scheme.

goal.content: To maintain records of service providers who treat voucher clients and submit claims for reimbursement via the VMU system.

preconditions.content: The VMU User must be logged into the system with appropriate user privileges to access service provider maintenance functions.
The system must have existing User Groups and Individual Users configured, as only the system admin can create User Groups and individual users under them.
The system must be running on the Oracle 9i platform with VB front end and Crystal Reports 9 for reporting capabilities.
High intrusion controls and access level controls must be in place in the system and database, including granular model settings for organizational level user access.

trigger.content: A VMU User initiates the process to add, edit, or delete service provider records in the system.

main_flow.content: The VMU User accesses the service provider maintenance screen within the system.
The system displays options for New (adding new records), Edit (updating available records), and Delete (deleting records if no child records are created).
If adding a new service provider, the VMU User enters mandatory information including Group Name (selected from existing User Groups), User Name, Password, and Verify Password.
The system validates that the Password and Verify Password values are equal before saving the user information.
The system checks that the User Name does not already exist to prevent duplicate names.
The system saves the service provider record only if all validation checks pass.
If editing an existing service provider, the VMU User selects the record and updates allowable fields; the system enforces access level controls based on the user’s privileges.
If deleting a service provider, the system verifies that no child records (e.g., claims or transactions) have been created for that provider before allowing deletion.
The system logs the action and updates the database with sequential links and surrogate keys to maintain storage efficiency.

exception_flow.content: If the Password and Verify Password values are not equal, the system shall not save the user information and shall prompt the VMU User to re-enter matching passwords.
If the VMU User attempts to create a User Group or Individual User with an existing name, the system shall reject the creation and notify the user of the duplicate name error.

If the VMU User attempts to delete a service provider record that has associated child records (e.g., claims or transactions), the system shall prevent deletion and display an error indicating dependent records exist.

If the VMU User lacks appropriate access level privileges for editing or deleting a specific service provider record, the system shall deny the action based on granular model settings and organizational level user controls.

postconditions.content: The service provider record is successfully added, updated, or deleted in the database with sequential links and surrogate keys to ensure storage efficiency.

Access level controls and granular model settings are enforced for all modifications, ensuring only authorized VMU Users can perform specific actions on service provider records.

Deletion of a service provider record is permitted only if no child records (e.g., claims or transactions) have been created for that provider.

goal.content: To enable the VMU to investigate and clear conspicuous claims as part of the monitoring system.

preconditions.content: The data from the forms is entered into a computer database.
Data checks and plausibilisations are done.
The system has provisions for user access controls, including granular model settings.

trigger.content: A claim is entered into the system and undergoes data checks and plausibilisations, resulting in a conspicuous status requiring investigation by the VMU.

main_flow.content: The VMU User accesses the system to review claims that have been flagged as conspicuous following data checks and plausibilisations.

The system displays master information for the claim, including Submitted Date, VSP Name, Voucher No, Visit Count, Patient Type, Patient Name, Age, Gender, Address, Contact No, Doctor Name, Doctors Note, HIV Details if any, Patient Status, Claim Amount, and Claim Status.
The VMU User reviews transaction details of the claim, which may include information related to first-time consultation or other service provisions.

The VMU User utilizes reference masters such as Drugs Master, Syndrome Master, Clinical Examination Master, Diagnosis Master, Lab Test Master, Other Measure Master, Patient Status Master, and Claim Status Master to validate and understand the claim components.
Based on the review, the VMU User determines whether the claim is legitimate or requires further action, in alignment with the system’s function to control fraud and ensure timely payments.
If the claim is cleared, the system updates the Claim Status accordingly; if not, it remains under investigation or is escalated per monitoring protocols.

exception_flow.content: If the VMU User attempts to access a claim without appropriate access level controls or organizational user settings, the system denies access due to high intrusion controls and granular model setting enforcement.

If during review, the system detects missing or invalid master data (e.g., undefined Drug Code, Syndrome Code, or Claim Status Code), it flags the claim as incomplete and prevents clearance until corrected.
If the VMU User identifies fraudulent activity during investigation, the claim is not cleared; instead, it remains under investigation per the monitoring system’s protocol for conspicuous claims.

goal.content: To change the system mode.

preconditions.content: The Operator is logged on to the RLCS system.
The Operator has authorization to change the system mode.
Only one 'operator' may be logged onto the system at any given time.

trigger.content: The Operator initiates a command to change the system operating mode.

main_flow.content: The Operator issues a command to change the system mode.
The RLCS application software updates and reads database tables to support system operations.
The system updates the System Mode entity, which includes modes such as Normal, Degraded, Emergency, or Maintenance.
The system logs the change in the System Operation Command Log, recording the date, time, and operator ID.

alternative_flow.content: If the Operator attempts to issue a command without the required security level, the system denies access based on Personnel Security Level attributes (Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions).
If the Operator is not authorized to change the system mode (e.g., Field Maintenance Staff), the system prevents the mode change.
If the system is in a state where mode change is restricted by Device Rules (e.g., Device X desired status conflicts with Device Y prohibited status), the command is rejected.

exception_flow.content: If the Operator attempts to issue a control command with 'Status Only' security level, the system denies the command as this level does not permit issuing any control commands.

If the Operator's Personnel Security Level does not authorize access to the specific System Mode being requested (based on attributes: Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions), the system restricts access.

The system closes the wrong-way longitudinal pop-ups, beginning at the shoulder edge and progressing toward the ramp nose.
Where more than one bank exists, the system closes the wrong-way transverse pop-ups from the reversible lanes toward the freeway.

If the offending device status is not corrected within the configurable time period, no automatic resumption is supported.

At any point in the closing sequence, if the status of a closure device that was previously opened at the current entrance changes to 'unknown' or 'closed' without an operator-initiated command, the closing sequence is halted. If the offending device status can be corrected within the configurable time period, the Operator can issue a resume command so the system attempts to complete the original closing sequence. If the offending device status is not corrected within the configurable time period, no automatic resumption is supported.

During the closing sequence, if the status of a closure device that was previously closed at the current entrance changes to 'unknown' or 'open', the closing sequence is halted. If the offending device status can be corrected within the configurable time period, the Operator can issue a resume command so the system attempts to complete the original closing sequence. If the offending device status is not corrected within the configurable time period, no automatic resumption is supported.

At a device-operation step during the closing sequence (e.g., Step 5), if a device command must be issued outside the predetermined operational event, the Operator with proper security can use Operational Override to issue the device command on demand (exit: the on-demand device command is issued).

postconditions.content: The reversible-lane entrance is in the 'Closed' state.

goal.content: To close a reversible-lane entrance by closing its Entrance devices according to the specified closing sequence.

preconditions.content: The operator has logged on at a control unit console.

trigger.content: The Operator initiates a closing sequence to close the Entrance devices of a reversible-lane entrance.

main_flow.content: The closing sequence closes Entrance devices in the following order: CMS.
CMS messages are changed from “Open” to “Closed” beginning with the farthest upstream sign (furthest away from the entrance) and proceeding, in order, downstream (towards the entrance).

The system provides a specific delay between the message change on each sign and the message change on the next downstream sign; the delay for each sign pair equals the time to travel between the two signs at a system specified speed.

If more than one bank, Entrance Transverse Pop-ups are closed in the direction from the freeway toward the reversible lanes.
Wrong Way Longitudinal Pop-ups are closed beginning at the shoulder edge, and progressing toward the ramp nose, next to the reversible lanes.

exception_flow.content: If the TMC workstations or network server fails, resulting in loss of field status at the TMC, alternate control shall be at FCU South or FCU North; the operator shall be able to dial in from a back up computer to either FCU North or FCU south and open and close the reversible lanes. Exit: alternate control at FCU South or FCU North via back up computer.

If FCU North or South fails (FCU Controller failures or FCU-TSU communications failure), causing loss of changeable messages signs and DCUs associated with the failed FCU, alternate control at the non-failed FCU (North or South). Exit: alternate control at the non-failed FCU.

If FCUs North and South both fail (FCU Controller failures or FCUs-TSU and FCU-FCU communications failure), causing loss of changeable message signs 1-12 and DCUs 1-5, alternate control units: Direct control at DCUs 1-5. Exit: direct control at DCUs 1-5.

goal.content: To diagnose a failed device at the sensor level.

preconditions.content: Field Maintenance Staff are operating in maintenance mode.

trigger.content: The trigger is when the user accesses or uses the diagnostic screen in the GUI.

main_flow.content: Field Maintenance Staff accesses the diagnostic screen to begin diagnosing the failed device.

use_case_name: Initialize a Newly Online Control Unit

goal.content: To initialize a newly online control unit by identifying it, initializing all its associated device sensors, and replicating specific items from the central database server into its non-volatile, non-removable memory.

preconditions.content: The private communications networks established by Department of Transportation District 11 are in place and available to the control unit.

The initialization process has available the data it depends on: Command, Device Description, Device Sensor Status, and Security Level from the Data Processing and Security entity, plus the Device Sensor Initialization Data required by the Identify & Initialize all Devices function.

The central database server is operational and contains the items to be replicated: Login Tables, Closure Device Timing Parameters, Air Calibration Factors, Reversible Lanes Configuration Table(s), and Reversible Lanes Operating Logic, Control Sequences, and Rule Sets.

trigger.content: A control unit becomes newly online and requires initialization.

main_flow.content: When the control unit comes online, the RLCS identifies the control unit and all of its associated device sensors.

The RLCS initializes each control unit and device sensor as it is identified using the Identify & Initialize all Devices function; depending on whether the unit is an FCU or a DCU, this includes initializing the inputs/outputs for the specific device sensors associated with that control unit type.
The RLCS performs a control system integrity check and initializes all specified tables.
The RLCS verifies that all cards required in that control unit are present and working properly.

For each FCU and DCU control unit, the RLCS replicates from the central database server into the control unit's non-volatile, non-removable memory: Login Tables, Closure Device Timing Parameters, Air Calibration Factors, Reversible Lanes Configuration Table(s), Reversible Lanes Operating Logic, Control Sequences, and Rule Sets.

When any of these non-volatile memory items is created or modified during replication, the RLCS appends or updates a UTC date/time stamp as the last step in building the time-stamped code/data section.

The RLCS produces a Message Digest table of one-way hash values for each Control Unit Non-Volatile Memory item and maintains the appropriate Message Digest table in non-volatile memory in the system control unit.

exception_flow.content: At main flow step 3, if the control system integrity check performed during startup fails, successful initialization is prevented and the condition is an exception.
During the startup phase that includes main flow step 3, if the startup process does not complete within 30 seconds, it is considered a failure condition requiring exception handling.

At main flow step 7, if verification of the non-volatile memory items fails, such as when a Message Digest comparison fails, the affected control unit is prevented from being used in control sequences.

postconditions.content: The newly online control unit and all its associated device sensors have been identified.
All associated device sensors for the control unit have been initialized.

The specific items replicated from the central database server—Login Tables, Closure Device Timing Parameters, Air Calibration Factors, Reversible Lanes Configuration Table(s), and Reversible Lanes Operating Logic, Control Sequences, and Rule Sets—are stored and maintained in the control unit's non-volatile, non-removable memory.
For non-volatile memory items created or modified during initialization, a UTC date/time stamp has been updated as the last step in building the time-stamped code/data section.
A Message Digest table containing one-way hash function values for each Control Unit Non-Volatile Memory item is produced and maintained in the system control unit's non-volatile memory.

goal.content: To identify a newly online control unit and all its associated device sensors, and initialize the control unit and device sensors as they are identified.

The RLCS software shall initialize each control unit and device sensor as it is identified.
The RLCS software in the field shall first identify the its unit when it starts, by reading the cabinet id.

use_case_name: Initialize a Newly Online Control Unit

goal.content: The use case ensures that a newly online control unit is identified, initialized with necessary device sensor data, and integrated into the system monitoring loop.

preconditions.content: The Control Unit must be physically connected to the RLCS network and capable of communication.
The RLCS application software must be running and able to process GUI commands and device initialization data.
The system must have access to the logical database containing Device, Device Category, Location, and Device Status entities with their minimum attributes.
The Personnel Security Level entity must be configured to allow appropriate Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions access for initialization operations.
Device Sensor Initialization Data must be available or generatable for the newly online unit.

trigger.content: A newly online Control Unit connects to the RLCS network and sends Device Sensor Initialization Data to initiate identification and integration into the system monitoring loop.

main_flow.content: The Control Unit sends Device Sensor Initialization Data to the system.
The Process GUI Commands function receives and processes the Device Sensor Initialization Data.
The Identify & Initialize all Devices function uses the received data to identify the new unit.
The system retrieves or references stored Device Description, Device Sensor Status, and Security Level information from the Data Processing and Security module.
The Set Alarms function configures alarm criteria for the newly initialized device based on its status and type.
The Monitor Devices function begins tracking the Device Sensor Status of the newly online Control Unit.
The Collect Log Data function records the initialization event and initial device status in the system logs.

exception_flow.content: If the Control Unit fails to send valid Device Sensor Initialization Data, the Process GUI Commands function cannot proceed, and the system logs a Command Failure Count increment via Track # of Failed Device Commands.

If the Identify & Initialize all Devices function cannot match the incoming data to any known Device ID or Device Category in the logical database, initialization is aborted and an alarm may be triggered via Set Alarms based on Device Alarm Criteria.

If the Personnel Security Level entity does not permit the required Command Level (e.g., ‘Control’ or ‘Override’) for initializing devices, the system denies initialization and records the failure in Device Command Log with Operator ID and timeout status.

If the newly online unit’s Device Status ID corresponds to an invalid or prohibited state (e.g., ‘alarm’ without clearance), the Monitor Devices function flags it as failed and triggers retry logic via Control Devices using Command Data (for retry).

If the Collect Log Data function cannot write the initialization event due to database lock or full log capacity, the System Operation Command Log entity records the failure with Date, Time, and System Operational Command ID for audit recovery.

postconditions.content: The newly online Control Unit is successfully identified and initialized within the RLCS system, with its Device Sensor Status integrated into the Monitor Devices function.
Device Sensor Initialization Data for the new unit has been processed and stored, enabling subsequent command and monitoring operations.
Alarm criteria have been set for the newly initialized device based on its Device Alarm Criteria entity attributes (e.g., Alarm low/high range, Description).
The initialization event and initial device status are recorded in the system logs via the Collect Log Data function, ensuring audit trail compliance.
The Personnel Security Level entity confirms that appropriate Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions access rights are assigned or validated for the initialized unit.

goal.content: To monitor facility and device status.

preconditions.content: The Operator is logged on.
