trigger.content: The Operator accesses the facility and device status display.

main_flow.content: The Operator accesses the facility and device status display.
The system presents a GUI display of the I-15 Reversible Lane Control System facility geographic area, including the layout of the mainline I-15 and SR-163 freeway area.

The system displays facility status information, including facility status (e.g., Open or Closed), current direction of traffic flow, customer eligibility, and current facility boundaries extending one mile in either direction.
The system displays device sensor status using dynamic icons for all field device sensors and controllers.
The system receives current device status information from field devices within 2 seconds of the status being issued.
The system checks each received status against alarm conditions for that device sensor and updates the status to indicate an alarm when an alarm condition exists.
The system refreshes the status display every 2 seconds.
The Operator views the current facility and device status information, including displayed alarm conditions and override states, on the GUI.

The GUI provides the ability to display the status of one device at the detail level, showing all sensor data for that device, and to display the current status of a category of devices at the detail level, showing all sensor data for all devices of the same category.

alternative_flow.content: When a device status has been overridden to continue an operating sequence after an intermediate device control failure, the system displays that overridden device status on the screen with a color different from the normal and alarm status colors, and the operating sequence continues to the end.

exception_flow.content: Exception 1 — Divergence at main flow step 6 (alarm condition check): If an alarm status occurs for a device, the RLCS detects the alarm condition within 2 seconds; the GUI issues an audible alarm, displays an icon different from the okay status, and changes the color of the affected device.

Exception 3 — Divergence at main flow step 6 (alarm condition): In the event of an alarm condition, the system displays appropriate emergency contact information.
Exception 4 — Divergence at main flow step 6 (alarm condition cleared): When the alarm condition is removed, the alarm icon automatically changes back to the normal status icon.
Exception 5 — Divergence at main flow step 5 (device status receipt): Failure to receive a valid status after a configurable number of retries is considered a device failure.

postconditions.content: The GUI displays the facility geographic area layout and current facility and device status information to the Operator, including facility status, traffic flow direction, customer eligibility, boundaries, device sensor status, alarm conditions, and override states.
The GUI provides the ability to display the status of one device at the detail level, showing all sensor data for that device.
The current status of the selected category of devices is displayed at the detail level, showing all sensor data for all devices of the same category (e.g., gates, pop-ups, CMS devices).

goal.content: To allow the Operator to perform status checks on all devices and system operations during normal operational modes.

preconditions.content: The Operator must have a valid Personnel ID, Name, Initials for login, password, and password date as defined in the Personnel entity.

The Operator must be assigned a Personnel Security Level that includes access to System Functions and Device entities, as security is restricted by Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions.
The RLCS database must be operational and storing current Device Status information (e.g., ok, alarm) for all monitored devices.
Each Device must have an associated Location, Device Category, and Device Status ID to enable status monitoring.
The Operator’s workstation must be linked to their Personnel record via the Personnel Workstations entity.

trigger.content: The Operator initiates a status check on devices and system operations via the GUI, which triggers the 'Monitor Devices' process (3.2.2.1) to collect Device Sensor Status data from RLCS Field Devices.

main_flow.content: The Operator initiates a status check via the GUI, triggering the 'Monitor Devices' process (3.2.2.1) to collect Device Sensor Status data from RLCS Field Devices.
The system retrieves current Device Status information (e.g., ok, alarm) for each monitored device from the RLCS database, where each Device has one Device Status and one Location.
The system displays the Device Sensor Status to the Operator through the GUI, allowing real-time monitoring of facility and device conditions.

If any device reports an alarm condition, the system references the associated Device Alarm Criteria and Alarm Type to determine severity (critical or warning) and presents this information to the Operator.
The system logs the status check event in the Device Command Log entity, recording the Date, Time, Device Status ID, and Operator ID for audit purposes.

exception_flow.content: If a device command fails during monitoring, the system tracks the number of failed device commands (3.2.2.5) and may retry the command using stored Command Data for retry.

If an alarm condition is detected, the system references Device Alarm Criteria and Alarm Type to determine severity; if no valid criteria exist for the device’s status, the alarm cannot be properly classified or escalated.

If the Operator’s Personnel Security Level does not permit access to the requested Device or System Function, the system denies the status check request per security restrictions defined in section 3.2.4.3.
If the RLCS database is unavailable or corrupted, the system cannot retrieve current Device Status information, preventing real-time monitoring and logging of status checks.
If a Device lacks required attributes such as Location ID, Device Category ID, or Device Status ID, the system cannot fully render or interpret its status for the Operator.

postconditions.content: The Operator has successfully viewed the current Device Status (e.g., ok, alarm) for all monitored devices.
A record of the status check event has been created in the Device Command Log entity, including Date, Time, Device Status ID, and Operator ID.
If an alarm condition was detected, it has been classified according to its associated Alarm Type (critical or warning) via the Device Alarm Criteria entity.
The system state remains consistent with the RLCS database, which continues to store historical transaction data for reporting system operations.

goal.content: The RLCS software monitors the status of all field devices and processes operator requests for changing field device status.

preconditions.content: The RLCS software startup process must have completed successfully, which includes identifying the unit, verifying required cards, performing a control system integrity check, and initializing specified tables.
Each workstation and control unit (FCU or DCU) must be online and identified by the system along with its associated device sensors.
The Operator must be logged in to the RLCS network computer.
The Operator must possess the appropriate access level and be using an authorized workstation.

trigger.content: The Operator logs into the RLCS system to monitor facility and device status, or a field device sensor reports a status change.

main_flow.content: The RLCS software displays the facility geographic area, traffic flow direction, customer eligibility, and device sensor status using dynamic icons on the GUI.
The system continually updates the status information every 2 seconds, even when no user is logged on.
If a device enters an alarm state, the GUI issues an audible alarm and changes the device icon color to distinguish it from the normal status.
The Monitor Devices process receives Device Sensor Status data from field devices and passes it to the Set Alarms and Collect Log Data processes.

alternative_flow.content: The Operator can set the operational status of failed devices using a control option.

The Operator can turn off the audible alarm permanently or temporarily for a given period.
The Operator can configure alarm conditions on the screen.
If a device status has been overridden, it appears on the screen with a different color from the normal and alarm status colors.
During 'degraded' mode, the system monitors device sensors at a frequency rate stored in the database specific to that mode.

exception_flow.content: At any point in an opening or closing sequence, the sequence shall be halted if: (1) A device fails to report completion of the current sequence step within the response time window allotted for the step; (2) The status of a closure device, which was previously opened at the current entrance, changes to 'unknown' or 'closed', without an operator-initiated command; (3) The status of a closure device, which was previously closed at the current entrance, changes to 'unknown' or 'open', without an operator-initiated command.
At any point in an opening sequence, the sequence shall be halted if the status of a closure device for the opposite direction of travel changes to 'unknown' or 'open'.

To resume an opening or closing sequence after a halt has occurred, the operator shall be able to issue a command to resume if the offending device status can be corrected within a configurable time period as defined in the database and in non-volatile memory.

postconditions.content: The current status of all entrance closure devices is maintained at each control unit and updated across all control units in the system.
Any change in device state is reported on the screen not later than 2 seconds from the time it occurs.
The system has monitored field controllers and connected devices on the RLCS network for control system integrity.
All users logged in to RLCS network computers and all commands issued in the field units have been reported by the system.
If a critical alarm condition was met during monitoring, the system has generated and presented the appropriate alarm to the operator.

goal.content: To generate current and historical reports of system operations.

preconditions.content: The Management user must be logged on to the RLCS Application.
The RLCS database must store historical transaction data necessary to generate reports of system operations.

trigger.content: Management initiates a request to generate current and historical reports of system operations.

main_flow.content: The RLCS retrieves all data necessary to operate the application software and generate current and historical reports of system operations from the database.
The system uses data exported from the RLCS database to create and format a variety of reports using a commercial off-the-shelf reporting tool.
The system formats the report for GUI display or for Print/Export output based on user selection.
The system outputs the reporting parameters to the COTS reporting package data store, and the report output to display, print, or file storage.

alternative_flow.content: If the report request involves data related to personnel security, the system retrieves attributes from the Personnel Security Level entity (Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions) to restrict access.
If the Management user has a 'Status Only' command level security, the system restricts the retrieval of control commands, allowing only status data to be included in the report.

goal.content: To retrieve current system status data from the RLCS for use by external systems such as AMS, Value Pricing/FasTrak, Traveler Info, and Ramp Metering Information System.

preconditions.content: The RLCS application is operational and running on a hardware platform compatible with Microsoft Windows NT or Unix-based operating systems.
The External Traffic System (such as AMS, Value Pricing/FasTrak, Traveler Info, or Ramp Metering Information System) is connected to the RLCS network and authorized to retrieve data.
System status data has been generated and stored by the RLCS Data Processing and Security function for export to external server data stores.
The RLCS database contains current system status information accessible via the Data Processing and Security module (3.2.4).

trigger.content: The External Traffic System requests current system status data from the RLCS.

main_flow.content: The External Traffic System sends a request for current system status data to the RLCS.
The RLCS Data Processing and Security function (3.2.4) retrieves the requested current system status data from the internal database.
The RLCS exports the system status data to the External Data Store associated with the requesting External Traffic System.
The External Traffic System receives the current system status data for use in its operations (e.g., AMS, Value Pricing/FasTrak, Traveler Info, Ramp Metering).

alternative_flow.content: If the External Traffic System is not authorized to access the RLCS data, the Data Processing and Security function (3.2.4) denies the request based on Personnel Security Level attributes including Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions.

If the requested system status data is not available in the RLCS database, the Data Processing and Security function returns an error indicating no current or historical data exists for the requested parameters.
If the External Traffic System requests data while the RLCS is exporting system status to another external server, the request may be queued or delayed until the export operation completes.

exception_flow.content: If the External Traffic System request fails authentication against Personnel Security Level attributes (Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, System Functions), the Data Processing and Security function denies access and terminates the use case.

If the RLCS database is unavailable or corrupted, preventing retrieval of system status data, the Data Processing and Security function returns a system error and the use case terminates without data export.

If the External Data Store target is unreachable during export, the RLCS logs the failure via Collect Log Data (3.2.2.7) and notifies monitoring functions; the use case terminates with partial success flag.

postconditions.content: The External Traffic System has received the current system status data exported from the RLCS.

The RLCS Data Processing and Security function (3.2.4) has successfully retrieved and exported the requested system status data to the external server data store associated with the requesting system.
The transaction is logged as part of the historical transaction data stored by the RLCS database for generating reports of system operations.

use_case_name: Update the Facility Map and Displayed Devices

goal.content: To refresh the facility map on the screen every 2 seconds to display current device status information.

preconditions.content: The RLCS shall support multiple users logged on, up to the limit of the number of users defined in the database.
The facility map on the screen shall refresh every 2 seconds but can be configurable within the database to more than 2 seconds by the user.
Not including device and network response times, requests from the GUI for status updates shall not exceed 2 seconds to update the GUI display.

trigger.content: The facility map on the screen is configured to refresh every 2 seconds, or at a user-configurable interval greater than 2 seconds.

main_flow.content: The RLCS shall store, process, and retrieve all data necessary to operate the application software as well as generate current and historical reports of system operations.
The RLCS database stores information needed to operate the RLCS as well as historical transaction data to generate reports of system operations.
The RLCS application software shall update and read database tables to support system operations.
The RLCS application software shall update and read password and device rule data in encrypted format.
The Personnel Security Level entity stores information about the five attributes used to restrict access to the RLCS: Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions.
Command levels are of three types: 'Status Only', 'Control', and 'Override'.
Users with 'Status Only' command level security may not issue any control commands at any level (device, macro, or super macro).
'Control' allows a user to issue control commands, and is a higher level of security.
'Override' allows a user to temporarily change the status of a device in the database for a configurable period of time in order to allow a command sequence to continue.
Commands shall be classified in these categories: (1) Device control commands, (2) Device Macro Commands, (3) Super Macro Commands, (4) Override Commands.
Device control commands are single commands that change the state of a device.
Device Macro Commands are a group of two or more sequentially executed commands that change the states of two or more closure devices.
Super Macro Commands are a group of two or more sequentially executed macros that change the states of an Entrance.
Override Commands are commands that force the status of a device to a temporary known state for the purpose of completing an operation which otherwise would not complete.

exception_flow.content: If a critical alarm is detected, the RLCS notification to the operator workstation shall occur within 2 seconds of alarm detection, and shall occur whether or not an operator is logged on to the system.

If device status information fails to be received from device sensors within 2 seconds of the status information being issued by the device sensor, the system must handle the delay as it exceeds the performance requirement.
If field devices fail to respond to commands from the RLCS within 12 seconds of the command confirmation being issued by the operator, the system encounters a response timeout exception.

If requests from the GUI for status updates exceed 2 seconds to update the GUI display (excluding device and network response times), the system fails to meet the display update performance requirement.
If the 'Track # of Failed Device Commands' function identifies a command failure, the system generates Command Failure Data and may initiate a retry sequence via 'Control Devices'.

postconditions.content: The facility map on the screen has been refreshed to display the current device status information.
The GUI display update for status changes has been completed within 2 seconds (excluding device and network response times).
The field device status information logging to the database has been updated (occurring every 2 seconds or at a configurable interval).

use_case_name: Update the Facility Map and Displayed Devices

goal.content: To allow the System Administrator to modify the facility map and add or remove devices from the display without requiring programming effort.

preconditions.content: The System Administrator is logged into the RLCS Software with System Administrative privileges.
The GUI is accessible and displaying the I-15 Reversible Lane Control System facility geographic area, including layout of mainline I-15, SR-163 freeway area.
Device sensor status and controller information are available for display using dynamic icons.
The system allows modification of the facility map without requiring programming effort.
The system allows devices to be added and removed from the display without requiring programming effort.

trigger.content: The System Administrator initiates a request to modify the facility map or add/remove devices from the display via the GUI configuration option.

main_flow.content: The System Administrator accesses the GUI configuration option to modify the facility map or add/remove devices from the display.
The GUI allows the facility map to be modified without requiring programming effort.
The GUI allows devices to be added and removed from the display without requiring programming effort.
When changes are made, the GUI configuration screen displays to the user which device, controller, or workstation in the RLCS network will be affected by the changes.
The system updates the displayed facility geographic area, including layout of mainline I-15, SR-163 freeway area, reflecting the modifications.
Device sensor status using dynamic icons for all field device sensors and controllers is updated on the display as applicable.

alternative_flow.content: If the System Administrator attempts to configure device rules, the system shall require an additional login password for that option.
If a device status has been overridden, on the screen it shall appear with different color from the normal and alarm status colors.
For alarm status, the GUI shall issue an audible alarm, and the icon shall be different from the okay status for that device. The visual alarm shall include a change of color for the affected device.
The System Administrator may turn off the audible alarm permanently or temporarily for a given period.
When the alarm condition is removed, the alarm icon shall change to the normal status icon automatically.

exception_flow.content: When the system administrator modifies the database tables, the GUI shall analyze the data before storing in the database and notify the system administrator of any conflicting or redundant entries.

postconditions.content: The facility map is modified without requiring programming effort.
Devices are added and removed from the display without requiring programming effort.

The GUI provides a display of the I-15 Reversible Lane Control System facility geographic area, including a layout of the mainline I-15, SR-163 freeway area in the same geographic area as the I-15 Reversible Lane.
Screen information includes Facility status (e.g. 'Open' or 'Closed').
Screen information includes Current direction of traffic flow.
Screen information includes Customer eligibility (e.g. 'RLCS and FasTrak Only', 'All Traffic').
Screen information includes Current facility boundaries extending one mile in either direction.
Device sensor status using dynamic icons for all field device sensors and controllers is displayed.

goal.content: The system shall provide for periodic verification that current, recomputed 'Message Digest' values correspond with 'record' values computed by the development process.

preconditions.content: The RLCS control system integrity check has been performed and all specified tables have been initialized.
The processing code and application software data, including login information, at the FCU and DCU controllers are resident in non-volatile memory.
The MD5 algorithm is used to secure application data and software in the controllers and the application server.

trigger.content: The Operator issues a command requesting Message Digest verification for a given control unit, thereby beginning a control unit integrity verification.

main_flow.content: The Operator issues a command requesting Message Digest verification for a given unit.
The system recomputes the current Message Digest value for the control unit using the MD5 algorithm.
The system compares the recomputed Message Digest value with the record value computed by the development process and confirms that they correspond.
The system records the Message Digest verification results in the system log.

exception_flow.content: At step 2, if a failure occurs in checking the non-volatile memory items, the system shall prevent the affected unit from being used in control sequences.

At step 3, if the integrity verification indicates a verification failure, the system shall generate a critical alarm condition for the affected control unit; if the failure occurs in checking the non-volatile memory items, the system shall prevent the affected unit from being used in control sequences.

postconditions.content: The current recomputed 'Message Digest' value for the verified control unit is confirmed to correspond with the 'record' value computed by the development process.
The 'Message Digest' verification results are recorded in the system log.

use_case_name: Browse and Search Files and Archives

goal.content: The User wants to browse and search files and archives within the PeaZip application interface.

preconditions.content: The computer system has an operating system.
The PeaZip application is running with its file manager interface displayed.

trigger.content: The use case is triggered when the User initiates browsing or searching from the PeaZip file manager interface, for example by pressing the 'File' button, selecting a 'Browser' submenu item, or using a navigation/search command such as F3 recursive search, F6 toggle browse/flat view, Ctrl+R go to root, or double-click to open/preview.

main_flow.content: The User presses the 'File' button in the initial PeaZip file manager window to open a submenu containing browsing choices.
The User selects the 'Filesystem' option from the submenu to access objects organized according to a functional hierarchy.
The PeaZip file manager interface displays a list of available drives (e.g., 'Vista (C:)', 'My Passport (D:)') with columns for Name, Type, Size (B), Free space, and Filesystem.
The User navigates the filesystem hierarchy using navigation controls such as back, forward, up, and refresh.
The User opens a directory or archive by using '<', Enter, or double-clicking on the folder or archive.
The User toggles between browse mode and flat view mode by pressing '*' or F6, causing all objects contained in the current path or archive to be displayed together.

alternative_flow.content: Diverges from Step 2: Instead of selecting 'Filesystem' from the File submenu, the User can select 'Recent archives' to access objects that have been recently browsed in PeaZip.
Diverges from Step 2: Instead of selecting 'Filesystem' from the File submenu, the User can select 'Bookmarks' to access objects that the User has rated as favorites.

Diverges from Step 2: Instead of selecting 'Filesystem' from the File submenu, the User can select 'Open path' or 'Open archive' to get direct access to a specific path of an object or a file/archive.
Diverges from Step 4: Instead of navigating the filesystem hierarchy using the back, forward, and up controls, the User can navigate directly to the computer system's or archive's root using Ctrl+R.
Diverges from Step 5: Instead of opening a directory or archive to continue browsing, the User can perform a non-recursive search (search in the current folder only) by pressing Ctrl+F3.
Diverges from Step 6: The User can press the 'Browser' button to open a submenu that provides direct access to toggle view modes.

exception_flow.content: At main-flow step 5, if the selected archive is encrypted, the User must know and insert the correct password (and, if present, the keyfile) to access the archive contents; without those credentials, the archive contents cannot be accessed.

postconditions.content: The User has gained access to the selected object from the list of objects organized by functional hierarchy, favorites, recent history, or direct path, and the PeaZip file manager interface displays the selected location with navigation controls available.

The PeaZip file manager interface displays the browsed or searched files and archives as a structured list in the view mode selected by the User, with metadata columns such as Name, Type, Size (B), Packed Date/time, Attributes, and CRC.

For drive and archive-content views, the interface displays the relevant object details: drives show Name, Type, Size (B), Free space, and Filesystem; archived contents show Name, Type, Size (B), Folders, Files, Date/time, Attributes, and Full name.
Upon completion of a search, whether recursive or non-recursive, the system displays the results within the current folder or subfolders as specified by the search mode triggered.
The status bar displays the current browsing context, such as 'Browsing: USER-PC [user]', confirming the active location within the filesystem hierarchy.

use_case_name: Browse and Search Files and Archives

goal.content: Enable PeaZip’s users to browse and gain access, in various ways, to every area of the computer system on which PeaZip runs as well as to included objects (archives and files), and to search in this folder and subfolders or in this folder only.

preconditions.content: An operating system is present on the computer system.
The user is in the PeaZip file manager interface, which is the initial window of the application.
For browsing an archive, the archive is in a read-only (browsing and extraction) format supported by PeaZip.
If the archive to be browsed is password-protected, the user knows the password and, if there is one, keyfile required to have access to the archive contents for browsing.

trigger.content: The user presses the 'File' button in the initial window of the application (file manager interface), uses the navigation bar, or invokes F3/Ctrl+F3 to browse and search files and archives.

main_flow.content: In the initial window of the application (file manager interface), the User presses the “File” button.
A submenu opens with choices that have to do with browsing and access to areas and objects of the computer systems.
The main window, under the “root” directory, shows a table listing disk information, and at the bottom of the window it indicates that the current browsing location is “USER-PC [user]”.
In the initial window of the application (file manager interface), the User presses the “Browser” button.
A submenu opens with choices that have to do with transferring to main interfaces of PeaZip and selecting view mode for objects (archives and files) displayed in file manager interface.
The User selects “Toggle browse/flat view”, which displays all together the objects contained in the current path or in the archive.
The User invokes F3 to perform recursive search (search in this folder and subfolders) or Ctrl+F3 to perform non recursive search (search here).
The User selects “Refresh” or presses F5 to refresh/update of currently displayed content.

alternative_flow.content: At step 2, the User can browse the desktop with F2, browse the user’s home with Ctrl+F2, browse the computer’s root with Shift+F2, or browse the archive root with Ctrl+Shift+F2 if browsing inside an archive (otherwise browse the computer’s root).
At step 2, the User can go to the computer system’s or archive’s root with Ctrl+R.

At step 2, the User can open a directory/archive with < or Enter or double click, go up one level with > or Ctrl+U or click on the blue arrow icon or F4, go back in history with Ctrl+B or Backspace, and go forward in history with Ctrl+F.
At step 2, the User can browse the most recently visited item with F7 or browse the first item in the bookmarks list with F8.
At step 4, the User can select “Go to archiving layout” to lead directly to the create archive interface or “Go to extraction layout” to lead directly to the extraction interface.
At step 5, instead of selecting “Toggle browse/flat view”, the User can toggle browse mode / flat view mode with * or F6.
At step 6, in search/filter mode, the User can go to the object’s path with Ctrl+P.
At step 7, instead of selecting “Refresh” or pressing F5, the User can click the refresh button in the navigation bar.

exception_flow.content: 1. If the User does not know or does not insert the password and (if there is one) keyfile required for an archive, the User cannot have access to the archive’s contents for browsing; browsing of that archive cannot proceed, so this exception exits the browse/search attempt for that archive.

postconditions.content: The User has browsed and gained access, in various ways, to every area of the computer system on which PeaZip runs, as well as to included objects (archives and files).
The User has direct access to a path of an object or a file/archive.
The User has searched and gained access to objects they would like to manage.
The objects contained in the current path or in the archive are displayed all together.
Currently displayed content is refreshed/updated.
For an archive requiring a password and (if there is one) keyfile, the User has access to the archives contents for browsing.
